d03cea605d90bcd4ea231942f1e54e5261cbc870.title: Multi-Label Neonatal EEG Segmentation Enriched with Semi-Synthetic Data
d03cea605d90bcd4ea231942f1e54e5261cbc870.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is widely used in routine clinical practice. In particular, it is of the utmost importance for monitoring newborns suffering from acute neonatal encephalopathy. In such a pathological context, continuous acquisitions during the first days of life must be analyzed, which represents an insurmountable workload for clinicians. Machine learning approaches are a way of helping human experts in their work. More specifically, deep learning models have the ability to segment specific physiological and pathological patterns. The main obstacle to the development of these models is their correct training from a sufficient number of annotations. Indeed, building annotated EEG datasets involves a time cost that is generally unacceptable. In this paper, a deep learning model dedicated to the segmentation of multiple patterns in newborn EEG is proposed. We study the impact o

cfd621b54d2e053af04f639fd3a0d99a900d9e32.title: TMI-CLNet: Triple-Modal Interaction Network for Chronic Liver Disease Prognosis from Imaging, Clinical, and Radiomic Data Fusion
cfd621b54d2e053af04f639fd3a0d99a900d9e32.abstract: Chronic liver disease represents a significant health challenge worldwide and accurate prognostic evaluations are essential for personalized treatment plans. Recent evidence suggests that integrating multimodal data, such as computed tomography imaging, radiomic features, and clinical information, can provide more comprehensive prognostic information. However, modalities have an inherent heterogeneity, and incorporating additional modalities may exacerbate the challenges of heterogeneous data fusion. Moreover, existing multimodal fusion methods often struggle to adapt to richer medical modalities, making it difficult to capture inter-modal relationships. To overcome these limitations, We present the Triple-Modal Interaction Chronic Liver Network (TMI-CLNet). Specifically, we develop an Intra-Modality Aggregation module and a Triple-Modal Cross-Attention Fusion module, which are designed

cfd3d73de3fe4d96e401fda70929e2bc8f48bca6.title: A Multimodal Slice Discovery Framework for Systematic Failure Detection and Explanation in Medical Image Classification
cfd3d73de3fe4d96e401fda70929e2bc8f48bca6.abstract: Despite advances in machine learning-based medical image classifiers, the safety and reliability of these systems remain major concerns in practical settings. Existing auditing approaches mainly rely on unimodal features or metadata-based subgroup analyses, which are limited in interpretability and often fail to capture hidden systematic failures. To address these limitations, we introduce the first automated auditing framework that extends slice discovery methods to multimodal representations specifically for medical applications. Comprehensive experiments were conducted under common failure scenarios using the MIMIC-CXR-JPG dataset, demonstrating the framework's strong capability in both failure discovery and explanation generation. cfbc8562d640e1b60f735ec555c22da3fa188bb4.title: Using Off-Target-Disease Data to Improve Target-Disease Lesion Segmentation
cfbc8562d640e1b60f735ec555c22da3fa188bb4.abstract: Does increasing the training data in deep learning always improve the accuracy of lesion segmentation on brain MRIs? To answer this question, we conduct experiments of small-diffuse lesion segmentation on 8 public brain MRI datasets with 3 different diseases, including Multiple Sclerosis (MS), White Matter Hyperintensities (WMH), and Chronic Stroke (CS). These diseases all have small lesions (lesions occupying < 2% of the whole brain MRI on average) that are often diffuse (injuring multiple brain regions), posing considerable challenges for lesion segmentation using deep learning. Our experimental results show that adding more data from other off-target diseases often led to a surprising decrease in accuracy on the target disease using a Naïve training strategy. cf61d63eda1fba1cdb532aa2e9c6c2fae649d9b9.title: Non-Invasive 3D Wound Measurement with RGB-D Imaging
cf61d63eda1fba1cdb532aa2e9c6c2fae649d9b9.abstract: Chronic wound monitoring and management require accurate and efficient wound measurement methods. This paper presents a fast, non-invasive 3D wound measurement algorithm based on RGB-D imaging. The method combines RGB-D odometry with B-spline surface reconstruction to generate detailed 3D wound meshes, enabling automatic computation of clinically relevant wound measurements such as perimeter, surface area, and dimensions. We evaluated our system on realistic silicone wound phantoms and measured sub-millimetre 3D reconstruction accuracy compared with high-resolution ground-truth scans. The extracted measurements demonstrated low variability across repeated captures and strong agreement with manual assessments. cea4a67c87893c2a47a12765c2850edba14aac93.title: MIHCGENER: A Framework for Multiple Immunohistochemical Image Generation Based on the Combination of Pathological Foundation Model and Generative Model
cea4a67c87893c2a47a12765c2850edba14aac93.abstract: The tumor microenvironment (TME) is important to the treatment and prognosis of cancer. Multiplex Immunohistochemical (mIHC) images can display the expression of multiple biomolecular markers while maintaining spatial location, making it an effective tool for TME analysis. However, acquiring mlHC images demands stringent laboratory conditions, extensive time and resources. In this study, we proposed an end-to-end generative framework to transform hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) images into mIHC images. In addition, we introduced a pathological foundation model into the feature encoding of pathological image generation to enhance the performance of our framework and proved the superiority and necessity of the foundation model. ce63efa3167d4d1c4bf6d33588e425aa484601da.title: Classifying Breast Composition by Applying Deep Learning to Microwave Images: A Feasibility Study
ce63efa3167d4d1c4bf6d33588e425aa484601da.abstract: Breast density (BD) is a recognized risk factor for breast cancer. For mammograms, BD is described with four categories (A to D) according to the Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System (BIRADS), based on the increasing proportion of glandular tissue in the breast. For risk assessment, new approaches to quantifying the composition of the breast are of interest. This study explores identifying breast composition in 292 microwave images (MWI) from 81 patients with a pretrained ResNet50 convolutional neural network (CNN). Image normalization, weighted stochastic oversampling, and focal loss techniques were used to address the small dataset size and class imbalance, and repeated stratified cross-validation enabled statistically robust performance estimates. ce586e0c57e4783d08b8819745847443388371af.title: Local $K$-Similarity Constraint for Medical Federated Learning with Label Noise
ce586e0c57e4783d08b8819745847443388371af.abstract: Federated learning enables leveraging private medical data from multiple institutions, without requiring the actual data to be shared. However, medical datasets in clients often exhibit erroneous annotations, affecting the robustness of the resulting global model. Most existing strategies to handle noisy clients in federation assume that a sufficient number of clients with clean labels are available, which can be leveraged to learn a robust global model while dampening the impact of noisy clients -an impractical assumption in real-world healthcare settings. In such scenarios, it is important to locally regularize the clients before communication with the server, to ensure the global model isn't corrupted by noisy clients. ce220ec16b3fcda1a4d8eac3e85b1a509d580ee6.title: LOCBAM: Advancing 3D Patch-Based Image Segmentation by Integrating Location Context
ce220ec16b3fcda1a4d8eac3e85b1a509d580ee6.abstract: Patch-based methods are widely used in 3D medical image segmentation to address memory constraints in processing highresolution volumetric data. However, these approaches often neglect the patch's location within the global volume, which can limit segmentation performance when anatomical context is important. In this paper, we investigate the role of location context in patch-based 3D segmentation and propose a novel attention mechanism, LocBAM, that explicitly processes spatial information. Experiments on BTCV, AMOS22, and KiTS23 demonstrate that incorporating location context stabilizes training and improves segmentation performance, particularly under low patch-to-volume coverage where global context is missing. Furthermore, LocBAM consistently outperforms classical coordinate encoding via CoordConv. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/compai-lab/2026-ISBI-hooft.

cd668d951c38c080772932bba6af563128bc78cd.title: Robust Pediatric Brain Tumor Segmentation: Evaluating Modality Importance and Resilience in Missing-Modality Scenarios
cd668d951c38c080772932bba6af563128bc78cd.abstract: Pediatric brain tumor segmentation from multi-parametric MRI (mpMRI) is essential for treatment planning and disease monitoring. However, most deep learning approaches assume the availability of complete imaging protocols, which is often unrealistic in pediatric clinical practice due to motion artifacts or shortened scan time. In this work, we present a systematic analysis of MRI modality importance for pediatric brain tumor segmentation using the BraTS-PEDs 2023 dataset. A 3D SegResNet model is trained and evaluated under different modality combinations, where separate models are constructed for each available subset of MRI sequences. Results show that T2-FLAIR provides strong cues for whole tumor delineation, while T1c is critical for enhancing tumor detection. The exclusion of T1c leads to the largest performance degradation, whereas the model shows limited sensitivity to missing T1.

cd14be839aa8476f11fe58548f4fcd0bf9ad184e.title: LognormalNet: Parametric Survival Model with Uncertainty Quantification via Evidential Likelihood-Based Inference
cd14be839aa8476f11fe58548f4fcd0bf9ad184e.abstract: Due to censored observations and multi-modal data heterogeneity, reliable survival prediction is a significant challenge for patients after cancer treatment. In this study, we propose LognormalNet, a parametric neural network that performs survival estimation and uncertainty quantification using evidential likelihood-based inference. The model captures the nonlinear relationship between patient covariates and survival time under a lognormal distribution. To characterize prediction uncertainty, we employ a random fuzzy set, derived by linearizing the network output and using a Gaussian approximation of the likelihood function. This framework can capture both aleatory uncertainty and epistemic uncertainty. Evaluated on the HECTOR2025 dataset, LognormalNet outperforms other survival models while effectively quantifying prediction uncertainty.

cce97e2ef6025576c01b4c89b555af95c56eba5d.title: Adaptive Cross-Attention for Robust Lung Segmentation with Noisy Labels
cce97e2ef6025576c01b4c89b555af95c56eba5d.abstract: Accurate lung segmentation in computed tomography (CT) images is essential for diagnosing and managing respiratory diseases. However, achieving reliable segmentation is challenging due to the scarcity and noise of labeled medical data. In this paper, we present a novel approach for lung segmentation under noisy labeling conditions via attention-guided transfer learning. Our method integrates an Adaptive Cross-Attention block, which selectively incorporates features from pretrained models to improve robustness in segmentation. Furthermore, we introduce an adaptive loss function that dynamically weighs pretrained and ground-truth outputs during training, effectively mitigating the impact of possible label noise. cc3ea3377a02f9ca5039d1262a3c2ea30797bb26.title: A Unified Brain Extraction Framework Powered by Structure-Intensity Disentanglement-Based Data Augmentation
cc3ea3377a02f9ca5039d1262a3c2ea30797bb26.abstract: Brain extraction is a fundamental step in neuroimaging analysis, yet existing methods are often constrained to specific modalities or age groups, limiting their applicability in largescale, lifespan studies. In this work, we present BrainExt, a unified foundation model for brain extraction across multiple imaging modalities and the whole lifespan. To address inter-modality and across-age variations, we first collect a large-scale multi-modal, lifespan brain dataset of 25,487 scans spanning from fetal to elderly subjects and introduce a Structure-Intensity Disentanglement Synthesis (SIDSyn) module to generate real-world distribution-aligned data for robust pre-training. The pre-trained model is subsequently fine-tuned on real clinical scans to better adapt to real-world data distributions. BrainExt demonstrates superior generalization and stability compared to existing methods, achieving

cb9f6f9adb08e04ddc7cd7d979d65a8fe9858361.title: Integrating Population and Individual Brain Network with Mixture-of-Experts for Mild Cognitive Impairment Study
cb9f6f9adb08e04ddc7cd7d979d65a8fe9858361.abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) diagnosis from neuroimaging requires a comprehensive understanding of brain connectivity patterns. While multi-atlas approaches provide complementary perspectives on brain organization, existing methods rely predominantly on functional connectivity and employ static fusion strategies that introduce information redundancy. To address this, we propose a novel framework that integrates individualized three-hinge gyrus (3 HG) -based brain networks with population-level atlases based networks through a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture. Specifically, brain graph encoders extract structural and functional connectivity embeddings from each atlas, which are processed by atlas-shared and atlas-specific experts to learn atlas-shared and atlas-specific brain patterns, respectively. ca8bc52f12269f495c03ecac5124b9bc13d08a59.title: Structure Preserving Adversarial Diffusion for Unpaired Medical Image Synthesis
ca8bc52f12269f495c03ecac5124b9bc13d08a59.abstract: Recent works have established diffusion models as viable candidates for unpaired medical image translation, by incorporating supervision through non-diffusive models in an end-to-end fashion.. Existing models typically rely on cycleconsistent, two-sided, non-diffusive modules of relatively high computational cost where structure preservation is not explicit. In this work, we propose SPAD, a novel one-sided approach that explicitly preserves the source domain firstorder (gradient) orientations, while enabling flexible contrast adaptation between source and target domains. Our approach provides direct edge guidance for the diffusive module, leading to better structural preservation. ca088747a6f956558ca6342c9aa5809d9dee7077.title: Detecting Pain During Cognitive Tasks via Visibility Graphs of Cortical Signals
ca088747a6f956558ca6342c9aa5809d9dee7077.abstract: Detecting pain is critical for developing adaptive systems in clinical and assistive settings, allowing for timely interventions. This work presents an approach to detect the presence of physical pain during the performance of cognitive tasks from cortical signals. Visibil-ity graphs (VGs) of these signals are constructed, and graph metrics of averaged clustering coefficient $(C)$ and edge den-sity $(D)$ are extracted. c81b3d00abb7718fbc83ba7847fcb2da212b82bc.title: Resmscam-FFT Net: Residual Multi-Scale Channel Attention Module with Fast Fourier Transform Network for Cardiac Segmentation
c81b3d00abb7718fbc83ba7847fcb2da212b82bc.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of global mortality, underscoring the critical need for accurate and timely diagnosis. Echocardiography has been established as the primary non-invasive diagnostic tool, but its reliance on operator expertise leads to significant variability and limits access to timely care. To address these challenges, we introduce ResMSCAM-FFT Net, a deep learning model for precise semantic segmentations and measurements of cardiac chambers in 2D echocardiogram videos. Rooted in the U-Net structure, ResMSCAM-FFT Net incorporates Pyramid Vision Transformer v2 (PVT v2) encoder for efficient multi-scale feature extraction, Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) Block to enforce global topological consistency and mitigate ultrasound artifacts, and Residual Multi-Scale Convolutional Attention Module (ResMSCAM) for content-aware local boundary refinement. c7bfd505ca36a070ee31b1244fe1b5d4a3a5c461.title: Multi-Stage Bidirectional Cross-Attention Model for Predicting Prognosis in Multiple Peritoneum Lesions with Clinical Information
c7bfd505ca36a070ee31b1244fe1b5d4a3a5c461.abstract: Peritoneal metastasis occurs when cancer cells spread from the primary tumor to the peritoneum, leading to morphological alterations that significantly impact patient survival. The specific changes across multiple peritoneal sites can effectively indicate a patient's risk level and prognosis. However, the considerable variation in peritoneal shape, size, and location poses significant challenges for feature extraction and prognostic analysis. Traditional multi-instance learning approaches typically fuse instance features extracted by the backbone network at the final stage, but their lack of intermediate interaction limits the ability to capture both common and distinct features. c73ba45577b7077a9f454b23da3deeac1063c4df.title: INTERACT-CMIL: Multi-Task Shared Learning and Inter-Task Consistency for Conjunctival Melanocytic Intraepithelial Lesion Grading
c73ba45577b7077a9f454b23da3deeac1063c4df.abstract: Accurate grading of Conjunctival Melanocytic Intraepithelial Lesions (CMIL) is essential for treatment and melanoma prediction but remains difficult due to subtle morphological cues and interrelated diagnostic criteria. c716bb4b17ecfff14d556967e65da0eb04c41424.title: Cervical Cancer Lesion Grading Based on Clinical Diagnostic Criteria and Multi-View Approach Using Intraoperative Colposcopic Images
c716bb4b17ecfff14d556967e65da0eb04c41424.abstract: Current research on cervical cancer grading often ignores the integration of clinical diagnostic practice, and effectively fusing multiple views of the lesion site is crucial for accurate analysis. In order to solve this problem, this paper proposes a multi-view classification network using acetic acid-stained colposcopy to screen intraoperative images. This model introduces a novel multi-linkage attention mechanism based on sliding Windows to enhance feature fusion across multiple views. Experimental results show that compared with Swin-Transformer, Vision Transformer and MobileNetV2(all without pre-training weights), the accuracy of the proposed model is improved by 2.60%, 9.68% and 14.43%, respectively. These results highlight the superior performance of the model in grading cervical cancer lesions and its potential as a valuable tool for clinical diagnosis.

c69fe4ad8123832eff95a89d01681cf2425bab90.title: DINOv2-Enhanced Dual-View Unimatch for Joint Carotid Plaque Segmentation and Classification
c69fe4ad8123832eff95a89d01681cf2425bab90.abstract: Carotid ultrasound analysis is significantly hindered by speckle noise, operator dependency, and the complexity of integrating multi-view information. Existing methods, often constrained by single-view perspectives and fully supervised paradigms, struggle to generalize across diverse clinical settings. To address these challenges, we propose DINOv2-Enhanced Dual-View UniMatch, a novel framework for joint carotid plaque segmentation and classification. Central to our approach is the utilization of the powerful DINOv2 foundation model as a shared backbone to extract robust, view-invariant features from complementary longitudinal and transverse scans, processed via independent DPT decoders. We introduce a decoupled two-stage training strategy integrated with the UniMatch protocol: (1) a semi-supervised stage to establish robust spatial priors using unlabeled data, followed by (2) a task-exp

c690c2a6e1f940c3c1aa34f44732fd089c8e6e81.title: Leveraging Whole Slide Difficulty in Multiple Instance Learning to Improve Prostate Cancer Grading
c690c2a6e1f940c3c1aa34f44732fd089c8e6e81.abstract: Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) has been widely applied in histopathology to classify Whole Slide Images (WSIs) with slide-level diagnoses. While the ground truth is established by expert pathologists, the slides can be difficult to diagnose for non-experts and lead to disagreements between the annotators. In this paper, we introduce the notion of Whole Slide Difficulty (WSD), based on the disagreement between an expert and a non-expert pathologist. We propose two different methods to leverage WSD, a multi-task approach and a weighted classification loss approach, and we apply them to Gleason grading of prostate cancer slides. Results show that integrating WSD during training consistently improves the classification performance across different feature encoders and MIL methods, particularly for higher Gleason grades (i.e., worse diagnosis).

c67dee7cf68f33812a11f3f590a5fd1bb5b99c7b.title: Follow Your Heart: Landmark-Guided Transducer Pose Scoring for Point-of-Care Echocardiography
c67dee7cf68f33812a11f3f590a5fd1bb5b99c7b.abstract: Point-of-care transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) makes it possible to assess a patient's cardiac function in almost any setting. A critical step in the TTE exam is acquisition of the apical 4-chamber (A4CH) view, which is used to evaluate clinically impactful measurements such as left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). However, optimizing transducer pose for high-quality image acquisition and subsequent measurement is a challenging task, particularly for novice users. In this work, we present a multi-task network that provides feedback cues for A4CH view acquisition and automatically estimates LVEF in high-quality A4CH images. The network cascades a transducer pose scoring module and an uncertainty-aware LV landmark detector with automated LVEF estimation. A strength is that network training and inference do not require cumbersome or costly setups for transducer position tracking. W

c611dc98d7573205c99f240f135ebed3d02549dd.title: MSDM: Generating Task-Specific Pathology Images with a Multimodal Conditioned Diffusion Model for Cell and Nuclei Segmentation
c611dc98d7573205c99f240f135ebed3d02549dd.abstract: Scarcity of annotated data, particularly for rare or atypical morphologies, present significant challenges for cell and nuclei segmentation in computational pathology. While manual annotation is labor-intensive and costly, synthetic data offers a cost-effective alternative. We introduce a Multimodal Semantic Diffusion Model (MSDM) for generating realistic pixel-precise image-mask pairs for cell and nuclei segmentation. By conditioning the generative process with cellular/nuclear morphologies (using horizontal and vertical maps), RGB color characteristics, and BERT-encoded assay/indication metadata, MSDM generates datasests with desired morphological properties. These heterogeneous modalities are integrated via multi-head crossattention, enabling fine-grained control over the generated images. Quantitative analysis demonstrates that synthetic images closely match real data, with low Wasse

c5f49070827e70b30fb015366cc45c48dcb47405.title: Fedharmo: Harmonizing Global Aggregation and Local Alignment in Cross-Domain Federated Medical Image Segmentation
c5f49070827e70b30fb015366cc45c48dcb47405.abstract: Federated learning has emerged as the mainstream technique for breaking data silos in the healthcare domain by enabling collaborative training of machine learning models among different clients while ensuring data privacy. However, due to the discrepancy in the data distribution of each client, the aggregated model may ultimately be shifted towards certain clients. Consequently, we propose FedHarmo, a federated learning segmentation framework that employs an adaptive aggregation weight updating strategy to prevent model aggregation shifted towards certain clients. Additionally, we utilize the distribution measurement metric to minimize the distance between the global model and local models. Comprehensive experiments on ten medical image datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method. Our code are available at https://github.com/GGbond-study/FedHarmo.

c5e3414141bfc375d1659269bf4fe80d38e67186.title: SonoYOLO + MedSAM2: A Pipeline for Automatic Detection and Segmentation of Regions of Interest in Cardiac Ultrasound Videos
c5e3414141bfc375d1659269bf4fe80d38e67186.abstract: Precise evaluation of cardiac function is essential for early diagnosis, risk assessment, and treatment of cardiovascular diseases. Cardiac ultrasound videos are widely used for this purpose, but cardiologists need to manually delineate the regions of interest in the videos, which is a time-consuming and error-prone process. While many automatic video segmentation methods exist, modern deep learning-based methods require dense annotations for training, which is labor-intensive. Recent zero-shot segmentation models specialized for medical data such as MedSAM2 do not require such dense annotations, but they still need manual prompts (e.g., bounding boxes), which hinders automatic deployment. To address these challenges, we propose a fully automated pipeline for detecting and segmenting regions of interest in cardiac ultrasound videos. The proposed pipeline (SonoYOLO + MedSAM2) consists of

c5dab4d958dc18890824de681dc123db4cb83bc3.title: Vision Transformer for Breast Cancer Diagnosis: Layer-Wise Analyses Beyond Attention Mechanism
c5dab4d958dc18890824de681dc123db4cb83bc3.abstract: Early detection of breast cancer is essential for improving survival, yet diagnostic accuracy remains limited in dense breasts where tumors overlap with complex glandular structures. Considering that breast density itself is an independent risk factor, an artificial intelligence (AI) framework that captures both local lesions and global anatomical context is required. Vision Transformer (ViT) has emerged as a promising model for representing longrange dependencies, and its potential has also been investigated in breast cancer diagnosis. Recently, the effectiveness of shape-guided attention mechanisms has been suggested; however, it remains unclear how the guidance influences the representation flow beyond the attention mechanism. In this study, we analyzed ViT models for breast cancer diagnosis using quantitative frameworks that track information propagation, including Norm-based Analysi

c57d5c4b22763b8e5bbad4ddab28d1ca3f8874a6.title: Attention-Based Multiple Instance Learning for Achilles Tendinopathy Detection in Ultrasound Imaging
c57d5c4b22763b8e5bbad4ddab28d1ca3f8874a6.abstract: Achilles tendinopathy is a common condition resulting in pain and inflammation in the Achilles tendon due to injury or overuse. Ultrasound is typically the medical imaging modality of choice during diagnosis due to its relatively broader accessibility, lower cost, and non-invasiveness when compared to other technologies but can produce noisy, poorer quality images depending on many factors in data collection. Past studies have applied fully supervised machine learning methods for detection of Achilles tendinopathy, requiring strenuous data cleaning and labeling, which is time consuming for physicians. To more closely align with a typical clinical workflow, this work applies a weakly supervised multiple instance learning approach with attention-based pooling to detect and emphasize ultrasound images in a set that are more indicative of a patient's tendon health. This approach achieved 97.

c538ee76b36048a9a9a6b46e034147c6327a2ead.title: LF-MAMBA: A State Space Model-Based Framework for Accurate Bilateral Hippocampi Segmentation in Low-Field Pediatric MRI
c538ee76b36048a9a9a6b46e034147c6327a2ead.abstract: Precise segmentation of bilateral hippocampi in pediatric brain MRI is essential for studying early brain development and diagnosing neurodevelopmental disorders. Current deep learning methods face challenges with low-field MRI due to lower image quality, signal-to-noise ratios, and tissue contrast. We introduce LF-Mamba, a UNet-based model specifically designed for low-field pediatric MRI segmentation, integrating structured state-space modeling for long-range dependency capture and frequency domain attention for effective feature fusion. We extensively evaluated LF-Mamba against state-of-the-art models on the LISA dataset, with results demonstrating that LF-Mamba outperforms existing models, achieving a mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 45.23% and a Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 60.24%. These results indicate that LF-Mamba enhances segmentation performance in low-field MRI,

c36c22a1ba2bed5b6b429f54aa06b44419fdd78d.title: Attention-Driven Multi-Sequence Mri Feature Learning and Fusion for Breast Cancer Diagnosis
c36c22a1ba2bed5b6b429f54aa06b44419fdd78d.abstract: The heterogeneity and complexity of breast lesions, along with the vast amount of imaging data provided by each sequence Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), make breast cancer diagnosis highly challenging. Many studies use deep learning methods for multi-sequence MRI joint analysis to improve diagnostic performance. However, existing approaches often ignore the requirements for distinct feature learning processes for different sequence MRIs. Additionally, they have not fully leveraged or discriminated relevant information during modeling, limiting the effectiveness of the model. Inspired by the diagnostic workflow of radiologists, we propose an Attention-driven Feature Learning and Fusion (AFLF) framework to classify benign and malignant breast lesions using multi-sequence MRI. Our framework employs an attention-based encoding network to learn attention-aware representations for each seque

c2b23e9ca69ae9677b19d25ae467e767534ec8df.title: Learnable Descent Algorithm for Cardiac Transmembrane Potential Imaging
c2b23e9ca69ae9677b19d25ae467e767534ec8df.abstract: Myocardial transmembrane potential (TMP) offers greater clinical value than body surface potential (BSP) or heart-surface reconstructions. In this work, we propose a TMP reconstruction method based on a convergent learned descent-type algorithm (LDA) and its induced deep neural network. Specifically, we propose a variational model where the data fidelity term links BSP measurements to the TMP via a heart-torso geometric matrix. The regularization term combines an $L_{2,1}$ norm to enhance sparsity with a feature extractor parameterized as a deep convolutional neural network. We applied the LDA, which leverages Nesterov's smoothing technique, the idea of residual learning, and an iteration selection policy as the safeguard for convergence, to solve the proposed non-smooth non-convex minimization model. We generate a neural network whose architecture follows the algorithm. This network inh

c0f26181d15a130709e588d71bea6abe29f6349b.title: A Proximal Approach for Stain Separation and Normalization of Whole-Slide Histopathological Images
c0f26181d15a130709e588d71bea6abe29f6349b.abstract: Stain variability in histopathological images presents a major obstacle to developing accurate and reliable computer-aided diagnosis systems. In this paper, we introduce a novel stain normalization framework based on a stain separation proximal algorithm. Specifically, we first propose a new stain separation method that extracts individual stain components from a given stained image. Subsequently, we perform stain normalization by aligning the separated source stains with those of a target reference image. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed approach effectively reduces inter-image color variations while preserving the essential structural details of the tissue.

c0c1f91b271af537fbfafdd5f0ed6c0c1674359f.title: Unpaired Semantic-Preserving Virtual Perls Generation via Conditional Generative Models
c0c1f91b271af537fbfafdd5f0ed6c0c1674359f.abstract: Virtual staining has emerged as a promising approach to reduce laboratory workload and enhance digital hematopathology workflows. However, stain-to-stain translation in hematology remains largely unexplored, mainly due to the absence of paired data. In this study, we propose a modified CycleGAN framework to virtually generate Perls-stained images from morphologically stained bone marrow smears. The model introduces a class-conditioned pairing strategy and a classification consistency loss guided by an external DenseNet-based sideroblast classifier to preserve diagnostic semantics. Trained on 12,738 unpaired cell images from 44 patients, the proposed approach achieved substantial improvements in both label preservation and image realism. c0bf1accd6f9d110430b7ef1970e9a13149fe7b5.title: Ucad: Uncertainty-Guided Contour-Aware Displacement for Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
c0bf1accd6f9d110430b7ef1970e9a13149fe7b5.abstract: Existing displacement strategies in semi-supervised segmentation only operate on rectangular regions, ignoring anatomical structures and resulting in boundary distortions and semantic inconsistency. To address these issues, we propose UCAD, an Uncertainty-Guided Contour-Aware Displacement framework for semi-supervised medical image segmentation that preserves contour-aware semantics while enhancing consistency learning. Our UCAD leverages superpixels to generate anatomically coherent regions aligned with anatomy boundaries, and an uncertainty-guided selection mechanism to selectively displace challenging regions for better consistency learning. We further propose a dynamic uncertainty-weighted consistency loss, which adaptively stabilizes training and effectively regularizes the model on unlabeled regions. c00412ea8643893fcf350368e915c6234fd13b15.title: Generalize or Specialize? The Effect of Coil Combining in Deep Learning Based MR Image Reconstruction
c00412ea8643893fcf350368e915c6234fd13b15.abstract: With the advent of deep-learning based MR image reconstruction, new questions are raised regarding best design choices. In particular, when using recent reconstruction models that have been developed for processing multi-channel MR data. A fundamental question is whether to first combine channels to improve model generalizability (i.e., a “coil-combined” approach) or to keep channel processing separate to fully utilize multi-channel information (i.e., an “all-coil” approach). In this work, we compare three popular architectures using coil-combined and all-coil styles on brain MR images. All-coil styles improved in-distribution performance, such as when reconstructing only presumed healthy individu-als. Coil-combined designs better generalized to unseen data from patients with pathology.

bffac8e024677acd686e14658f3b0bc2113e9105.title: Protomsnet: A Prototypical Network for Interpretable Detection of Mitral Stenosis in Echocardiography
bffac8e024677acd686e14658f3b0bc2113e9105.abstract: Mitral stenosis (MS), a pathological narrowing of the mitral valve, is primarily evaluated using echocardiography, a modality that relies heavily on operator expertise for both image acquisition and interpretation. To reduce this dependency, machine learning (ML) methods have been developed to automate valvular disease detection. However, the rarity of MS limits the availability of labeled data for model training, and the poor interpretability of many ML models hinders clinical adoption. We propose ProtoMSNet, a prototypical network for MS detection from easily acquired echocardiographic views. ProtoMSNet enhances interpretability by offering explainable decisions through the use of informative visual prototypes. bf1ce467b21e555700308670ada286b6d004bbe6.title: Segmentation From Partial Views Via Patient-Specific Shape Priors
bf1ce467b21e555700308670ada286b6d004bbe6.abstract: Precision surgical interventions rely on accurate integration of preoperative and intraoperative imaging to guide clinical decision-making and improve patient outcomes. Traditionally, most 3D imaging modalities capture the entirety of the target object, allowing for the segmentation of its entire volume. However, some medical imaging devices trade full field-of-view for other considerations, such as size and ability to access the target organ in unique ways. This is particularly true of ultrasound, where imaging deeper organs from outside the body is not viable due to attenuation, thus motivating the need for alternative imaging strategies. In scenarios such as image-guided intervention, it is often necessary to put this partial view of the object in its full anatomical context, such as alignment to a pre-operative MRI. be6c4ba9b20a5af1f3c37ec72aaeb9de1188fb69.title: Robust by Design: A Continuous Monitoring and Data Integration Framework for Medical AI
be6c4ba9b20a5af1f3c37ec72aaeb9de1188fb69.abstract: Adaptive medical AI models often face performance drops in dynamic clinical environments due to data drift. We propose an autonomous continuous monitoring and data integration framework that maintains robust performance over time. Focusing on glomerular pathology image classification (proliferative vs. non-proliferative lupus nephritis), our three-stage method uses multi-metric feature analysis and Monte Carlo dropout-based uncertainty gating to decide when to retrain on new data. Only images statistically similar to the training distribution (via Euclidean, cosine, Mahalanobis metrics) and with low predictive entropy are integrated. The model is then incrementally retrained with these images under strict performance safeguards (no metric degradation ¿5%). bd584fd0f78bf36e0a1e2e0dd8a4de71575c1514.title: Integration of Cardiac Histopathological and Imaging Data to Improve Understanding of Stereotactic Arrhythmia Radioablation
bd584fd0f78bf36e0a1e2e0dd8a4de71575c1514.abstract: Ventricular tachycardia (VT) refractory to conventional therapies can be treated with stereotactic arrhythmia radioablation (STAR), yet its biological mechanisms remain unclear. To locally analyze the myocardial response to irradiation, we propose an full workflow integrating in-vivo treatment planning, ex-vivo imaging, and histopathology from an explanted human heart post-STAR. The method establishes a landmarkbased registration framework aligning ex-vivo and in-vivo data within a common coordinate system using anatomical landmarks (base, apex, and a rotation point). Twenty-one anatomical landmarks enabled consistent registration of CT, radiation dose maps and histopathology descriptors. bd1ff9100ed180ecb6b3810a48e31d8516e83911.title: HyLLM: A RAG-Based Large Language Model Framework for Phenotype-Guided Reasoning in Hypertensive Management
bd1ff9100ed180ecb6b3810a48e31d8516e83911.abstract: Hypertension is a pervasive condition that often goes unnoticed but can cause significant damage to vital organs. While imaging has proven central to detecting end-organ changes, interpreting results can be challenging for clinicians due the heterogeneous nature of multi-modal imaging data. In this study, we present HyLLM, a multi-stage large language model (LLM) framework designed to generate phenotypeguided explanations for the severity of hypertension-induced organ damage. It leverages a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline to extract contextual information from evidence-based resources including PubMed database and current clinical guidelines. Three major LLMs, namely GPT-OSS, DeepSeek, and Mistral, were employed within the framework and evaluated with quantitative and clinical metrics using UK Biobank imaging substudy. bcff0e10f965bf0a1b9d88b8101182de3372ddcc.title: Time-Aware Neural Operator for Liver Radiofrequency Ablation Planning
bcff0e10f965bf0a1b9d88b8101182de3372ddcc.abstract: Radiofrequency ablation (RFA) benefits from fast, accurate predictors of thermal dose, yet high-fidelity FEM solvers remain too slow for routine treatment planning. We present a time-aware, hybrid 3D Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) surrogate for liver RFA that performs one-shot prediction at arbitrary times. The model combines an FNO trunk with explicit time conditioning and a factorised spatial modulator that generates per-parameter scale/shift fields from temporal and biophysical (electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity and perfusion) inputs, enabling structured, physics-guided modulation of the operator. bc462f6337c6fece9572344394a5812985a9ef5a.title: Self-Supervised Vision Transformer for Surgical Phase Recognition in Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection
bc462f6337c6fece9572344394a5812985a9ef5a.abstract: Surgical phase recognition is critical for context-aware interventions, but deep learning models require large, costly annotated datasets. This work presents DINO-Endo, an efficient framework pairing a self-supervised DINOv2 Vision Transformer (ViT-S/14) backbone with lightweight temporal models. Through sequential domain adaptation—pretraining on unannotated porcine videos followed by human endoscopic videos—our approach produces highly discriminative features that enable simple temporal decoders to achieve state-of-the-art performance. We demonstrate 89.5% accuracy on patient dataset and 90.0% on complex porcine dataset, outperforming existing methods while using 14-times fewer parameters than foundation models like V-JEPA2. bbad4bf55dcc6cb3b69cb11193cd5bfc13701329.title: Ultrasound Nerve Segmentation with Deep Learning for Leprosy
bbad4bf55dcc6cb3b69cb11193cd5bfc13701329.abstract: Purpose: This study aims to provide an AI tool for detecting nerves in ultrasound images to help diagnose Hansen's disease (Leprosy) in rural areas. The significant difference in the cross-sectional area (CSA) of superficial nerves in symmetrical extremities is a landmark in the early stages of the disease. Despite its potential, ultrasound nerve evaluation is limited due to the difficulty in accurately identifying nerves in ultrasound images. Methodology: We propose the first Leprosy video nerve segmentation pipeline based on YOLOv8 and X-Mem architectures to automate frame detection, segmentation, and label propagation. bb2c3a37a7a516497a8b956accbb1894abdeedb9.title: Optical Flow-Guided Echocardiography Label Augmentation for the Segment Anything Model
bb2c3a37a7a516497a8b956accbb1894abdeedb9.abstract: Echocardiography plays a crucial role in evaluating cardiac function; however, conventional segmentation techniques often struggle with limited annotations and domain shifts arising from variations in patient and device environments. In this study, we propose the Echo Flow Labeling (EFL) framework, a pseudo-label augmentation strategy driven by optical flow, designed to extend sparse end-diastolic and end-systolic annotations to intermediate frames. Our method leverages unsupervised optical flow estimation, a novel pointbased label refinement, and an occlusion-aware weighting scheme to enhance segmentation consistency and boundary accuracy in SAM-based models. babc0ba9aed557685bc5e356a04316b45e46d926.title: Ga-Shape: A Dual-Path Framework Guided by Gestational Age and Local Shape Descriptors for Fetal Brain MRI Segmentation
babc0ba9aed557685bc5e356a04316b45e46d926.abstract: Accurate segmentation of fetal brain tissues in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is essential for diagnosing diseases, assessing developmental delays, and analyzing patterns of fetal brain development. The rapid growth of the fetal brain during pregnancy results in significant shape variations at different gestational ages, while the folding of the cerebral cortex introduces subtle local shape changes, making brain tissue segmentation more challenging. To tackle these challenges, we present a dual-path framework for brain tissue segmentation, which integrates a primary segmentation network with an auxiliary network designed to predict gestational age and local shape descriptors (LSDs). ba57e8a306a9da14364ff9cdb243f5f10e8fdb3d.title: A Semi-Supervised Cascaded Dual-Model Framework for Carotid Plaque Segmentation and Vulnerability Assessment
ba57e8a306a9da14364ff9cdb243f5f10e8fdb3d.abstract: Ischemic stroke remains a leading cause of death worldwide. Ultrasound imaging plays a vital role in evaluating carotid plaques, but automatic segmentation and vulnerability assessment face significant challenges due to high annotation costs and subjective manual evaluation. To address these issues, this paper proposes a semi-supervised learning framework that leverages abundant unlabeled ultrasound images to reduce reliance on costly labeled data. Our approach introduces three key improvements: a cascaded dual-model architecture decoupling segmentation and classification tasks; an enhanced semi-supervised training strategy with optimal teacher model and dynamic threshold pseudo-label filtering; and a differentiated loss function to mitigate class imbalance. ba19ce1efe26aefe07b24f10d852904bf34918b0.title: A Multi-Modal Transformer for Ultrasound-Guided Diffuse Optical Tomography
ba19ce1efe26aefe07b24f10d852904bf34918b0.abstract: Diffuse Optical Tomography (DOT) is a non-invasive imaging modality that estimates tissue optical properties using near-infrared (NIR) light. Conventional DOT reconstruction methods suffer from poor spatial resolution and instability due to the ill-posed inverse problem. In this work, we propose MDOT-former, a multi-modal transformer that integrates B-mode ultrasound (US) imaging with DOT to enhance reconstruction accuracy. The proposed model employs a multimodal cross-attention transformer to extract morphological features from US images and improve the localization and quantification of optical properties. To facilitate model training, we introduce an in-silico simulation framework that synthesizes paired DOT and US data. We evaluate MDOT-former using both in-silico and ex-vivo experiments, demonstrating a significant improvement over state-of-the-art (SOTA) learning-based algorithms.

b9d3cc3315b222603b894b8986579a124347f38a.title: Dynamic Convergence of Multiple Overlapping Brain States as a Biomarker for Mental Disorders
b9d3cc3315b222603b894b8986579a124347f38a.abstract: Exploring the biomarkers linked to various psychiatric disorders is essential for improving diagnostic accuracy and monitoring disease progression. Recent developments in neuroimaging techniques have shifted the emphasis from conventional univariate approaches, which evaluate isolated brain areas, to sophisticated multivariate models that examine intricate interactions across multiple brain networks. Dynamic functional network connectivity (dFNC), the coupling among independent component fluctuations, has become an important method in this landscape, providing a sophisticated understanding of how connectivity fluctuates over time between brain regions. b8fda81b1c2a1023db5eedd819f49d4df17b6bfb.title: Mssanet: Multi-Scale Self-Attention Mechanism Network for Polyp Segmentation
b8fda81b1c2a1023db5eedd819f49d4df17b6bfb.abstract: Accurate medical image segmentation is the foundation of effective diagnosis and treatment, and efficient polyp segmentation is particularly crucial in the early diagnosis of colorectal cancer. At present, many segmentation algorithms are based on deep learning. However, although convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are highly efficient, their ability to model long-distance dependencies is limited. Although the Transformer has powerful performance, its computational cost and the number of parameters is large. To alleviate these challenges, we have proposed an efficient multi-scale segmentation model (MSSANet) specifically tailored for polyp segmentation in colonoscopy images. b899b1d5686c5ed4d7c247d22b82ae81647aa4f0.title: Two-Stage Cortical Surface Reconstruction from MRI with Arbitrary Slice Thickness
b899b1d5686c5ed4d7c247d22b82ae81647aa4f0.abstract: Reconstructing the cortical surface from brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans is crucial for cortical surface analysis. However, existing cortical surface reconstruction (CSR) methods are mostly tailored for high-resolution MRI with specific parameters, whereas clinical scans often suffer from thicker slices and inconsistent resolutions. To address this, we propose a two-stage deep learning approach for accurate and robust cortical surface reconstruction from MRI with arbitrary slice thickness. In the first stage, we employ an implicit neural representation (INR) super-resolution method with cycle-consistency loss to unify MRI with varying slice thicknesses to a consistent thickness while preserving underlying statistical properties. b7892e03fa21c9e1551c162a8a7736e6850c1393.title: Dynamic Group Joint ICA (Dyna-gjICA) Uncovers Neural Mechanisms Underlying Depression with and without Anxiety
b7892e03fa21c9e1551c162a8a7736e6850c1393.abstract: Multimodal fusion of electroencephalography (EEG) and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) remains challenging because EEG and fMRI differ in structure, and most existing methods compress their dynamics into static summaries. Previously, we developed a group joint independent component analysis (gjICA) framework to jointly decompose EEG and fMRI, but it did not capture spatially evolving fMRI networks. Here, we extend gjICA to dynamic gjICA (Dyna-gjICA) to incorporate spatial dynamic features of fMRI, enabling joint analysis of time-resolved fMRI networks and EEG spectral dynamics.
