b76e738afb0165edb4ec12359d009581f44c2d6c.title: Prompt-Free Lightweight Sam Adaptation for Histopathology Nuclei Segmentation with Strong Cross-Dataset Generalization
b76e738afb0165edb4ec12359d009581f44c2d6c.abstract: Histopathology nuclei segmentation is crucial for quantitative tissue analysis and cancer diagnosis. Although existing segmentation methods have achieved strong performance, they are often computationally heavy and show limited generalization across datasets, which constrains their practical deployment. Recent SAM-based approaches have shown great potential in general and medical imaging, but typically rely on prompt guidance or complex decoders, making them less suitable for histopathology images with dense nuclei and heterogeneous appearances. We propose a prompt-free and lightweight SAM adaptation that leverages multi-level encoder features and residual decoding for accurate and efficient nuclei segmentation. The framework fine-tunes only LoRA modules within the frozen SAM encoder, requiring just 4.1M trainable parameters. Experiments on three benchmark datasets TNBC, MoNuSeg, and Pan

b723549f9edaa31313dcc3d6e55d37372975b6fe.title: Scribble-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation With Dynamic Teacher Switching and Hierarchical Consistency
b723549f9edaa31313dcc3d6e55d37372975b6fe.abstract: Scribble-supervised methods have emerged to mitigate the prohibitive annotation burden in medical image segmentation. However, the inherent sparsity of these annotations introduces significant ambiguity, which results in noisy pseudo-label propagation and hinders the learning of robust anatomical boundaries. To address this challenge, we propose SDTNet, a novel dual-teacher, single-student framework designed to maximize supervision quality from these weak signals. Our method features a Dynamic Teacher Switching (DTS) module to adaptively select the most reliable teacher. This selected teacher then guides the student via two synergistic mechanisms: high-confidence pseudo-labels, refined by a Pick Reliable Pixels (PRP) mechanism, and multi-level feature alignment, enforced by a Hierarchical Consistency (HiCo) module. Extensive experiments on the ACDC and MSCMRseg datasets demonstrate that

b6dbf8ee9ecf84d0cb549594e2e5f9a4982dec6f.title: Iterative Confidence-Based Pseudo-Labeling for Semi-Supervised Lung Cancer Segmentation Under Annotation Scarcity
b6dbf8ee9ecf84d0cb549594e2e5f9a4982dec6f.abstract: Semi-supervised learning (SSL) offers a promising solution to the annotation scarcity challenge in medical image segmentation. In this work, we propose a novel iterative confidencebased SSL framework for 3D lung tumor segmentation that combines model ensembling with quality-aware pseudo-label selection. Using a few labeled CT scans only, our method estimates a confidence score from inter-model agreement showing strong correlation with segmentation quality and outperforming Monte Carlo Dropout uncertainty estimation. Further, by iteratively selecting the most confident pseudo-labels from unlabeled samples, our approach surpasses both supervised baselines and naive pseudo-labeling. An ablation study further confirms that the confidence score reliably discriminates pseudo-label quality, with high-confidence selections consistently outperforming random and low-confidence alternatives. More b

b60ace7ea599bfa30ec3a64287a0ec4c4c35d4c1.title: Robust Training of Deep Learning Models for Mammogram Classification
b60ace7ea599bfa30ec3a64287a0ec4c4c35d4c1.abstract: Deep neural networks are increasingly applied in healthcare to detect and diagnose medical conditions, including breast cancer through mammogram analysis. However, these models are vulnerable to adversarial attacks and distribution shifts, undermining diagnostic reliability and trust. This study explores baseline methods to address these vulnerabilities and proposes a modified robust training approach to enhance model robustness and reliability in mammogram analysis.

b4e3f5e657cc54e681bc27e0d7fbda90408bb8bb.title: Safm-Cta: Segmentation-Augmented Foundation Model for CT-to-CTA Translation
b4e3f5e657cc54e681bc27e0d7fbda90408bb8bb.abstract: Computed Tomography Angiography (CTA) synthesis from non-contrast Computed Tomography (CT) scans offers a contrast-free alternative for vascular assessment, particularly benefiting patients at risk from iodinated contrast agents. However, existing generative models such as GANs or diffusion networks often fail to maintain vascular continuity and anatomical realism. In this study, we propose SAFM-CTA, a Segmentation-Augmented Foundation Model for high-fidelity CT-to-CTA translation. SAFM-CTA integrates a pretrained 3D Vision Transformer encoder that captures global anatomical priors with a multitask decoder jointly trained for CTA synthesis and vascular segmentation. Through segmentation-guided optimization and vessel-weighted content loss, the model enforces explicit anatomical consistency during generation. Evaluated on 1,886 paired CT-CTA scans, SAFM-CTA surpasses state-of-the-art meth

b40941ac9cb2e407428209b3009d69385c815672.title: Training-Free One-Shot Medical Image Segmentation with SAM via Confidence and Consistency-Based Bidirectional Prompt Evolution
b40941ac9cb2e407428209b3009d69385c815672.abstract: Medical image segmentation is crucial for precise diagnosis and quantitative analysis, yet its widespread adoption faces two main challenges: 1) the high cost and expertise required for pixel-level annotation, and 2) the computational complexity of model training. Recently, vision foundation models (VFMs), particularly the Segment Anything Model (SAM), have demonstrated strong prompt-based generalization for accurate boundary detection. However, automatically generating precise prompts for SAM remains a key bottleneck. To address these issues, we propose a training-free, one-shot framework that generates prompts by transferring a label from a support image to a query image based on DINOv3 feature similarity. In addition, to enhance the accuracy of the prompts fed into SAM, we propose the Confidence and Consistency-based Bidirectional Prompt Evolution ($\mathrm{C}^{2}$ BPE) module, which

b35563dab221a10a9b61c51b28c275811d97b89f.title: MEDL: Unsupervised Multi-Stage Ensemble Deep Learning With Diffusion Models for Denoising MRI Scans
b35563dab221a10a9b61c51b28c275811d97b89f.abstract: Image denoising is a persistent challenge, often relying on paired datasets or known noise distributions. While deep neural networks are effective, they are impractical for medical applications like Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) due to their dependency on paired datasets and struggle with unknown noise distributions. Recent advances in self-supervised techniques and diffusion models allow denoising from a single noisy image, but current methods struggle with over-smoothing and hallucination, limiting clinical applicability. To address these issues, we propose a Multi-stage Ensemble Deep Learning framework that capitalizes on the power of diffusion models and operates independently of signal or noise priors. By rescaling multi-stage reconstructions, it balances smoothing and hallucination. Evaluations show a 1dB and 2.5% improvement in PSNR and SSIM over the best existing methods, with

b2f1d0e4926fbc581a20bdf56c268755168c08ea.title: Towards Causality-Aware Modeling for Multimodal Brain-Muscle Interactions
b2f1d0e4926fbc581a20bdf56c268755168c08ea.abstract: Robust characterization of dynamic causal interactions in multivariate biomedical signals is essential for advancing computational and algorithmic methods in biomedical imaging. Conventional approaches, such as Dynamic Bayesian Networks (DBNs), often assume linear or simple statistical dependencies, while manifold-based techniques like Convergent Cross Mapping (CCM) capture nonlinear, lagged interactions but lack probabilistic quantification and interventional modeling. We introduce a DBN-informed CCM framework that integrates geometric manifold reconstruction with probabilistic temporal modeling. Applied to multimodal EEG–EMG recordings from dystonic and neurotypical children, the method quantifies uncertainty, supports interventional simulation, and reveals distinct frequency-specific reorganization of cortico-muscular pathways in dystonia. Experimental results show marked improvements

b22e3836e951b10c8b7671d6537b15e7a94a6e0b.title: Adaptive Collaborative Learning Polyp Segmentation Framework Based on Contour-Driven Parallel Attention Network
b22e3836e951b10c8b7671d6537b15e7a94a6e0b.abstract: Automatic polyp segmentation plays a crucial role in the early diagnosis and treatment of colorectal cancer (CRC). However, this technology often faces challenges such as complex polyp morphology, unclear boundaries, and limited generalization capability of the algorithms. In response, a novel end-to-end polyp segmentation framework incorporating a parallel attention mechanism was proposed. The backbone collaborates with an adaptive active contour model that dynamically updates model evolution parameters during training to achieve optimal performance. This strategy enables mutual reinforcement and supervision between models. Additionally, the fractal geometric properties of the object were accounted during training, which reduces image noise while enhancing the model's sensitivity to polyp morphology. Our algorithm outperforms current state-of-the-art methods on multiple authoritative da

b226b5d2eafb64321936135f0ded71c58b6de561.title: Polyp Detection in Colonoscopy Videos via Boosted Multi-Scale Feature Fusion
b226b5d2eafb64321936135f0ded71c58b6de561.abstract: Computer-aided detection (CAD) systems are vital for advancing colorectal cancer screening and prevention through effective polyp detection approaches. Recent breakthroughs in deep learning technology have greatly enhanced medical image analysis and CAD systems for polyp detection. This paper proposes to use a boosted multi-scale feature fusion method for polyp detection in colonoscopy videos. The method is evaluated on a publicly available colonoscopy video dataset, in terms of metrics mAP, precision, recall and F1-score. In comparison with other state-of-the-art polyp detection methods, our method achieves better performance in both accuracy and efficiency, positioning it as a robust choice for real-time polyp detection in colonoscopy videos.

b1fe96589fbb9b87cae1c3c46cdf1425a9b97f09.title: Theoretical Bounds on Parallel Imaging Implicit Data Crimes in an MRI Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space
b1fe96589fbb9b87cae1c3c46cdf1425a9b97f09.abstract: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) diagnoses and manages a wide range of diseases, yet long scan times drive high costs and limit accessibility. AI methods have demonstrated substantial potential for reducing scan times, but despite rapid progress, clinical translation of AI often fails. One particular failure mode, referred to as implicit data crimes, is a result of hidden biases introduced when MRI datasets incompletely model the MRI physics of the acquisition. Previous work identified data crimes resulting from algorithmic completion of k -space with parallel imaging and drew on simulation to demonstrate the resulting downstream biases. This work proposes a mathematical framework to re-characterize the problem as one of error reduction during interpolation between sets of evaluation coordinates. We establish a generalized matrix-based definition of the reconstruction error upper bound a

b0ae389e8b84ae7b5d1eff911ffe5d04c7f25200.title: UCMoLE: Cluster-Routed Mixture of Low-Rank Experts for Endoscopic Ulcerative Colitis Captioning
b0ae389e8b84ae7b5d1eff911ffe5d04c7f25200.abstract: Automatic ulcerative colitis (UC) assessment is important for consistent clinical evaluation to support treatment planning and disease management. However, most existing UC scoring systems provide only discrete severity grades without detailed clinical explanations, limiting interpretability and comprehensive documentation. In this work, we propose a clusterrouted mixture of low-rank experts for endoscopic UC image captioning (UCMoLE), which generates both UC severity scores and clinically meaningful textual explanations to enable more trustworthy assessment. UCMoLE first learns a general low-rank expert to adapt a vision–language model to the endoscopy domain, then clusters the learned image embedding space and routes each test image to a specialist lowrank expert based on centroid distance, allowing fine-grained modelling of endoscopic images. In the EndoUC challenge, our method achiev

b013f03c710b3d2593eb2d32a7d24fe045b5977a.title: Population-Prior-Assisted Implicit Neural Representations for Instance-Specific Unsupervised Accelerated Mri Reconstruction
b013f03c710b3d2593eb2d32a7d24fe045b5977a.abstract: Accelerated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) remains challenging due to the inherent trade-off between scan time and image quality. Conventional compressed sensing (CS) degrades fast under aggressive undersampling. Supervised deep learning, especially unrolled methods, are promising. But they require large datasets with fully sampled k -space for training and generalize poorly across varied undersampling patterns and accelerations, limiting clinical translation. We propose an unsupervised instance-specific reconstruction framework that integrates Implicit Neural Representation (INR) with a population-pretrained autoencoder (AE) prior. The continuous modeling capacity of INR enables smooth interpolation and high-frequency detail recovery, while the plug-and-play AE prior constrains the solution to the manifold of feasible high-quality images. A three-stage optimization strategy is develop

afd0f060215f6fba009536758f3328f8189b6af0.title: Multi-Frequency Regularized Approach for Simultaneous Estimation of the Acoustic Nonlinearity Parameter and Attenuation Coefficient
afd0f060215f6fba009536758f3328f8189b6af0.abstract: The acoustic nonlinearity parameter (B/A) could enhance conventional ultrasound diagnostics in diseases associated with changes in fat tissue content. Recently, a simultaneous estimator of the B/A and the attenuation coefficient (AC) in pulse-echo was introduced, which was based on fitting measurements derived from backscattered data from a dual-energy model to a nonlinear model using the Gauss-Newton Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm (GNLM). However, the GNLM algorithm presented high sensitivity to the initial guess values. This paper improves the Gauss-Newton method by using data from several tone-burst transmissions at different center frequencies rather than only one narrowband tone-burst. In addition, it is combined with a total variation regularization approach (GNTV). The results in simulated and experimental phantoms suggest that incorporating regularization and increasing the number

af4a0c35d6858df3c20512d6a956b0f5eb852951.title: DYSC-CCA: Dynamic Similarity-Constrained Canonical Correlation Analysis for Multimodal Alzheimer's Diagnosis
af4a0c35d6858df3c20512d6a956b0f5eb852951.abstract: Imaging genetics integrates imaging modalities (e.g., MRI and PET) with genomic data and has made significant progress in identifying biomarkers and aiding disease diagnosis, most often through canonical correlation analysis (CCA). Existing CCA-based studies have focused on maximizing crossmodal correlations, overlooking (i) patient-wise similarity patterns that sharpen diagnostic boundaries and (ii) the feature redundancy that arises when high-dimensional, highly correlated modalities are combined. Here, we propose Dynamic Similarity Constrained-CCA (DySC-CCA), a deep CCA framework for Alzheimer's disease (AD) diagnosis that aligns patient-wise relationships across modalities. It also has an orthogonality-based regularizer that suppresses redundant information and enforces feature complementarity. We evaluated DySC-CCA on the ADNI dataset using three imaging modalities and genetic data

ae8995a7abcd674c98450d0e4bf3a771231794f9.title: Interactive Surgical Visualization with Real-Time Endoscopic Scene Reconstruction and Functional Imaging Overlay
ae8995a7abcd674c98450d0e4bf3a771231794f9.abstract: Minimally invasive surgery benefits from dynamic 3D scene reconstruction, yet existing frameworks often rely on post-surgical training, providing limited interactivity and neglecting biologically meaningful signals. Moreover, processing entire surgical videos incurs substantial computational and latency overhead, limiting practical intraoperative use. We introduce a framework for live 3D endoscopic reconstruction with surgeon-in-the-loop control that integrates frame-aligned intraoperative Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging (FLIm) into the reconstructed scene to enrich functional context. Our system processes batch-wise video streams to incrementally reconstruct the surgical scene in 3D, while tracking per-frame FLIm through tissue deformation and superimposing it onto a 3D Gaussian Splatting representation via depth-guided colored Gaussian markers. A linked frontend interface enables rapid i

ae421483f6fe80d90566bba6fcb4310bb69d75b3.title: Diffusion Autoencoder for Unsupervised Artifact Restoration in Handheld Fundus Images
ae421483f6fe80d90566bba6fcb4310bb69d75b3.abstract: The advent of handheld fundus imaging devices has made ophthalmologic diagnosis and disease screening more accessible, efficient, and cost-effective. However, images captured from these setups often suffer from artifacts such as flash reflections, exposure variations, and motion-induced blur, which degrade image quality and hinder downstream analysis. While generative models have been effective in image restoration, most depend on paired supervision or predefined artifact structures, making them less adaptable to unstructured degradations commonly observed in handheld fundus images. To address this, we propose an unsupervised diffusion autoencoder that integrates a context encoder with the denoising process to learn semantically meaningful representations for artifact restoration. The model is trained only on high-quality table-top fundus images and infers to restore artifact-affected ha

adcdfc5ba7a60a05d20f9e06882817952904e36d.title: MUM: Enhancing Medical Diagnostics Through Unpaired Multimodal Data Integration
adcdfc5ba7a60a05d20f9e06882817952904e36d.abstract: Most AI healthcare applications are single-modality, focusing on tasks like electrocardiogram-based arrhythmia detection or echocardiogram interpretation for heart function. Yet, effective clinical decision-making often requires integrating diverse data sources, such as biosignals, imaging, audio, and lab reports. While multimodal integration could allow more accurate, personalized diagnostics, current approaches rely heavily on paired datasets, which are costly and challenging to curate. This limits applicability, despite the availability of unpaired data. We propose Multi-Uni-Modal (MUM), an efficient multimodal multitask learning framework that handles both paired and unpaired datasets, combining the diagnostic power of multimodal learning with the simplicity of training unimodal models. Extensive experiments show that MUM improves task performance by 2.7-4% while reducing learnable p

ad4f00a8b59a4f5dba32f36921d88f02512b5b9d.title: Efficient Fine-Tuning of SAM for Interactive Medical Image Multi-Organ Segmentation
ad4f00a8b59a4f5dba32f36921d88f02512b5b9d.abstract: Recently, Segment Anything Model (SAM) has significantly advanced interactive segmentation techniques, particularly its fine-tuned variants in medical imaging. Although previous approaches can adapt SAM to diverse downstream tasks with additional data, two challenges persist. On the one hand, organ ambiguities render SAM susceptible to human factor prompts, leading to unsatisfactory segmentation results. On the other hand, fine-tuning with massive data and the segment-single-region paradigm incur considerable computational and time costs. To this end, we propose to efficiently fine-tune SAM for interactive multi-organ medical segmentation by parallel heuristic prompt generation (PHPG) and class-balanced data pruning (CBDP). Specifically, PHPG generates prompts for diverse human behaviors guided by error prediction, effectively enhancing the consistency of prompts between training and tes

acc754c5f2fd3ad3d3b79b71fbc4b74ac8bc2c5e.title: Two-Stage Physics-Guided Self-Supervised Quantitative MRI with Diffusion-Based Refinement for Synthetic DIR Imaging in Multiple Sclerosis
acc754c5f2fd3ad3d3b79b71fbc4b74ac8bc2c5e.abstract: Quantitative mapping and double inversion recovery (DIR) imaging enhance lesion visibility in multiple sclerosis (MS) but are limited by long, non-routine acquisition times. We propose a physics-guided self-supervised framework to estimate T1, T2, and PD maps directly from standard clinical scans (T1w, T2w, and FLAIR). Stage 1 utilizes a conditional GAN to generate pseudo-quantitative maps constrained by Bloch-based forward modeling, enabling training without paired labels. Stage 2 leverages these pseudo-labels to learn a conditional diffusion prior, followed by physics-consistency posterior sampling to derive high-fidelity quantitative maps. Evaluation on 50 MS patients demonstrates that our twostage approach significantly outperforms GAN-only baselines, achieving up to +28 dB PSNR gain and near-perfect structural agreement (SSIM $\approx 0.999$). The refined maps enable high-quality DI

acb2fe79a7419b5925d2d7e82c692f48d41f053e.title: Depression Detection Using Face Videos from Clinical Interviews
acb2fe79a7419b5925d2d7e82c692f48d41f053e.abstract: Depression affects a large number of people, especially Japan's suicide rate remains high, causing severe health and economic consequences. However, identifying depression is difficult because it lacks objectivity and is highly dependent on the experience of the physicians to identify non-verbal symptoms. In this paper, we investigated the accuracy of depression detection using videos of natural conversations between patients and physicians in clinical interviews. In our study, a large database of clinical interview videos of 297 patients who visited Tokyo Women's Medical University (TWMU) Hospital from April 2024 to April 2025 was used. The features used in this study were extracted only from the head direction and the upper part of the face (mainly eyes and eyebrows), allowing depression detection even when patients wear surgical masks during clinical interviews, which is a common prac

ac4f233bdc7d9d36686dfb6432b6f20f5601ddb6.title: Vessel-Aware Deep Learning for OCTA-Based Detection of AMD
ac4f233bdc7d9d36686dfb6432b6f20f5601ddb6.abstract: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is characterized by early micro-vascular alterations that can be captured noninvasively using optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA), yet most deep learning (DL) models rely on global features and fail to exploit clinically meaningful vascular biomarkers. We introduce an external multiplicative attention framework that incorporates vessel-specific tortuosity maps and vasculature dropout maps derived from arteries, veins, and capillaries. These biomarker maps are generated from vessel segmentations and smoothed across multiple spatial scales to highlight coherent patterns of vascular remodeling and capillary rarefaction. Tortuosity reflects abnormalities in vessel geometry linked to impaired auto-regulation, while dropout maps capture localized perfusion deficits that precede structural retinal damage. The maps are fused with the OCTA projec

ac3c3504381bba4523af0101ade334f61b8f57bc.title: Ultrasharp: Beltrami Transformers for Ultrasound Super-Resolution
ac3c3504381bba4523af0101ade334f61b8f57bc.abstract: Ultrasound (US) super-resolution (SR) is challenged by anisotropic point spread functions (PSFs), multiplicative speckle noise, and the clinical need for edge fidelity at tissue interfaces. We propose UltraSharp, a geometry- and physics-aware transformer that injects Beltrami image geometry into attention while enforcing formation-consistent reconstruction. The proposed framework employs edge-aware Beltrami positional encodings to capture geodesic structure, anisotropic geodesic attention to limit cross-boundary feature mixing, and physics- and speckle-aware losses to preserve realistic texture statistics. Across cardiac, breast, and fetal US, UltraSharp improves edge quality and texture while maintaining fidelity. We report standard SR metrics and USspecific measures, including contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), edge spread, speckle SNR, and downstream segmentation accuracy.

ac21ce97ce9141c8c70ef2c6d3ee1a69fbcd9f17.title: When Vision-Language Models Look but Don't See: Anatomical Bias in Endoscopic Spatial Reasoning
ac21ce97ce9141c8c70ef2c6d3ee1a69fbcd9f17.abstract: Reliable spatial understanding is essential for complete mucosal inspection during upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, particularly under the Systematic Screening Protocol for the Stomach (SSS). Vision-Language Models (VLMs) show promise for assisting navigation but often rely on textual priors rather than visual information, a limitation known as anatomical bias. To evaluate spatial reasoning, we introduce EndoSSS-RP, a benchmark based on the GastroHUN dataset (380 patients, 2,796 images, 3,678 binary questions). Each question, targeting left/right or above/below relationships between gastric surfaces (e.g., anterior vs. posterior wall), is tested on original, flipped, and rotated images to assess model robustness in determining relative position across different orientations. Prompts are structured across three levels: L1 (anatomical terms only), L2 (anatomical terms with visual markers)

abe2f2488e7d3c248ebb556bb692b8886c8b7a27.title: Reconstruction Algorithm Based on Multi-Harmonic Feature Fusion and Enhanced U-Net for Low-Concentration Magnetic Particle Imaging
abe2f2488e7d3c248ebb556bb692b8886c8b7a27.abstract: To address weak signals and severe background artifacts in low-concentration magnetic particle imaging, this paper proposes a noise-resilient reconstruction algorithm based on multi-harmonic feature fusion and an enhanced U-Net(MH-U-Net). Our algorithm introduces enhancements in both the signal and image domains to improve the reconstruction quality. In the signal domain, the algorithm performs a weighted fusion of the imaginary parts of the 3rd and 5th harmonics, utilizes filtered back projection to preserve highfrequency edges, and employs a grid search to determine the optimal weights. In the image domain, an optimized U-Net architecture driven by a joint loss function is employed for precise denoising. Experimental results demonstrate that our algorithm achieves high structural similarity on the training set, demonstrating a substantial performance improvement compared to the baselin

aa989266490437145978c11e10154c882572df4b.title: A Calibrated Memorization Index (MI) for Detecting Training Data Leakage in Generative MRI Models
aa989266490437145978c11e10154c882572df4b.abstract: Image generative models are known to duplicate images from the training data as part of their outputs, which can lead to privacy concerns when used for medical image generation. We propose a calibrated per-sample metric for detecting memorization and duplication of training data. Our metric uses image features extracted using an MRI foundation model, aggregates multi-layer whitened nearest-neighbor similarities, and maps them to a bounded Overfit/Novelty Index (ONI) and Memorization Index (MI) scores. Across three MRI datasets with controlled duplication percentages and typical image augmentations, our metric robustly detects duplication and provides more consistent metric values across datasets. At the sample level, our metric achieves near-perfect detection of duplicates.

aa749746a1aaa910e3e3a57729d0089c350698ab.title: Enhancing Early Liver Cancer Diagnosis: AI-Based Detection of Small Malignant Lesions on Contrast-Enhanced CT
aa749746a1aaa910e3e3a57729d0089c350698ab.abstract: This study presents an AI-based computer-aided detection (CADe) solution that integrates multiple deep neural networks to identify hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and other malignant lesions. The solution is designed to assist radiologists in detecting liver cancer during CT image interpretation.

a9f3a53e275fa4dcc614593bfea8e682fdf1319e.title: Multi-Branch and Multi-Task Learning Framework for Autism Diagnosis with Modality Incomplete Data
a9f3a53e275fa4dcc614593bfea8e682fdf1319e.abstract: Multimodal neuroimaging has shown promise for improving the diagnosis of brain disorders. However, its clinical applicability is often limited by incomplete data due to high acquisition costs, equipment constraints, or patient compliance. Existing strategies, such as data imputation and knowledge distillation, suffer from noise propagation and poor adaptability to diverse missing modality scenarios. To overcome these challenges, we propose a novel MultiBranch and Multi-Task Learning (MBMT) framework that leverages hard parameter sharing (HPS) to enhance knowledge transfer and incorporates feature disentanglement (FD) to effectively separate specific and common representations, reducing redundancy and noise while enabling complementary multimodal integration. Results showed that MBMT achieved superior performance on autism diagnostic tasks with varying levels of modality incompleteness, d

a9773476f751039fc838aa6170f50c75a9fea05a.title: Identifying Brain Strokes by Image Analysis Using Transfer Learning
a9773476f751039fc838aa6170f50c75a9fea05a.abstract: Brain Stroke is a life-threatening medical condition that requires prompt diagnosis and treatment to minimize its devastating effects like partial paralysis, speech impairment, and memory loss. The classification of brain strokes is crucial for accurate and timely medical treatment. Our research employs transfer learning, such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), ResNet, RadiNet, and MobileNet algorithms, to classify brain strokes from Computed Tomography (CT) scans, focusing on improving both the speed and accuracy of stroke diagnosis using transfer learning techniques. To deal with the unbalanced nature of the dataset, we implemented various features of data augmentation techniques and achieved class balance in the dataset. Our proposed model MobileNet on augmented down-sampling dataset demonstrates, exceptional overall F1-scores achieving up to 99%, precision of 99% and recall of 9

a9514e6a955bd98f9e45643d979b715a57eb160d.title: Robust Classification of Urinary Sediment with Limited Data Through Semi-Supervised Ensemble Models
a9514e6a955bd98f9e45643d979b715a57eb160d.abstract: This paper proposes ensemble-based approaches to improve classification performance with limited labeled data in urine sediment images. These methods achieve significant advancements over conventional approaches. In experiments, for the case with 102 labeled data points, the proposed techniques achieved F1 scores of 0.884 and 0.901, substantially outperforming state-of-the-art baselines in both precision and recall. Classification accuracy for rare classes, such as Cryst and Cast, also improved considerably. These results emphasize the effectiveness of ensembling in reducing overfitting and variance in data-scarce settings, particularly enhancing stability and accuracy for rare particle classification. This approach holds potential for fields like medical imaging, where data is often limited, yet high classification performance is essential.

a8c82bdf84fe2f69975bd991f43ad0b395bff720.title: EDA: Enhanced Domain-Adversarial Training for Anatomical Landmark Detection
a8c82bdf84fe2f69975bd991f43ad0b395bff720.abstract: Manually annotating anatomical landmarks in medical images requires experienced clinicians and is a labor-intensive process. However, recent AI-assisted methods for landmark detection often rely on the training and test data originating from the same domain. This work introduces a novel unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) framework aimed at anatomical landmark detection from a medical image, designed to bridge the gap between a source domain with labels and an unlabeled target domain. Specifically, we have developed a new Domain-Adversarial Network that incorporates skip connections to transfer and fuse high-resolution feature maps. Additionally, we proposed Dynamic Gaussian Learning, which allows the model to escape from local error regions. We carry out experiments on landmark detection for both head and chest, and the results demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art perf

a8c09bcd9ec2bb3238400576b51bec3c0a9d6cb9.title: RWKVFUSE: Parallel Encoders Network for Medical Image Segmentation
a8c09bcd9ec2bb3238400576b51bec3c0a9d6cb9.abstract: Medical image segmentation is essential for accurate lesion identification and disease diagnosis. Conventional CNN-based methods are limited by their restricted receptive fields, whereas Transformer models effectively capture global dependencies but incur quadratic computational costs. Recently, sequence modeling approaches with linear attention mechanisms, such as the RWKV, have demonstrated the ability to model long-range dependencies with linear complexity. To address this, we propose a dual-encoder architecture, RWKVFuse, which integrates VRWKV and CNNs to extract fine-grained spatial features and long-range dependencies. Extensive experiments across four imaging modalities show that the proposed RWKVFuse model outperforms state-of-the-art methods in metrics such as DSC and HD95. Our code is available at: https://github.com/alqurri/rwkv

a8b29eab28b0bf1409602d1714ce5939aba0e926.title: Functional Network Connectivity in White Matter: A Group Informed ICA-Based Network Approach
a8b29eab28b0bf1409602d1714ce5939aba0e926.abstract: White matter (WM) has traditionally been undervalued in functional brain connectivity studies due to its weaker blood-oxygenation-level-dependent (BOLD) signals compared to gray matter (GM). Conventional atlas-based approaches often overlook the individualized aspects of functional networks, limiting their applicability for WM. In this study, we introduce the first WM intrinsic connectivity network (ICN) templates derived from a large dataset of over 100,000 scans, demonstrating the feasibility of estimating individualized WM networks using multivariate-spatially constrained ICA (scICA). By combining WM and GM ICNs, our work provides an expanded framework for evaluating functional network connectivity (FNC) across both tissue types, offering new insights into the integrative role of WM in functional connectivity. This approach holds particular promise for enhancing the understanding of c

a8a3586062ac3446d87214e5886960b5c0605ab9.title: Hyper-DSCNet: Integrating Radiographic Details and Syndromic Context with Hypergraph Learning for Chest X-Ray Detection
a8a3586062ac3446d87214e5886960b5c0605ab9.abstract: Chest X-ray imaging plays a crucial role in thoracic disease screening, yet faces challenges in detecting complex lesions ranging from micro-nodules to interconnected syndromes like heart failure. Current deep learning models exhibit limitations in local detail perception and multi-lesion semantic relationship modeling. Based on this, we propose Hyper-DSCNet, a Hypergraph learning method that integrates three core modules: a Radiographic Detail Enhancement(RDE) module for small lesions, a Syndromic Context Modeling (SCM) module for capturing high-order associations, and a Multi-finding Adaptive Fusion (MFA) module for dynamic feature integration. Evaluation on the ChestX-Det dataset shows 3.0% AP50 and 6.8% AP-s improvements over baselines, demonstrating strong performance and clinical potential.

a89075e67e8353ee873bb08385a916f060329758.title: BrainTAP: Brain Disorder Prediction with Adaptive Distill and Selective Prior Integration
a89075e67e8353ee873bb08385a916f060329758.abstract: Predicting clinical outcomes from brain networks in largescale neuroimaging cohorts such as the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study requires effectively integrating functional connectivity (FC) and structural connectivity (SC) while incorporating expert neurobiological knowledge. However, existing multimodal fusion approaches are shallow or over-homogenize the inherently heterogeneous characteristics of FC and SC, while expert-defined anatomical priors are underutilized with static integration. To address these limitations, we propose Brain Transformer with Adaptive Mutual-Distill and Selective Prior Fusion (BrainTAP). We introduce Adaptive Mutual Distill (AMD), which enables layer-wise information exchange between modalities through learnable distill-intact ratios, preserving modalityspecific signals while capturing cross-modal synergies. We further develop Selective Pri

a7a7e6d30d3883f388044c8ac1c98607aaa163ae.title: Texture-Guided Adversarial Segmentation of Non-Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer in T2-Weighted Imaging
a7a7e6d30d3883f388044c8ac1c98607aaa163ae.abstract: The segmentation of non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) from T2-weighted imaging remains challenging due to tumors blending with the bladder wall and exhibit a wide range of shapes and textures. This study proposes a hybrid framework that integrates engineered texture features with a generative adversarial network (GAN) to improve the segmentation of NMIBC in 118 patients. The generator receives a three channel input from the ROI of grayscale image, a texture probability map derived from the joint histogramanalysis of circular binary pattern (CBP) descriptor, and the adaptive texture-appearance probability computed through dynamic neighborhood matching in joint grayscale–CBP space. These channels help the network to identify consistent tissue patterns and differentiate areas that seem to have similar brightness by modeling how texture and intensity vary together across nearby pixe

a7868670dbbd5822e22eb5a44ce0b1489a21b068.title: Joint-Specialist Learning with Endoscopic Descriptor Guidance for Ulcerative Colitis Grading
a7868670dbbd5822e22eb5a44ce0b1489a21b068.abstract: Accurate endoscopic grading of ulcerative colitis (UC) is essential for disease monitoring and treatment planning. Most existing approaches focus on predicting either the Mayo endoscopic score (MES) or ulcerative colitis endoscopic index of severity (UCEIS) independently, without modeling their clinical relationship. In the work, we propose a multi-task joint-specialist learning framework with endoscopic descriptor guidance (JSL-EDG) for comprehensive UC grading. Our method employs a shared encoder to jointly learn representations for both MES and UCEIS, while two dedicated specialist models further enhance specific scoring for each task. We present an endoscopic descriptor loss that supervises metadata to strengthen clinically meaningful learning for UCEIS. Additionally, we introduce a descriptor-UCEIS consistency loss to align the predicted UCEIS scores with metadata, using severity co

a67a49c3f863e38db389eb06dd99b133f2b3ef80.title: Automated Prediction of Paravalvular Regurgitation Before Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation
a67a49c3f863e38db389eb06dd99b133f2b3ef80.abstract: Severe aortic stenosis is a common and life-threatening condition in elderly patients, often treated with Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation (TAVI). Despite procedural advances, paravalvular aortic regurgitation (PVR) remains one of the most frequent post-TAVI complications, with a proven impact on long-term prognosis. In this work, we investigate the potential of deep learning to predict the occurrence of PVR from preoperative cardiac CT. To this end, a dataset of preoperative TAVI patients was collected, and 3D convolutional neural networks were trained on isotropic CT volumes. The results achieved suggest that volumetric deep learning can capture subtle anatomical features from pre-TAVI imaging, opening new perspectives for personalized risk assessment and procedural optimization.

a674a41e647ecdc01a4f13784a56172eb4629956.title: Synthesizing Brain Magnetic Resonance Images for Myelin Assessment
a674a41e647ecdc01a4f13784a56172eb4629956.abstract: Myelin is a critical factor in brain development, aging, and neurological disorders, including Alzheimer's disease and traumatic brain injury. The ratio of <tex>$T_{1}$</tex>-weighted to <tex>$T_{2}$</tex> weighted (<tex>$T_{1} \mathrm{w} / T_{2} \mathrm{w}$</tex>) MRI intensities is a proxy for intracortical myelin content, but the scarcity of <tex>$T_{2} \mathrm{w}$</tex> MRIs limits the utility of this method in research and clinical practice. We present T2VNet, a 3D autoencoder synthesizing <tex>$T_{2} \mathrm{w}$</tex> MRIs from <tex>$T_{1}$</tex> w MRIs to allow myelin computation. Trained on 1,033 participants and evaluated on an independent cohort of 140 participants, T2VNet demonstrates strong performance in recovering clinically relevant contrast (MultiSSIM3 <tex>$\simeq 0.90$</tex>, PSNR <tex>$>27 \text{dB}$</tex>). a655ed6eef5cc3fa38d01487234320ebde69dc06.title: MedDataset: Synthesizing Infinite Image and Segmentation Data Using Diffusion Models
a655ed6eef5cc3fa38d01487234320ebde69dc06.abstract: Deep learning models perform best when trained on large datasets, but in medical imaging, obtaining such data is challenging due to privacy concerns, scarcity of rare conditions, high costs, and time-intensive annotations. Generative models, particularly diffusion models, offer a promising solution by creating high-quality synthetic data with minimal effort. In this paper, we introduce MedDataset, an end-to-end framework that generates diverse synthetic medical images along with their segmentation masks without relying on any conditional inputs like masks or labels during image generation. Our approach leverages an unconditional diffusion model to produce images, and a novel Time-Gated Decoder that decodes the rich latent features into accurate segmentation masks by effectively utilizing information from different noise levels in the diffusion process. Remarkably, training the decoder re

a6028bf72099d38c8c2446808fd762cb2ac583a1.title: Automated Sarcopenia Risk Stratification from POCUS Using Vision Transformers and Radiomics
a6028bf72099d38c8c2446808fd762cb2ac583a1.abstract: Sarcopenia is an age-related condition characterized by progressive loss of skeletal muscle mass, quality and function, leading to increased morbidity and mortality. Early detection remains challenging due to lack of scalable assessment tools. POCUS offers a portable, non-ionizing modality for bedside muscle evaluation, but currently analysis is operator dependent and time-consuming. This study proposes, an automated framework for sarcopenia risk stratification from standardized POCUS acquisitions. A Vision transformer-based segmentation model (UltraSAM) was fine-tuned to delineate three lower-limb muscles in Bmode ultrasound images acquired from 70 elderly inpatients. The model achieved 88.0% Dice and 79.6%. IoU. Segmentation masks were used to automatically estimate muscle thickness and extract reproducible radiomic features, which were combined with clinical variables. This feature se

a5c3b032f908a295fb35d6ea1060f6df4ca3ca38.title: Decomposing Pathological Features into Patho-Spatial Graphs for Skin Lesion Diagnosis
a5c3b032f908a295fb35d6ea1060f6df4ca3ca38.abstract: Existing deep learning models for skin lesion diagnosis often operate as black boxes, lacking an explicit understanding of the pathological structures topology, which contradicts the diagnostic logic of dermatologists. To address this, we introduce DermPrism, a novel multi-stage framework. At its core is the Patho-Spatial Graph (PSG) Block, which decomposes the visual representation into a structured pathological graph. This is achieved by a Pathological Characteristic Point (PCP) Miner that identifies diagnostically salient points, a Hierarchical Graph Connector that builds a multi-scale topological map, and a Geometric Learner that reasons over this graph. By explicitly modeling the where and how of pathological features, DermPrism bridges the critical gap between pixel-level recognition and high-level clinical reasoning. Experiments demonstrate that our topology-aware, decompositional

a4cdeb7349ae59a080b988b5f2e8effa3db87b40.title: LIDSS: A Latent Information-Driven Dynamic Framework for Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
a4cdeb7349ae59a080b988b5f2e8effa3db87b40.abstract: Semi-supervised learning has emerged as a promising approach to address the challenge of scarce high-quality annotations in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) segmentation. However, existing methods often suffer from limited segmentation accuracy due to difficulties in effectively leveraging labeled data, which stems from low tissue contrast, ambiguous anatomical boundaries, and a lack of reliable supervision in unlabeled regions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel latent information-driven dynamic semi-supervised segmentation (LIDSS) framework. LIDSS incorporates three key components: an enhanced boundary refinement module (EBRM) to improve discriminative feature extraction along tissue borders, a confidence-guided adaptive replacement module (CGAR) that enhances feature learning robustness through an adaptive fusion mechanism, and a self-contrasting auxiliary training stra

a4b35dd1a2ce4e2276fd52086c26d27d9a866bd8.title: Superficial White Matter Microstructure Alterations in the Right Temporal Lobe Associated with Post-Traumatic Epilepsy
a4b35dd1a2ce4e2276fd52086c26d27d9a866bd8.abstract: Post-traumatic epilepsy (PTE), a delayed consequence of traumatic brain injury (TBI), typically arises more than a week post-injury. While pathological changes in white matter (WM) post-TBI have been highlighted using diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), alterations in superficial white matter (SWM)-key in cortico-cortical connectivity-are less understood in PTE. We analyzed DTI metrics (AD, MD, RD, and FA) across 68 SWM regions in 27 TBI patients with PTE and 41 without, as part of the EpiBioS4Rx study. Employing Elastic Net Regression (ENR), we achieved an average area under the curve (AUC) of 0.86 in classifying PTE from TBI patients and identified critical SWM regions linked to PTE, including the right temporal pole, parahippocampal gyrus, and superior temporal gyrus. These SWM alterations correlated with functional outcomes, marking an important advancement in understanding microstructur

a3c61e7b41023e4285bced899490072964e6fabe.title: Hypernetwork-Based Adaptive Aggregation for Multimodal Multiple-Instance Learning in Predicting Coronary Calcium Debulking
a3c61e7b41023e4285bced899490072964e6fabe.abstract: In this paper, we present the first attempt to estimate the necessity of debulking coronary artery calcifications from computed tomography (CT) images. We formulate this task as a Multiple-instance Learning (MIL) problem. The difficulty of this task lies in that physicians adjust their focus and decision criteria for device usage according to tabular data representing each patient's condition. To address this issue, we propose a hypernetwork-based adaptive aggregation transformer (HyperAdAgFormer), which adaptively modifies the feature aggregation strategy for each patient based on tabular data through a hypernetwork. The experiments using the clinical dataset demonstrated the effectiveness of HyperAdAgFormer.

a3774d8c4562eaba0790c996ace854bda66aa5ee.title: Multimodal MRI and 18F-FPIA PET for Non-Invasive IDH Mutation Prediction Using MRI-Foundation Model Embeddings
a3774d8c4562eaba0790c996ace854bda66aa5ee.abstract: Non-invasive prediction of isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) mutation status in gliomas remains a major challenge. We assessed the applicability of an MRI-based foundation model for IDH classification in two complementary settings. (1) MRI-only setting: XGBoost classifiers were trained on the BraTS dataset and externally validated on an independent clinical 18F-FPIA PET-MRI (mpFPIA) cohort using features derived exclusively from MRI sequences (T1, FLAIR, ASL, ADC). (2) Multimodal PET-MRI setting: static 18F-FPIA-PET-derived embeddings were integrated with MRI embeddings, and performance was evaluated via 5 -fold crossvalidation within the mpFPIA cohort. In the MRI-only analysis, the T1+FLAIR+ASL combination achieved the strongest external validation (accuracy 0.80, AUC 0.90) after dimensionality reduction to five principal components. a32dda14d12d50c6cf35dfa4f99a9006f23e1359.title: Mitral Valve Deep Learning Localization in CT Scans for MIMVR Surgery
a32dda14d12d50c6cf35dfa4f99a9006f23e1359.abstract: Minimal invasive mitral valve repair (MIVMR), a recently developed method guided by video endoscopy, still remains complex and technically challenging. The clinical outcomes are strongly dependent on the appropriate choice of the thoracic incision, since it enables, or not, a good visualization and manipulation of the valve. This makes the accurate localization of mitral valve very important. In this paper, we propose a mitral valve deep learning localization method employing an edgepoint-based approach instead of traditional segmentation. Leveraging existing annotations of heart chambers, our method extracts relevant 2D slices surrounding the mitral valve annulus from CT scans, capturing both global structural and local texture features. These fused features are processed through a deep learning-based 2D landmark localization network to automatically detect the leaflet edgepoints. Subse

a320a4e8373e3e2a5826afba02de2bad742c1248.title: A Foundation Model for Cell Segmentation from Immunohistochemistry: A Pilot Study
a320a4e8373e3e2a5826afba02de2bad742c1248.abstract: Cell segmentation plays an important role in the basic research and disease diagnosis of immunohistochemistry (IHC). Although frontiers of large foundation models have been well investigated in H&E stained computational pathology, few works have focused on the diverse and complex analytics of IHC cells, meaning there is currently no foundation model specifically pre-trained on IHC datasets. Furthermore, existing foundation models fail to adequately consider the diversity of contextual priors in IHC images, such as imaging, preparation, and staining methods. Additionally, in downstream segmentation tasks, the popular transformer architecture lacks designs for capturing the subtle structural features of cells. a20d43267518100d4d5da93034c50c21cb8bc0bb.title: Deep Vortography: Intracardiac Vortex Analysis Using Color Doppler
a20d43267518100d4d5da93034c50c21cb8bc0bb.abstract: We present a deep-learning framework that estimates the two-dimensional left ventricular stream function directly from conventional color Doppler, bypassing velocity vector reconstruction. Ground-truth stream functions were computed from $i$ VFM-reconstructed polar velocity components and used to train an U-Net that takes five polar-grid channels as input (de-aliased Doppler velocity, Doppler power, binary left-ventricular cavity mask, and radial and angular coordinates) and outputs the stream function $\psi(r, \theta)$. Vortical regions were identified by the largest closed iso-contours of $\psi$. On a patient test set (317 frames from 3 patients), the model achieved a global $R^{2}=0.94$ and a normalized RMSE of $7.0 \% \pm 4.1 \%$, with strong spatial agreement of vortex regions (Dice of $0.90 \pm 0.02)$. a1f6710b370e6d27a13ac0431924b7445833b132.title: Multi-Map Fusion for Weakly Supervised Disease Localization from Globally Assigned Diagnostic Labels in Brain MRI
a1f6710b370e6d27a13ac0431924b7445833b132.abstract: Deep learning for brain MRI analysis is often limited by the need for dense voxelwise annotations, which are costly and unreliable for subtle abnormalities. We propose GALAFormer, a weakly supervised Transformer-based framework that localizes disease-relevant regions using only subjectlevel diagnostic labels propagated to 2D slices. The method aggregates complementary internal localization signals-tokenlevel activation, attention rollout, and gradient-based rele-vance-through a confidence-guided fusion module, enabling anatomically coherent and interpretable localization without spatial supervision. Experiments on three $\mathrm{T}_{1}$-weighted MRI datasets spanning tumors, multiple sclerosis, and Alzheimer's disease demonstrate robust generalization and consistently improved localization over existing weakly supervised approaches.

a1cb8a23f2e3cd6f636cc194c221330a1e4d59d1.title: Breaking the Disconnection Dilemma in Class-Imbalanced Cerebrovascular Segmentation
a1cb8a23f2e3cd6f636cc194c221330a1e4d59d1.abstract: Cerebrovascular segmentation plays a vital role in medical image processing, as it aids in diagnosing and treating cere-brovascular diseases. However, current methods often fail to meet the practical accuracy standards required in clinical settings. This paper presents a novel cerebrovascular segmentation method based on 3D UNet. First, we construct a connectivity matrix to obtain cerebrovascular connectivity information, which is then combined with the centreline distance weighted loss to effectively reduce errors caused by disconnection and class imbalance. To validate the effectiveness of this method, we conducted a series of experiments on a public dataset, and the results demonstrated significant performance improvements across multiple metrics in the cerebrovascular segmentation task.

a1b6bc9712d9b8a19f9b776bb0e426b11bebacf6.title: From Binary to Continuous: Learning to Continuously Quantify Histopathological Patterns from Binary Labeled Images
a1b6bc9712d9b8a19f9b776bb0e426b11bebacf6.abstract: Quantifying histopathological patterns on continuous scales is clinically valuable but often impractical due to annotation costs; most public datasets provide only binary or categorical labels. We present a probabilistic regression framework that learns continuous scores from binary supervision. Image patches are encoded into a latent space where a small set of learned prototypes captures intra-class variability. A Kernel Density Matrix (KDM) layer maps latent features to a full predictive distribution, enabling uncertainty estimations and prototype based interpretability. We study the approach on BreastPathQ, using its continuous cellularity scores only for evaluation while training with binarized labels. The method reconstructs the continuous value and yields uncertainty-aware predictions that are traceable to prototypical evidence. While our experiments are limited to a single dataset

a171ab4e43f47debc034745b5b56b0cd89e6971e.title: Predicting Axillary Lymph Node Metastasis in Breast Cancer by Integrating Dual-ROI Features from Multi-Parametric MRI
a171ab4e43f47debc034745b5b56b0cd89e6971e.abstract: Prediction of axillary lymph node metastasis in breast cancer is a critical factor in determining the prognosis of breast cancer patients and the necessity of axillary intervention. However, current research methods are limited to single-parameter MRI sequences, only use images from the primary tumor area or the axillary lymph node region, and the methods for achieving feature fusion pay relatively little attention to modal interactivity. To address these, we propose a multi-modal fusion model that uses a Cross-Sequence Module to capture relationships between different sequences, while the interaction between the primary tumor and axillary lymph node regions of interest (ROIs) is achieved through a module we refer to as the Dual-ROI Dependency Module, in order to predict axillary lymph node metastasis. Experimental results demonstrate that this method achieves strong predictive performan

a0ec1fdabfa613cffb54c84c91110944e4dc1edd.title: PROZONESAM2: Prostate Zonal Segmentation Using Sam2 and Gland-To-Zones Consistency Constraints
a0ec1fdabfa613cffb54c84c91110944e4dc1edd.abstract: Accurate prostate zonal segmentation on MRI is crucial for prostate cancer (PCa) detection and treatment. Traditional CNN-based methods, though effective in single-center training, often lack global context awareness and generalize poorly to external datasets, especially in the peripheral zone (PZ) with fuzzy boundaries. Recently, foundation models like the Segment Anything Model (SAM) have shown strong segmentation ability, but domain gaps and limited medical annotations hinder their direct use in medical imaging. To address these challenges, we propose ProZoneSAM2, a region-constrained fine-tuning segmentation method built upon SAM2. a07bfde2716517f03c1fa32b4c8ce12d664fe2e5.title: Unsupervised Learning-Based Large Deformation Diffeomorphic Metric Mapping for Fast Image Registration
a07bfde2716517f03c1fa32b4c8ce12d664fe2e5.abstract: Diffeomorphic image registration is a fundamental tool in medical image processing that facilitates medical image analysis tasks as it preserves the image topology during the registration. In this work, we focused on the traditional large deformation diffeomorphic metric mapping (LDDMM) and proposed a time-varying velocity prediction model by utilizing fully convolutional networks (FCNs) for fast dif-feomorphic image registration. In contrast to prevailing unsupervised learning-based registration methodologies, the proposed approach incorporated the Laplacian operator of LDDMM into the framework of FCNs for parameter learning. The evaluation of the proposed method involved the utilization of two distinct T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (T1w MRI) datasets. Comparative analyses were conducted against two conventional diffeomorphic image registration algorithms and two state-of-the-a

a0643c6f39c01a180c1490bfdbbab894e6f6f972.title: SLIM-UAM - Semi-Supervised Learning In Medical Imaging: Uncertainty-Attention Model
a0643c6f39c01a180c1490bfdbbab894e6f6f972.abstract: Deep CNN/ViT supervised models for medical imaging typically require substantial amounts of high-quality labeled data, which can be challenging in resource-poor settings. This paper proposes a novel attention-integrated uncertainty-aware semi-supervised framework for medical image segmentation. By implementing the mean-teacher model, a knowledge distillation technique, our framework leverages unlabeled data by encouraging consistent predictions under various perturbations. Enhanced with an attention mechanism, our model (SLIM-UAM) significantly improves segmentation performance tested on two datasets (Left Atrium Segmentation Dataset and Medical Segmentation Decathlon - Spleen Dataset). It not only outperforms SOTA semi-supervised methods but provides performance similar to SOTA supervised model trained using 4x more labeled data. a01980e536631bf315a4c241c1bbb881d09e0529.title: SwinDiff_ConSeg: Automatic Segmentation of Ureters in Consecutive CT Urography Based on Swin Transformer and Diffusion Model
a01980e536631bf315a4c241c1bbb881d09e0529.abstract: CT urography (CTU) is a widely utilized imaging technique for comprehensively examining the entire urinary system to diagnose causes of blood in the urine, known as hematuria. However, the assessment can be time-consuming as the urinary tract spans the entirety of the abdomen and pelvis and components of the urinary tract are often difficult to visualize. In particular, the ureters are very small and identifying a stone or tumor within the ureters often proves difficult for radiologists. To aid in the detection of pathology, we propose a method for segmenting the ureters. Our novel method uses consecutive slices in CTU examinations. This approach leverages both the Swin Transformer and the Diffusion Model. 9fdb22d9938330b064874e568bee92af32d99835.title: Multi-Modal Integration for Predicting Biochemical Recurrence in Prostate Cancer
9fdb22d9938330b064874e568bee92af32d99835.abstract: Predicting biochemical recurrence (BCR) is crucial for Prostate Cancer (PCa) treatment plan. We present a novel multi-modal approach using deep learning framework that integrates Whole Slide Images (WSI) with associated clinical text to improve BCR prediction. Our model leverages contrastive learning approach where both visual and textual data are used to effectively capture the interplay between histopathology features and textual information by jointly modeling these data sources. Evaluation results indicate that our model building approach is able to effectively integrates spatial insights from WSIs and clinical texts, leading in enhanced BCR prediction performance compared to other existing methodologies and individual modalities. This approach has the potential to advance precision medicine in PCa care.

9fb88c216510672a7edb8b9d506a097d0a64799c.title: Identifying Optimal nnU-Net Configuration for Cerebral Microbleed Segmentation
9fb88c216510672a7edb8b9d506a097d0a64799c.abstract: The nnU-Net has become the de facto standard in medical image segmentation. While the generalizability of nnUNet has widely been studied across various domains, we question the optimality of the automated nnU-Net configuration specifically for cerebral microbleed (CMB) segmentation. We identified that the standard nnU-Net setup, particularly the recommended input patch size, is primarily optimized for the heterogeneous nature of multi-organ segmentation, resulting in suboptimal performance for CMB segmentation. To address this limitation, we propose a patch selection algorithm based on a local minima search that fully leverages the imaging characteristics of CMB lesions. Experiments on two independent cohorts demonstrate that our approach improves the overall performance without altering the segmentation backbone, highlighting the important role of preprocessing. 9f2acc0de0384b64cd5bd85c42ebb3e5c28a23db.title: Locating Standard Planes in Endometrium Ultrasound Videos via Clinical Prior Knowledge of Key Anatomical Structures
9f2acc0de0384b64cd5bd85c42ebb3e5c28a23db.abstract: Accurate localization of standard planes is crucial for sonog-raphers diagnosing and evaluating endometrial function from ultrasound videos. Traditionally, this process is performed manually, resulting in significant inter- and intra-observer variability. To address these challenges and enhance diagnos-tic consistency, we propose an automated model that localizes endometrial standard planes by detecting key anatomical structures. Specifically, our model segments the endometrium and identifies uterine cavity lines, facilitating standard plane localization based on clinical prior knowledge. Experimen-tal results demonstrate that our model outperforms existing methods, achieving an AUC of 0.922 and an accuracy of 0.869. The model's predictions provide consistent and in-terpretable results, supporting sonographers in their assessments.

9f1741a9f6f242fa35d9d6eb915f5d4331051789.title: Phase-Aware Vision Transformers Enable Prediction of Hepatocellular Carcinoma Recurrence After Liver Transplantation
9f1741a9f6f242fa35d9d6eb915f5d4331051789.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) recurrence after liver transplantation remains a critical clinical challenge, yet current prediction frameworks based on morphology and serum biomarkers incompletely capture the high-dimensional features encoded in post-contrast MRI. We propose a phase-aware selfsupervised learning framework that leverages Swin Vision Transformers to learn multiphase MRI representations through a joint reconstruction and phase discrimination objective, producing anatomically and temporally informed embeddings. These embeddings are combined with clinical covariates within a Tabular Prior-Fitted Network classifier to predict post-transplant recurrence under a fully nested cross-validation design. 9ee428499c3218085b1f302a846793607f29ea42.title: The Retinal-Glycemic Link: Using Retinal Imaging to Explore Glycemic Variability
9ee428499c3218085b1f302a846793607f29ea42.abstract: Retinal vasculature provides insight into systemic body health. In this work, we characterize and illustrate the potential for early detection of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) using optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) images. Using the AI-READI cohort ($\mathrm{N}=1062$), we extract vascular metrics from OCTA images and correlate them with diabetic state (based on hemoglobin $\mathrm{A} 1 \mathrm{c}, \text{HbA} 1 \mathrm{c}$) as well as continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) variables. Our results show that OCTA features of foveal avascular zone area, roundness of vessels, and degree of branching are most highly-correlated with HbA 1 c and CGM variables. 9eb8c6ce8abbd60ec242326996de3a59896329a4.title: Monocular Depth Estimation with Guided Edge-Aware Attention for Endoscopic Images
9eb8c6ce8abbd60ec242326996de3a59896329a4.abstract: In endoscopic imaging, monocular depth estimation (MDE) is crucial for enhancing 3D scene understanding, tissue assessment, and improving diagnostic and surgical precision. However, depth estimation around edges remains a challenge, as standard regression approaches often produce overly smooth predictions and blurred discontinuities. To address this, we propose a framework that integrates edge-aware supervision with a guidance-driven decoder to achieve precise edge preservation and structure-consistent depth reconstruction. First, we introduce EdgeAttenLoss, an edge-aware loss that employs attention maps to emphasise edge regions during training, enhancing boundary precision. Second, a lightweight Guidance Map Extractor encodes the RGB input into spatially rich features that provide structural cues for decoding. 9db0ba5a40e0d8c6a62b362b51da02a251f3ee3b.title: Rethinking 3D Small Object Segmentation: Comparative Insights Between nnU-Net and Transformers
9db0ba5a40e0d8c6a62b362b51da02a251f3ee3b.abstract: Transformers have shown strong potential in medical image segmentation, particularly as foundation models. However, comparative studies indicate that nnU-Net, a CNN-based framework, often outperforms transformer-based models. This study investigates why nnU-Net achieves superior performance, focusing on small object segmentation in CT scans and examining the role of transformers in developing foundation models for medical image segmentation. Six transformer-based and two CNN-based methods were trained in the MONAI framework using identical data augmentations and training settings. nnU-Net employed its self-configuration strategy to automatically determine optimal parameters. 9d6f7907d81e1e40c083f6ba2282f712dcd43d06.title: Positional Segmentor-Guided Counterfactual Fine-Tuning for Spatially Localized Image Synthesis
9d6f7907d81e1e40c083f6ba2282f712dcd43d06.abstract: Counterfactual image generation enables controlled data augmentation, bias mitigation, and disease modeling. However, existing methods guided by external classifiers or regressors are limited to subject-level factors (e.g., age) and fail to produce localized structural changes, often resulting in global artifacts. Pixel-level guidance using segmentation masks has been explored but requires user-defined counterfactual masks, which is tedious and impractical. Segmentor-guided Counterfactual Fine-Tuning (Seg-CFT) addressed this by using segmentation-derived measurements to supervise structurespecific variables, yet it remains restricted to global interventions. We propose Positional Seg-CFT, which subdivides each structure into regional segments and derives independent measurements per region, enabling spatially localized and anatomically coherent counterfactuals.
