9c6e387054e9e9bc5fa89af729f470d49bb427af.title: Comparative Evaluation of Five Hippocampal Segmentation Algorithms in Limbic Encephalitis: Addressing Inflammation and Atrophy Challenges
9c6e387054e9e9bc5fa89af729f470d49bb427af.abstract: Limbic encephalitis (LE) mainly affects the hippocampus, where inflammation and atrophy can complicate MRI volumetry methods. While manual segmentation is the gold standard, it is laborious and subjective, motivating automated alternatives. We evaluated five hippocampal segmentation methods-FreeSurfer, FastSurfer, SPM, JointLabelFusion, and nnU-Net-on 187 MRIs from 65 CASPR2LE patients and 191 MRIs from 64 matched controls. Expert manual segmentations served as reference, with performance assessed across accuracy and robustness metrics. FreeSurfer proved the most reliable, accurately capturing disease-related trajectories, whereas other tools were limited by crashes, training data, or anatomical variability.

9adc49eaed89ab2d8add8d127d9d2fcb0c3650ed.title: Multi-Modal Domain Adaptation for Cancer Diagnosis via Integration of Pathological Images and Clinical Text Data
9adc49eaed89ab2d8add8d127d9d2fcb0c3650ed.abstract: Whole-slide pathological images (WSIs) have long been regarded as the gold standard for cancer diagnosis and treatment planning. Recent research shows that the integrative analysis of WSIs with their corresponding pathological reports can significantly enhance diagnostic accuracy, as it leverages complementary visual-textual cues. However, data from different centers often have notable distribution shifts that hinder model adaptation across different sites. To solve this problem, we propose $\mathrm{M}^{2} \text{DA}$-ICT (Multi-modal Domain Adaptation via Integration of Pathological Images and Clinical Texts), a new framework for enhancing cross-center cancer diagnosis. Specifically, for the pathological images, we introduce a graph-based topology alignment module, which represents each WSI as a patch-level graph and aligns domain distributions using Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) on bot

99d564466384ed4fcff97ad4c3ab8b6f4c75dff7.title: VITG-VS: Preserving Spatial Heterogeneity in Virtual Staining of Renal Autofluorescence Images
99d564466384ed4fcff97ad4c3ab8b6f4c75dff7.abstract: Label-free imaging technique integrated with virtual staining has rapidly advanced in the field of renal pathology. However, most existing convolutional neural network (CNN) based virtual staining methods encounter difficulties in preserving spatial heterogeneity, especially in images characterized by complex tissue variability. To achieve better results in auto-fluorescence virtual staining tasks, we introduce a novel transformer-based generative adversarial network named ViTG-VS. This method integrates the global perceptual advantages of the transformer architecture with convolutional operations that capture local information. Furthermore, we incorporate a content-aware positional encoding to capture the spatial variations of morphological information distribution. Quantitative and qualitative results indicate that ViTG-VS performs well in the virtual staining of renal pathology. The s

99bb3e9f7fac1b4f270a479aee27c2782059e93a.title: Channel-Agnostic vs. Channel-Adaptive: Foundation Model Strategies for Spatial Proteomics
99bb3e9f7fac1b4f270a479aee27c2782059e93a.abstract: Spatial proteomics via multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) requires vision foundation models capable of handling variable channel composition and leveraging tissue structure information. Using DINOv2 framework, we trained and benchmarked channel-agnostic (standard ViT-s/14) and channel-adaptive (KRONOS-style ViT-s/14 with marker embeddings) architectures, on a large mIF dataset of 14,946 slides (48,993 single-marker images), 45 markers, and diverse tissue and disease types. Including the autofluorescence (AF) channel enabled channel-agnostic models to achieve consistently high linear probing F1-scores (BCL-2: $0.76, \text{HBsAg}: 0.69, \text{HBcAg}: 0.71$), compared to channel-adaptive (BCL-2: $0.61, \text{HBsAg}: 0.52, \text{HBcAg}$: 0.69) and reference models trained on H&E (UNI) or natural images (DINOv2). Channel-adaptive model performance fluctuated between tests (HBsAg (SD): 0.21),

99893ca28173162fb91e5ccdc328c4b7b253bf88.title: TAR-Diff: Diffusion-Based Ultrasound Video Generation for Medical Diagnosis with Temporal Attention Residuals
99893ca28173162fb91e5ccdc328c4b7b253bf88.abstract: Deep learning methods have demonstrated remarkable potential in analyzing breast ultrasound images, offering advantages in clinical efficiency. However, while dynamic lesion changes are key for diagnosis, large-scale annotated video datasets are scarce, limiting the performance and generalization of vision-based models. We propose a diffusion-based framework that synthesizes realistic breast ultrasound videos while capturing temporal changes relevant to diagnosis. Through the integration of multi-scale conditioning and temporal attention residual layers, the model effectively learns to focus on relevant spatiotemporal features, improving the generation of coherent and clinically useful ultrasound video sequences. Extensive results on the BUSI and BUSV datasets are presented, evaluating the generated videos through qualitative and quantitative analyses as well as across downstream tasks i

9959feb7adb9bf171b275181eccdeac10a14a062.title: Contrastive Meta-Domain Adaptation for Robust Skin Lesion Classification Across Clinical and Acquisition Conditions
9959feb7adb9bf171b275181eccdeac10a14a062.abstract: Deep learning models for dermatological image analysis remain sensitive to acquisition variability and domain-specific visual characteristics, leading to performance degradation when deployed in clinical settings. We investigate how visual artifacts and domain shifts affect deep learning-based skin lesion classification. We propose an adaptation strategy, grounded in the idea of visual meta-domains, that transfers visual representations from larger dermoscopic datasets into clinical image domains, thereby improving generalization robustness. Experiments across multiple dermatology datasets show consistent gains in classification performance and reduced gaps between dermoscopic and clinical images. These results emphasize the importance of domain-aware training for deployable systems.

992050f89265d323303f6f4d6d3d4c81c82a4db5.title: Uncertainty Quantification for Multimodal Generation in Cancer Ai
992050f89265d323303f6f4d6d3d4c81c82a4db5.abstract: Transcriptomic data offer valuable insights for cancer diagnosis and prognosis, but high cost limits their routine use. Recent studies have shown that transcriptomic profiles can be efficiently synthesized from digital histopathology images. However, they are of little practical use unless the reliability of such black-box predictions is rigorously evaluated. In this work, we propose a novel conformal prediction based methodology to quantify and calibrate generative uncertainty. Experimental results on publicly available multimodal datasets, The Cancer Genomic Atlas (TCGA), Clinical Proteomic Tumor Analysis Consortium (CPTAC) and STImage, spanning independent cancer cohorts of glioma-glioblastoma, renal, and breast show that our conformal-based methodology not only efficiently estimates uncertainty bounds to guarantee a desired ground truth coverage but also calibrates the model to be fa

98c3f981202d33e61127125299803f0043fc8b37.title: Classification of Surgeons' Gender from Videos of the Surgical Field
98c3f981202d33e61127125299803f0043fc8b37.abstract: We present a novel approach to classify the gender of the operating surgeon in videos from the microscope (that show only the surgical field) using the SurgGender model and a step-based analysis technique. This method addresses both technical and ethical challenges of implicit gender biases, which impact training and career progression. By focusing on gender classification, our work aims to support equitable, context-aware surgical systems. The SurgGender leverages 3D shifted window-based self-attention to capture key spatialtemporal patterns. Our step-based approach enhances classification by isolating relevant video segments and reducing non-informative noise. Rigorous testing demonstrates that this method improves accuracy and processing efficiency, establishing a foundation for bias-aware surgical video analysis.

976312ecd3afc05997b73b5cee0ad30528124927.title: External Spatial Adapter Tuning: Memory-Efficient Adaptation of Foundation Model for Sddh Diagnosis with Ultrasound Images
976312ecd3afc05997b73b5cee0ad30528124927.abstract: Ultrasound-based computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) has indicated effectiveness for developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH). Recently, foundation models have shown promising potential to further improve the performance of a CAD model. However, their deployment in clinical applications remains challenging due to the high computational cost and overfitting risk of full fine-tuning. To address this issue, a new memory-efficient adaptation framework, named External Spatial Adapter Tuning (ESAT), is proposed for the CAD of DDH. The ESAT develops spatial adapters based on lowrank depthwise separable convolution at each layer of foundation model, so as to extract and refine hierarchical spatial features. These adapter outputs are further fused externally for the classification task, so that the gradient flow is fully decoupled from the foundation model. In real-world DDH diagnosis experiments, the

9758876d6cd3ad621eaa06f9808a1311c3ceb9ed.title: PAT-DIFF: Pathology-Aware Residual Diffusion Framework for MRI-to-PET Translation in Alzheimer's Disease
9758876d6cd3ad621eaa06f9808a1311c3ceb9ed.abstract: Positron Emission Tomography (PET) and Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) provide complementary information for Alzheimer's disease (AD) diagnosis, but acquiring both is often impractical owing to the high cost and radiation exposure associated with PET. To bridge these complementary domains, we propose PaT-Diff, a pathology-aware residual diffusion framework that translates MRI into PET representations in a clinically interpretable and biomarker-consistent manner. The model learns AD-related residual representations that bridge the anatomical MRI and pathological PET domains while integrating demographic attributes via CLIP-based clinical conditioning. To further emphasize amyloid-relevant regions associated with AD pathology, a pathology-weighted reconstruction loss combines pixel-level and pathology-region-weighted objectives. Experiments on paired MRI-PET scans from the ADNI dataset de

9702acbcfa67ab1b9b28309207b4dc99b3219cbc.title: Benchmarking Lesion-Level Response Assessment of Metastatic Bone Disease on WB-MRI Using Manual, Interactive and Automated Segmentation Methods
9702acbcfa67ab1b9b28309207b4dc99b3219cbc.abstract: Reliable application of response criteria on whole-body MRI (WB-MRI) requires lesion measurements with variability sufficiently small to remain within clinically meaningful decision thresholds. Although manual approaches are established in clinical research, comparative evidence against novel deep learning pipelines remains limited. In a cohort of 40 advanced prostate cancer patients, we benchmarked three pipelines for per-lesion response assessment in skeletal metastases: manual Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (RECIST) diameters, semi-automated segmentation (nnInteractive), and fully automated segmentation with an end-to-end deep learning model. We quantified per-lesion agreement with reference delineations and method reproducibility, then measured each method's decision-band detectability, i.e., its ability to detect true changes that exceed pre-specified clinical decision

96e1d41fe704e354290e9e344f42a387faca6f6f.title: Diffusion-Driven 3D CECT-to-NCECT Conversion for Head and Neck Imaging
96e1d41fe704e354290e9e344f42a387faca6f6f.abstract: Many medical applications, such as proton therapy and radiotherapy planning, require both Contrast Enhanced CT (CECT) for tumor and organ delineation and Non-Contrast Enhanced CT (NCECT) for accurate radiation dose calculation. The need for both scans can introduce dosimetric uncertainties due to tissue motion, particularly in thoracic and abdominal tumors. This study presents a diffusion model-based deep learning framework to generate NCECT directly from CECT, offering a solution that reduces the need for the NCECT scan and minimizes motion-related uncertainties. We trained and evaluated the diffusion model using 6400 2D CT slices from abdominal CECT and NCECT image pairs from 25 patients. The model's performance was evaluated using structural similarity index measure (SSIM), Mean Square Error (MSE), and qualitative visual assessments, focusing on the accuracy of NCECT image generation.

96dbb93ae97936e0b5cd6df21bf21c2ab19c169e.title: Multi-View Consistent Wound Segmentation with Neural Fields
96dbb93ae97936e0b5cd6df21bf21c2ab19c169e.abstract: Wound care is often challenged by the economic and logistical burdens that consistently afflict patients and hospitals worldwide. In recent decades, healthcare professionals have sought support from computer vision and machine learning algorithms. In particular, wound segmentation has gained interest due to its ability to provide professionals with fast, automatic tissue assessment from standard RGB images. Some approaches have extended segmentation to 3D, enabling more complete and precise healing progress tracking. However, inferring multi-view consistent 3D structures from 2D images remains a challenge. In this paper, we evaluate WoundNeRF, a NeRF SDF-based method for estimating robust wound segmentations from automatically generated annotations. We demonstrate the potential of this paradigm in recovering accurate segmentations by comparing it against state-of-the-art Vision Transform

96c41fe474d8ab36dcda2688e75114632f09888a.title: Modeling Structure-Function Discordance in Glaucoma Visual Field Analysis
96c41fe474d8ab36dcda2688e75114632f09888a.abstract: The Humphrey Visual Field (HVF) test is essential for assessing functional vision loss in glaucoma, but artifacts and patient variability can reduce test reliability. This work models and aims to predict two types of structure-function discordance between HVF sensitivity and retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness from optical coherence tomography (OCT): (i) functional loss with normal structure (FLD) and (ii) structural loss with normal function (SLD). Groundtruth labels were derived by combining HVF pattern deviations with OCT RNFL classifications, while predictions relied solely on HVF data. We evaluated three methods: (i) neighbor-based rules, (ii) zone-majority classification, and (iii) a lightweight convolutional neural architecture with dual outputs each specialized for FLD or SLD. The CNN outperformed rule-based baselines, demonstrating that HVF-based models can predict struct

96255f33d38d621771c1d84162a328046bf77f1f.title: AutoATQ: Automating Along-Tract Quantification Without Tractography
96255f33d38d621771c1d84162a328046bf77f1f.abstract: Diffusion MRI (dMRI) is a unique noninvasive technique for characterizing brain white-matter microstructure, and tractometry is a key analytical method for identifying localized abnormalities. However, traditional tractometry relies on tractography, which has significant limitations, including indirect inference of anatomy, false-positive streamlines, and difficulties with crossing fibers. Additionally, it requires a lengthy acquisition of $q$-space data. To this end, we propose a novel deep learning framework for direct microstructural characterization using white matter bundle masks, thereby eliminating the need for tractography. Our approach uses the U-Mamba network to accurately segment 72 predefined white matter bundles from parameterized spherical mean images, thereby enhancing tissue specificity. We also introduce a dedicated point cloud network to estimate the centerline of each

961bc08029a6521951855417065e2322e385f570.title: A Multi-Scale Linear-Time Encoder for Whole-Slide Image Analysis
961bc08029a6521951855417065e2322e385f570.abstract: We introduce Multi-scale Adaptive Recurrent Biomedical Linear-time Encoder (MARBLE), the first purely Mamba-based multi-state multiple instance learning (MIL) framework for whole-slide image (WSI) analysis. MARBLE processes multiple magnification levels in parallel and integrates coarse-to-fine reasoning within a linear-time state-space model, efficiently capturing cross-scale dependencies with minimal parameter overhead. WSI analysis remains challenging due to gigapixel resolutions and hierarchical magnifications, while existing MIL methods typically operate at a single scale and transformer-based approaches suffer from quadratic attention costs. By coupling parallel multi-scale processing with linear-time sequence modeling, MARBLE provides a scalable and modular alternative to attention-based architectures. Experiments on five public datasets show improvements of up to $\mathbf{6. 9 \%

9602ec3d3f2d671180e47751191ebeece936c2f8.title: ACE-Net: 3D VFM-CNN Fusion with Adaptive Covariance Eigen-Gate for Coronary Artery Segmentation
9602ec3d3f2d671180e47751191ebeece936c2f8.abstract: Accurate segmentation of coronary arteries from CT angiography is crucial for quantitative stenosis evaluation and surgical planning. This task requires models to capture both global anatomical context and fine-grained local details. While 3D Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) and CNNs are naturally suited for these complementary roles, effectively fusing their heterogeneous feature streams remains a major challenge. To address this, we propose ACE-Net, a unified framework built upon a parallel dual-encoder architecture that couples a 3D foundation model-driven encoder (finetuned from SAM-Med3D) for global structural encoding with a 3D U-Net-based shape encoder for fine-grained local representation. To bridge the feature heterogeneity between the two streams, ACE-Net incorporates the Adaptive Covariance Eigen-Gate (ACE-Gate), which explicitly models interchannel dependencies via covariance

959a2879cc33cd2e3a732187d96913e1364c4307.title: BrainOrg-QC: Automated Morphological Quality Control of Cerebral Organoids
959a2879cc33cd2e3a732187d96913e1364c4307.abstract: Cerebral organoids are three-dimensional (3D) self-organized cellular structures that recapitulate key aspects of human brain development. They have become promising models in neuroscience research, particularly for modeling neurological diseases and evaluating neurotoxicity. However, they exhibit substantial heterogeneity, notably in morphology and size, which hampers their reproducibility and scalability. Critically, current organoid characterization methods lack standardization, limiting their broader applicability. Here, we present an automated quality control (QC) framework for 60-day cortical organoids that integrates non-invasive imagebased assessment of morphology and growth. Our deep learning method combines organoid segmentation for quantitative growth profiling with a ConvNeXt-based multi-head ordinal regression (CORAL) network that predicts QC scores for three key morphologic

94990a14c40e0b96103091b4a04b6c49a438444a.title: How to Evaluate Generated skVCT from MVCT? Optimal Parameters and Clinical Validation
94990a14c40e0b96103091b4a04b6c49a438444a.abstract: This study investigates the correlation of computer vision metrics with the clinical utility of domain-transferred synthetic medical images. Here, we use a Cycle-Consistency Generative Adversarial Network using softly paired data to create synthetic kilovoltage computed tomography (CT) from megavoltage computed tomography images, leveraging a unique database of 1109 head-and-neck CTs, an order of magnitude larger than previous works. The quality of synthetic images was quantified using standard metrics such as Structural Similarity, which we used to identify the best models in the clinical context of adaptative radiation therapy. Using the framework defined here, we identify the optimal parameter values of widely used metrics and validate our findings through a clinical evaluation using a panel of nine radiation oncologists who evaluated 4320 images.

93cb40094fa91b78663f1313ade2202d4b2bb078.title: Semi-Supervised Fetal Echocardiography Segmentation and CHD Classification
93cb40094fa91b78663f1313ade2202d4b2bb078.abstract: Automated analysis of fetal cardiac ultrasound requires simultaneous segmentation of anatomical structures and classification of congenital heart disease (CHD), yet expert annotation is scarce in clinical practice. We present a semisupervised dual-task framework that jointly optimizes pixel-level segmentation of 14 cardiac structures (plus background) and multi-label CHD classification across 7 pathological categories from four standard cardiac imaging planes. The framework builds on a shared DINOv2 ViT-B/14 backbone with partial fine-tuning, where the lower six transformer blocks are frozen to preserve generic visual representations while the upper six are fully updated for cardiac domain adaptation. A dual-bottleneck design isolates the segmentation and classification gradient flows, preventing destructive task interference. Semi-supervised training follows a UniMatch-style paradigm wi

9385709dfff82ca116145d1993e57da1658a1ef4.title: Poseidon: Portable Ocular Surface Evaluation with Integrated Design of Hardware and Network
9385709dfff82ca116145d1993e57da1658a1ef4.abstract: This work presents POSEIDON, a portable ocular surface evaluation system built on a hardware-software co-design paradigm for real-time, quantitative assessment of ocular surface diseases. The system integrates dual-modality imaging into an end-to-end pipeline, with a lightweight network for meibomian gland delineation on edge devices with limited power and memory. By unifying imaging, computation, and clinical interpretation in a compact system, POSEIDON establishes a scalable route toward intelligent ocular surface disease analysis and democratized eye-health monitoring.

93446c004e04c16f245dbb9209b927596ce49240.title: ST-SAM: A Spatio-Temporal Enhanced Segment Anything Model for Echocardiogram Video Segmentation
93446c004e04c16f245dbb9209b927596ce49240.abstract: Echocardiogram video segmentation is crucial for enabling rapid, objective, and reproducible quantification of cardiac structures, which is the key for the diagnosis and treatment of cardiovascular diseases. Although recent SAM-based methods have achieved promising results, they often struggle to effectively capture spatio-temporal features in echocardiogram videos, resulting in limited performance for multi-structure segmentation. To this end, we propose the Spatio-Temporal Segment Anything Model (ST-SAM)—a novel framework comprising a Spatial Topology Module (STM) and a Temporal Graph Enhanced Module (TGEM) that jointly enhance spatial topological relationships and temporal consistency in echocardiogram videos. Experimental results demonstrate that ST-SAM outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods by an average of 3.0% Dice across four-chamber segmentation tasks. The source code can

9252790c9e712c619e32e7bf22caeaef6cab6736.title: Decoupling Multi-Contrast Super-Resolution: Pairing Unpaired Synthesis with Implicit Representations
9252790c9e712c619e32e7bf22caeaef6cab6736.abstract: Multi-Contrast Super-Resolution (MCSR) for Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is often hindered by the need for large, perfectly paired, and fixed-scale training datasets, limiting clinical applicability. To overcome these challenges, we propose a modular MCSR framework that eliminates these requirements. Our method decouples the task into two stages: (1) an unpaired cross-modal synthesis (U-CMS) module translates a high-resolution (HR) reference image into the target contrast, and (2) an unsupervised super-resolution (USR) module, based on implicit neural representations (INRs), reconstructs the final image at an arbitrary scale. This design fuses population-level knowledge from unpaired synthesis with subject-specific details from the low-resolution (LR) input. Experiments on 4× and 8× upscaling demonstrate superior performance and anatomical fidelity over existing baselines, highlightin

924593ed0b42a092e2fcf8d3f74150d3fb506d75.title: Reconstruct Dense Live-Cell Microscopy Images via Learning Continuous Fluorescence Field
924593ed0b42a092e2fcf8d3f74150d3fb506d75.abstract: Live-cell imaging plays an increasingly important role in developmental biology and drug discovery. The phototoxity of laser light, however, inevitably induces a tradeoff between image quality and cell viability. While learning-based denoising models have been proposed for improving noisy low-quality images, it is practically challenging to obtain high-quality training reference in live-cell imaging. In this work, we present a reference-free framework MicroNeRF for reconstructing dense image stack from sparse slices. By formalizing the fluorescence field as an implicit neural representation, high-quality stack can be posteriorly sampled from continuous manifold. Additionally, we address the interference among fluorescent signals through an adaptive learnable point spread function. Experimental results demonstrate the superiority of MicroNeRF in sparse reconstruction and downstream segmen

91732a0b312b62fca6a7b64e6508edb5b69d5b55.title: Explainable Brain Tumor Detection with Eye Fixation Density Map Alignment
91732a0b312b62fca6a7b64e6508edb5b69d5b55.abstract: Deep learning-based object detectors have demonstrated strong performance in localizing brain tumors on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). However, clinical adoption requires not only accurate predictions but also trustworthy explanations that align with expert reasoning. Saliency-based explainable AI (XAI) methods visualize where a model focuses its attention. Despite this, their alignment with expert visual attention and robustness to benign image variations remains insufficiently studied in neuroimaging. To address this gap, we propose a gaze-informed evaluation framework that quantitatively assesses the interpretability of a highperforming explainable AI model using expert eye-tracking data. Our Method compares saliency maps from two state-of-the-art object detectors against expert eye-tracking fixation density maps (ETFDs) collected from experienced neurosurgeons. We employ two compl

9040fa17bea6c694e11f1eb0cd9ff0e7e7cc8d82.title: Clinically Grounded Radiology Report Generation via Explanation-Guided Policy Optimization
9040fa17bea6c694e11f1eb0cd9ff0e7e7cc8d82.abstract: Radiology report generation requires models that are both linguistically fluent and clinically grounded. While recent Medical Vision-Language Models (Med-VLMs) have shown promise, they often suffer from hallucinations and factual misalignment with medical images. Existing preference optimization methods improve fluency but overlook clinical relevance, leading to shallow lexical learning. To address this, we propose a Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) framework guided by the GREEN (Generative Radiology Evaluation and Error Notation) score a chest X ray report specific, fine-grained reward metric. By employing tokenlevel GREEN score-based rewards, our approach captures clinical semantics and entity fidelity, resulting in reports that are both factually consistent and clinically trustworthy.

900088998a40b933f7097c746633b21d1edded5f.title: Enhanced Diagnostic Performance Via Large-Resolution Inference Optimization for Pathology Foundation Models
900088998a40b933f7097c746633b21d1edded5f.abstract: Despite their prominent performance on tasks such as ROI classification and segmentation, many pathology foundation models remain constrained by a specific input size e.g. $224 \times 224$, creating substantial inefficiencies when applied to whole-slide images (WSIs), which span thousands of resolutions. A naïve strategy is to either enlarge inputs or downsample the WSIs. However, enlarging inputs results in prohibitive GPU memory consumption, while downsampling alters the microns-per-pixel resolution and obscures critical morphological details. To overcome these limitations, we propose an space- and time- efficient inference strategy that sparsifies attention using spatially aware neighboring blocks and filters out non-informative tokens through global attention scores. This design substantially reduces GPU memory and runtime during high-resolution WSI inference while preserving and eve

8fe06c0ce3bc987a03b98460a8e455e61ef9df41.title: Open-Set Semi-Supervised Learning for Long-Tailed Medical Datasets
8fe06c0ce3bc987a03b98460a8e455e61ef9df41.abstract: Many practical medical imaging scenarios include categories that are under-represented but still crucial. The relevance of image recognition models to real-world applications lies in their ability to generalize to these rare classes as well as unseen classes. Real-world generalization requires taking into account the various complexities that can be encountered in the real-world. First, training data is highly imbalanced, which may lead to model exhibiting bias toward the more frequently represented classes. Moreover, real-world data may contain unseen classes that need to be identified, and model performance is affected by the data scarcity. While medical image recognition has been extensively addressed in the literature, current methods do not take into account all the intricacies in the real-world scenarios. To this end, we propose an open-set learning method for highly imbal-anced me

8fd2e893c03a9a233401bb806803c9a3e82d81ef.title: Sequential Spatial-Temporal Network for Interpretable Automatic Ultrasonic Assessment of Fetal Head During Labor
8fd2e893c03a9a233401bb806803c9a3e82d81ef.abstract: The intrapartum ultrasound guideline established by ISUOG highlights the Angle of Progression (AoP) and Head Symphysis Distance (HSD) as pivotal metrics for assessing fetal head descent and predicting delivery outcomes. Accurate measurement of the AoP and HSD requires a structured process. This begins with identifying standardized ultrasound planes, followed by the detection of specific anatomical landmarks within the regions of the pubic symphysis and fetal head that correlate with the delivery parameters AoP and HSD. Finally, these measurements are derived based on the identified anatomical landmarks. Addressing the clinical demands and standard operation process outlined in the ISUOG guideline, we introduce the Sequential Spatial-Temporal Network (SSTN), the first interpretable model specifically designed for the video of intrapartum ultrasound analysis. The SSTN operates by first ide

8f8953700f938cbbbf7cd283ce7d41e31183d20e.title: Deep Learning for Cardiac TMP Imaging: A Physics-Informed Data Augmentation Approach
8f8953700f938cbbbf7cd283ce7d41e31183d20e.abstract: The noninvasive imaging of myocardial transmembrane potential (TMP) from body surface potentials (BSP) holds clinical promise but is a challenging ill-posed inverse problem. Although deep learning (DL) has shown potential, its application is constrained by two issues: the lack of extensive, high-fidelity training datasets and the tendency of unconstrained models to yield physiologically unrealistic outcomes. This paper introduces a novel end-to-end DL framework designed to overcome these obstacles. Our approach is built upon a simulation-driven data generation technique. We employ the Aliev-Panfilov (AP) model, a computationally efficient model for cardiac excitation dynamics, guided by a structured sampling of initial pacing conditions, to synthesize a diverse training corpus. Subsequently, a convolutional neural network is trained by minimizing a composite loss function. This objective

8f6546fdb088cdc2a23ede59ae08405e90aa1921.title: Improving Fairness in Vision Language Models for Medical Applications via Max Deviation Penalty
8f6546fdb088cdc2a23ede59ae08405e90aa1921.abstract: Fairness in medical artificial intelligence (AI) tools is essential, as biased model behaviour can lead to unequal diagnostic outcomes and raise serious ethical concerns, ultimately reducing clinical trust. Although Vision Language Models (VLMs) show strong performance in medical imaging, they still exhibit demographic biases, particularly across gender, race, and other sensitive attributes. Addressing these disparities is difficult due to the utility-fairness trade off, where improving equity often reduces diagnostic accuracy. To overcome these challenges, we propose the Max Deviation Penalty, a lightweight regularization objective that integrates seamlessly into parameter efficient finetuning schemes. Experiments across diverse medical and general domain benchmarks demonstrate that our method consistently achieves state of the art performance in balancing fairness and utility, surpassi

8f54bcef1536d51a3c113b6f24d73739b8b9d390.title: SACL: Semantics-Aware Contrastive Learning for One-Shot Medical Image Segmentation
8f54bcef1536d51a3c113b6f24d73739b8b9d390.abstract: One-shot medical image segmentation remains a challenging task due to the diversified anatomical structures and the presence of ambiguous surrounding tissues. While large pre-trained models have shown success in few-shot segmentation, they typically require extensive datasets for fine-tuning. Approaches such as synthetic pseudo-labeling and semi-supervised learning offer simpler, cost-effective solutions by learning from noisy annotations with consistency regularization. However, a significant challenge is the domain shift between homogenous synthetic data and more complex clinical data, which limits the generalizability of these models. In this paper, we propose a novel semantics-aware contrastive learning (SACL) method for one-shot medical image segmentation. SACL includes two key components: (1) semantic-aware image translation (SAIT), which addresses the domain shift between syntheti

8f1967ca68757b83cf11c0409594da5009a4a2d4.title: NEUSEG: INTERPRETABLE UNSUPERVISED GM/WM SEGMENTATION IN BRAIN HISTOPATHOLOGY USING NUCLEI MORPHOMETRICS
8f1967ca68757b83cf11c0409594da5009a4a2d4.abstract: We present NEUSEG, a fully automated, interpretable, and unsupervised pipeline for gray/white matter (GM/WM) segmentation in brain histopathology whole-slide images (WSIs). GM/WM segmentation in WSIs is challenging due to their gigapixel-scale resolution and substantial variability in staining, regional morphology, and underlying pathology. To address this, NEUSEG combines nuclei morphometrics with a two-component Gaussian Mixture Model and refines boundaries using a Conditional Random Field and morphological post-processing. In comparison with a supervised CNN baseline, NEUSEG achieved comparable accuracy on in-distribution slides and superior robustness under out-of-distribution conditions. Across 252 WSIs with expert-annotated regions of interest (ROIs), median annotation-to-contour distances were 32.89 μm for the GMBG boundary and 129.79 μm for the GM-WM boundary, with no significant

8f0190092844a6f4b209cf67f8cb7adf8fa19873.title: Bias Mitigation for Brain Age Prediction via Age Delta Correlation Loss
8f0190092844a6f4b209cf67f8cb7adf8fa19873.abstract: Deep regression models for brain age prediction derived from T1-weighted MRI are known to suffer from the regression-to-the-mean bias, leading to overestimation in younger individuals and underestimation in older ones. Although post-hoc linear calibration is commonly used to correct the bias, this two-step approach produces a problematic biomarker for Alzheimer's disease classification, as it results in a suboptimal model. To address this, we introduce $\mathcal{L}_{\text{ADC}}$, a loss term designed to penalize the Pearson correlation between the brain-age delta and chronological age, which we integrate end-to-end with the standard Mean Squared Error (MSE). The proposed training pipeline enables balanced control of the accuracy-bias trade-off during model training without depending on post-hoc adjustments alone. Across ResNet-18 and VQ-VAE backbones, our method consistently reduces the

8e74b578b8b39aa754a863b59bc19309eae02c9c.title: GP-CPS: Gradient Penalty Cross Pseudo Supervision for Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
8e74b578b8b39aa754a863b59bc19309eae02c9c.abstract: Medical imaging has always been constrained due to the challenges in the acquisition process, poor signal-to-noise ratios, high costs, and the complexity of medical image features. This work introduces a semi supervised framework called Gradient Penalty Cross Pseudo Supervision (GP-CPS), which is based on the Cross Pseudo Supervision (CPS) model and innovatively introduces the concept of gradient penalty, sig-nificantly enhancing the model's performance. To our knowledge, this is the first time the concept of gradient penalty has been applied in the field of image segmentation. Furthermore, this work introduces a concept of fused cross pseudo super-vision to enhance the diversity of training and strengthen the robustness of the model. Using the publicly accessible Kvasir-SEG dataset, the proposed model is compared with baselines and advanced models. Across all four groups with varying am

8e3eb016ff404a2d74364e8339ed4aeeacdd54e2.title: High-Fidelity 3D CT Super-Resolution on Real-Paired Datasets with Adaptive Interpolation and Feature Consistency
8e3eb016ff404a2d74364e8339ed4aeeacdd54e2.abstract: High-resolution thin-slice Computed Tomography (CT) imaging is critical for accurate diagnosis, yet clinical scans are often acquired with thick slices to reduce radiation dose and scanning time. This leads to anisotropic volumes that obscure fine anatomical details and hinder 3D analysis. While deep learning-based super-resolution (SR) methods have made progress in reconstructing high-resolution volumes from thick-slice inputs, they remain limited by challenges in slice generation, feature enhancement, and structural refinement. In this work, we present a unified framework that systematically addresses these three aspects. An adaptive slice interpolation module enables content-driven and positionaware generation of intermediate features for anatomically consistent upsampling. A frequency-enhanced throughplane attention block enriches multi-view representations by integrating spatial and

8e2fe057e2c84ef68b439516bdec787d522fb1e9.title: Toward Achieving Adjustable Smoothing Level in Cardiac-Gated SPECT Studies with a Deep Learning Denoising Network
8e2fe057e2c84ef68b439516bdec787d522fb1e9.abstract: Post-reconstruction filtering is essential for suppressing the elevated imaging noise in cardiac-gated SPECT acquisitions, where the smoothing level often needs to be adjusted to better accommodate inter-subject variability in acquired data statistics. In this study we investigate the feasibility of achieving an adjustable smoothing level by employing a pre-trained deep learning (DL) denoising network for processing cardiac-gated images, the purpose being to avoid the need to re-train the DL network when the desired smoothing level varies for a given patient. We evaluated the performance of this approach on a set of 30 clinical gated acquisitions using a DL network pre-trained from the ungated data of 862 studies. The results demonstrated that, in terms of the noise level in the reconstructed myocardium and the image resolution of the left ventricle, the proposed approach could achieve a

8e0a9808e34713b51ae1cdf46980a7d495c94829.title: Fully Unsupervised Deep Spectral Clustering for Retinal Vessel Segmentation
8e0a9808e34713b51ae1cdf46980a7d495c94829.abstract: Blood vessel segmentation plays a crucial role in the diagnosis and treatment of eye diseases. Fully supervised and semi-supervised deep learning-based methods require large, labeled datasets for their training. We propose a novel, fully unsupervised deep learning segmentation framework that implements the spectral clustering algorithm to address this issue. A deep neural network is used to learn the continuous Laplace-Beltrami partial differential operator of the images and solve its eigen decomposition in an end-to-end manner with a tai-lored loss function. The learned eigen decomposition spans the image space and is specifically tuned to the input image. Pixels are mapped to this space, and a k-means clustering algorithm produces the final segmentation results. We validated our method on the publicly available DRIVE and STARE reti-nal vessel datasets, demonstrating qualitative and qua

8d884ba8710d7d033e07f281f5b7ec770476201d.title: Optimal Transport with Foundation Models for Multi-Stain CBIR in Digital Pathology
8d884ba8710d7d033e07f281f5b7ec770476201d.abstract: Combining multiple staining in histopathology is vital to relate complementary information within a tissue. We present a novel framework that enables local correspondence in the form of patch retrieval (CBIR) in multi-stain whole-slide images without the need for explicit registration. By leveraging foundation models as meaningful patch encoders, we are able to retrieve an H&E patch in a dataset of patches extracted from IHC slides. Using Fused Gromov-Wasserstein optimal transport for weak supervision, we learn a lightweight correction module that aligns embeddings and improves retrieval accuracy by up to 30% (depending on patch size and model), at negligible cost, despite staining and structural variations. Our method paves the way for efficient multi-stain integration in digital pathology workflows.

8d51108489922742d73d8329b2ffaf4119d50a5c.title: Towards ROI-Free Modality Translation for MRI with Test-Time Augmentation
8d51108489922742d73d8329b2ffaf4119d50a5c.abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) equips medical professions with comprehensive information to examine various regions of interest (ROI). Nevertheless, the acquisition of a sufficient amount of MRI modalities can be arduous due to limitations such as financial constraints or disabilities of the patient. Recently, researchers have suggested image-to-image translation between MRI modalities utilizing generative models. However, these models still suffer from the disparity between the data quantities of different ROI. In this research, we propose MRI Translation Test-Time Augmentation (MRI-TA), an original method that utilizes the modality representation of a ROI with sufficient data to augment the model for another ROI with lacking data during test time. We perform experiments using T1 and T2 modalities from BraTS2024, GTU and Mendeley Lumber datasets and show promising results in performan

8d2af6457dc535053f5f672bd2da5fa6e6f44308.title: Intensity Normalization Using Elastic Warping for FDG-PET Images
8d2af6457dc535053f5f672bd2da5fa6e6f44308.abstract: Intensity normalization is a critical preprocessing step in brain FDG-PET image analysis, enabling quantitative comparison across subjects. Traditional linear methods rely on scaling factors from specific regions or overall brain uptake, which are sensitive to the choice of reference region and spatial disturbances. We propose a novel normalization method based on elastic warping using the Fisher-Rao metric. In contrast to linear scaling methods, our approach allows flexible stretching and squeezing of the intensity range without requiring prior disease knowledge. Compared to conventional methods, our proposed method demonstrates a modest performance improvement in detecting hypo-metabolic voxels, as validated by TTC staining in a rat stroke model, while exhibiting substantially greater robustness against both rigid and scaling spatial disturbances.

8ceead97eae6255b39fafb85c30b7d22e5d720e4.title: Transformer-Based Foundation Model for Universal Ultrasound Image Analysis
8ceead97eae6255b39fafb85c30b7d22e5d720e4.abstract: We propose a transformer-based foundation model for unified multi-task, multi-organ, multi-disease ultrasound image analysis, targeting 27 subtasks across segmentation, classification, detection, and landmark regression. The model follows hard parameter sharing: the encoder of a Swin Transformer pretrained on ImageNet is shared by all tasks, while each task uses its own prediction head. For segmentation and detection tasks, we use feature pyramid network decoders with separate segmentation and detection branches; for classification and regression tasks, we use encoder-level features with specific heads. Compared to other existing methods in offline experiments, the proposed method has the best performance. At the Foundation Model Challenge for Ultrasound Image Analysis (FMC UIA) challenge, our method achieved 8th place among 24th participating teams. The code is public at https://github.

8c5667c6b1efbcee756d2b3deb8c6fa6445f849d.title: Track, Measure, Evaluate: A Clinically Aligned Pipeline for Automatic Radiotherapy Response Assessment in Brain Tumors
8c5667c6b1efbcee756d2b3deb8c6fa6445f849d.abstract: Precise monitoring of tumor size dynamics on serial MRI is essential for radiotherapy response assessment. This task is challenging and resource intensive in the clinic, particularly in patients with multiple brain tumors. We present a modelagnostic lesion tracking, measurement, and response assessment framework that operates directly on binary masks from any segmentation models. The system assigns identity to each lesion at the baseline scan, maintains correspondence across follow-up scans using a compact tracking region of interest, and computes standardized measurements at each visit after radiotherapy. The framework is tunable to align with different response assessment criteria (e.g., RANO-BM, RANO-LGG, RANO-HGG) by adjusting the measurement and aggregation rules. In this study we use lesion-level RANO-BM criteria for the longest diameter-based as well as volumetric response assessm

8c15a8ad68ddb7821b130515eef752b2cda6a852.title: A Dual-Track Framework for Enhancing Age-Related Macular Degeneration Diagnosis Through Embedding and Vision Classification
8c15a8ad68ddb7821b130515eef752b2cda6a852.abstract: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a leading cause of vision loss in older adults, making timely and accurate diagnosis crucial for effective treatment. This study suggests a new framework for AMD diagnosis that integrates embedding extraction and direct vision classification to improve diagnostic performance. We employ a dual-track methodology, utilizing advanced pretrained models for embedding extraction (utilizing Virchow2) alongside a vision-based approach (utilizing Nomic) to classify fundus images into distinct AMD categories: (1) normal, (2) intermediate, (3) geographic atrophy, and (4) wet AMD. Our experiments achieved the best results, with an accuracy of 98.03%, an F1 score of 98.05%, and a precision of 98.08%. By experimentally investigating the applicability of pretrained embedding models originally designed for histopathological patches to fundus images, we bridge a g

8b56452df42c5c380e649f38c06c1f397f175267.title: Freqformer: Frequency-Aware Single Image Super Resolution Network for Biomedical HSI
8b56452df42c5c380e649f38c06c1f397f175267.abstract: Hyperspectral Imaging (HSI) provides rich spectral information that supports a wide range of biomedical applications, yet its spatial resolution remains inherently limited by sensor design and acquisition time. Single Image Super Resolution (SISR) offers a computational solution to enhance HSI spatial detail without compromising spectral integrity. Despite recent progress in HSI-SISR, existing models underutilize frequency-domain cues and often fail when applied to biomedical datasets. This paper presents FreqFormer-HSR, a frequency-enhanced reconstruction framework that augments spatial-spectral feature extraction through lightweight frequency modulation and multi-scale residual refinement. We evaluate the proposed method on two biomedical HSI datasets using a consistent experimental pipeline and compare against representative baselines. Quantitative and visual analyses demonstrate that

8b3c208efa269291729e0c00073f9a618608d96d.title: Diagnosis with Nanoscale Protein Distributions: Single-Molecule Fluorescence Localization Microscopy and Attention-Based Learning
8b3c208efa269291729e0c00073f9a618608d96d.abstract: Single-molecule (fluorescence) localization microscopy (SMLM) finds the position of markers for target proteins at approx. 10 nm precision. Diagnosis of some diseases currently relies on inspection of nanoscale morphology by electron microscopy (EM), an expensive and slow test with limited sample coverage. Nanoscale biological processes also underlie health and disease in general, and so there is a need for more efficient diagnostic methods. We demonstrate that SMLM of routine biopsy samples can be used to assist diagnosis via data classification models. We predict diagnosis of 20 patients with chronic renal diseases (focal segmental glomerulosclerosis or minimal change disease) with a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.97 in cross-validation, and balanced accuracy of 90%. We tested state-of-the-art pretrained feature extraction from image tiles at 0.045 mic

8b070bad595108c0638c33283658521f4c19b8f2.title: Peripheral Prototypical Contrastive Loss for Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
8b070bad595108c0638c33283658521f4c19b8f2.abstract: Robust segmentation of biomedical images remains challenging primarily due to ill-defined object boundaries. Although several loss functions have recently been proposed to enhance object boundary recognition, concerns remain about the susceptibility to unstable annotations resulting from boundary ambiguities. Here, we introduce the Peripheral Prototypical Contrastive (PPC) loss, which leverages prototypical contrastive learning to improve boundary recognition and enable stable training even under noisy annotation conditions. The PPC loss utilizes prototype features obtained from local regions near object boundaries, focusing specifically on ambiguous areas that have been challenging for existing approaches. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets demonstrated that the PPC loss consistently improve segmentation performance even under conditions with noisy labels. A newly proposed s

88fac3ffa31741ba693e78b943131ed9ec3512fd.title: Shape-Guided Self-Supervised Learning for Intracranial Aneurysm Segmentation
88fac3ffa31741ba693e78b943131ed9ec3512fd.abstract: Intracranial aneurysm (IA) is a localized dilation of a cerebral artery that can rupture and cause life-threatening subarachnoid hemorrhage. Accurate segmentation of aneurysms is essential for quantitative morphological assessment and clinical decision-making. IA segmentation remains challenging due to class imbalance, scarce annotations, and high shape variability. Traditional shape-based methods lack shape adaptability, while deep learning approaches often ignore explicit shape priors and are limited by small datasets. To address these issues, we propose a clinically inspired, shape-guided self-supervised learning framework that uses a synthetic deformation engine to generate pseudoaneurysmal geometries, enabling robust learning of aneurysm shape representations without dense labels. Experiments show consistent performance gains (up to +3.0% in aneurysm IoU) across multiple point-based

88ce5656e27bb07e745f33f5b380a2ad70d52922.title: Upstream Probabilistic Meta-Imputation for Multimodal Pediatric Pancreatitis Classification
88ce5656e27bb07e745f33f5b380a2ad70d52922.abstract: Pediatric pancreatitis is a progressive and debilitating inflammatory condition, including acute pancreatitis and chronic pancreatitis, that presents significant clinical diagnostic challenges. Machine learning-based methods also face diagnostic challenges due to limited sample availability and multimodal imaging complexity. To address these challenges, this paper proposes Upstream Probabilistic Meta-Imputation (UPMI), a light-weight augmentation strategy that operates upstream of a stacking classifier in a low-dimensional meta-feature space rather than in image space. Modality-specific logistic regressions (T1W and T2W MRI radiomics) produce probability outputs that are transformed into a 7-dimensional meta-feature vector. 8828d0351043eb567d846dcf03d9c1dcce1e20d8.title: Automatic Segmentation of Calcified Plaque in Carotid Arteries
8828d0351043eb567d846dcf03d9c1dcce1e20d8.abstract: Stroke remains a leading cause of death globally, with calcified plaque in the carotid artery being a significant risk factor. Evaluating the impact of calcified carotid plaque, particularly in patients with embolic stroke of undetermined source (ESUS), is critical yet challenging. Manual segmentation, essential for assessing stroke risk, is time-consuming, and conventional methods like 2D and 3D UNet often struggle with the small size of calcified plaques. Therefore, this paper in-troduces a two-step segmentation process. First, segments the carotid artery to narrow the search space and focus on the region of interest around the artery. Then, it segments the calcified plaque within that targeted region. This approach achieves an intersection over union (IoU) of 0.9412 for the 2D model and 0.8095 for the 3D model, outperforming the baseline methods that directly segment plaques. All deve

8723ad0eb35a101bb01b146c09fd0dada71a488f.title: Beyond AUROC: Evaluating Temporal Stability, False-Positive Load, and Uncertainty Calibration in Capsule Endoscopy Video AI
8723ad0eb35a101bb01b146c09fd0dada71a488f.abstract: Frame-level performance metrics (e.g., AUROC, accuracy) can substantially overestimate real-world reliability for medical video AI because they ignore temporal consistency and reviewer burden. Using the Kvasir Capsule dataset, we report a complementary evaluation suite capturing: (i) temporal stability on lesion segments, (ii) false-positive workload on normal segments, and (iii) uncertainty calibration for risk-aware deployment. Although the classifier achieves near-ceiling framelevel discrimination (AUROC = 0.999, AUPRC = 0.998, F1 = 0.978), our temporal analysis reveals clinically relevant failure modes: severe prediction flicker on some lesion segments (worst TJI = 322.6 flips/1000 frames; worst TDP = 0.19) and concentrated false-positive burden on specific normal segments (worst VRBI = 65.6). Uncertainty analysis indicates well-calibrated confidence (ECE = 0.007) and meaningful unce

86da3a8d64dd334c3d978a689fc602f1393afbba.title: Osteo-Net: Mask R-CNN Based Osteoclasts Detector
86da3a8d64dd334c3d978a689fc602f1393afbba.abstract: Accurate segmentation of osteoclasts in whole-slide images (WSIs) is essential for quantifying cell counts and sizes, a prerequisite for studying bone diseases such as osteoporosis and osteopetrosis. We propose a WSI-to-instance pipeline, Osteo-Net, that integrates patch-level augmentation with seam-robust stitching (feathering, edge trimming, and mask enforcement). Osteo-Net uses Mask R-CNN (ResNet-50 FPN) with SE attention and a composite loss (focal loss for classification and BCE+Dice for masks). On validation patches, Osteo-Net achieves a Dice score of 0.95141 and F1 of 0.93636, and on held-out WSIs it attains Dice 0.9031, substantially outperforming a fine-tuned Cellpose-sam baseline (Dice 0.6623). Ablation analysis shows that focal loss and SE attention drive these gains, whereas CBAM and removal of augmentation degrade performance. These results indicate that tailored loss design

84f222ea75b48637a8ab052f3f150552b16a0c55.title: Easy and Hard Partitions: An Investigation On Dataset Partitions in Biomedical Image Analysis
84f222ea75b48637a8ab052f3f150552b16a0c55.abstract: Researchers and practitioners are often provided with bench-marking datasets that include predefined training and testing partitions. Their task is to design and optimize machine learning models using the training data, aiming to achieve high performance (e.g., accuracy) on the test data. While mod-ern advancements in deep learning-such as transformers and models like Mamba-have made model research increasingly sophisticated, the fixed dataset partition setup raises an im-portant question: Can dataset construction, as the foundation of model development, be improved to better support specific goals in model benchmarking and evaluation? In this paper, we propose a new approach, Easy-and-Hard Partitions (EHP), for constructing benchmarking datasets to advance the development of biomedical AI models. Given a set of labeled samples, our aim is to partition it into two sub-sets (training and

84c97ea9415ff30041a4467b46c3fc65250c41a8.title: Segmentation-Guided Multi-Task Learning for MRI-Based Prediction of Brain Metastasis Origin
84c97ea9415ff30041a4467b46c3fc65250c41a8.abstract: The histologic origin of the primary tumor in brain metastases is closely linked to distinct biological behaviors and therapeutic responses. Although accurate lesion segmentation and primary-site prediction from multi-parametric MRI are essential for preoperative planning, they are often performed as independent tasks, failing to exploit their inherent correlation. To address this limitation, we propose a fully automated multi-task learning framework built on multi-parametric MRI, where the segmentation task explicitly guides primary-site prediction through shared feature representations. Specifically, a hybrid encoder combining convolutional neural networks (CNN) and Transformers is employed to jointly capture local spatial details and global contextual information, enabling shared representation learning across tasks. Then, a 3D CNN decoder produces voxelwise segmentation, while a para

84b984fa6861e2fbcb388d6a2049a50297071da2.title: Segmentation of Hemorrhagic Stroke Using Graph Convolutional Network
84b984fa6861e2fbcb388d6a2049a50297071da2.abstract: Stroke is a serious global public health problem, and several studies on tools to assist its diagnosis have been conducted, many of them involving image processing techniques and deep learning. However, the use of graph convolutional networks (GCN) for stroke classification and segmentation has yet to be explored. This work uses GCN to implement a hemorrhagic stroke segmentation system in Computed Tomography (CT) scans. The results show that the proposed methodology performs well in segmentation, reaching 95.98% in the Dice coefficient and 92.54% in the Jaccard coefficient.

845a7a14a1bff3d4004d41cdcb446b4133a6e3bf.title: CAC-GAN: High-Fidelity Synthesis of MRI Sequences Using Contrast-Aware Cyclegan
845a7a14a1bff3d4004d41cdcb446b4133a6e3bf.abstract: Artificial synthesis of MRI sequences can reduce scan time, cost, and patient discomfort by synthesizing different MRI sequences from one input sequence. However, existing GAN-based approaches struggle with structural inconsistencies and sequence-specific variations, especially across different field strengths. To address these challenges, we propose a Contrast-aware CycleGAN (CAC-GAN), integrating three key innovations: (i) Single Cycle Consistency Loss (SCCL), which enforces cycle constraints only in the target contrast direction to preserve contrast variations; (ii) Feature Matching $\left(\mathcal{L}_{F M}\right)$, which aims to align intermediate image representations to enhance structural fidelity in synthesized images; and (iii) Contrast Loss $\left(\mathcal{L}_{c}\right)$, enforcing matching of pixel intensity distributions to stabilize global contrast. We evaluate our approach o

842adfd4f0cdb79ca316a20d5190f3c97915ba6c.title: MR-Derived Skeletal Muscle Features as Predictors of Diabetes Risk in the German National Cohort
842adfd4f0cdb79ca316a20d5190f3c97915ba6c.abstract: Skeletal muscle composition may provide novel insights into diabetes risk. To assess the predictive value of gluteus, psoas, and thigh muscle features, we segmented these muscle groups from MRI scans of 28,077 participants in the German National Cohort and derived fat fractions, volumes, and cross-sectional areas. Combined with metadata variables, an overall set of 208 features was used to predict HbA 1 c levels and diabetes diagnosis status. We trained XGBoost models on the full feature set to avoid human bias in feature selection and quantified contributions using Shapley Additive Explanations, which capture both main effects and interactions between features. To reduce variance from model uncertainty, training and analysis were repeated 50 times and averaged. Our results show that gluteus fat fraction is among the strongest predictors of diabetes, on par with established risk factors

82ebc1e2ef8fa2eea8884a5bc96bf69c551257ff.title: RTFGM-Net: A Deep Learning Model for Auto-Detection of Hypsarrhythmia EEG in West Syndrome
82ebc1e2ef8fa2eea8884a5bc96bf69c551257ff.abstract: West syndrome (WS) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by developmental delays and motor spasms, often diagnosed through visual detection of hypsarrhythmia in long-term electroencephalography (EEG) recordings. However, manual analysis is time-consuming and prone to errors, underscoring the need for automated diagnostic approaches. In this paper, we propose ResNet-based Time-Frequency Gating Mamba Network RTFGM-Net, an efficient deep learning framework for automated hypsarrhythmia detection in EEG signals. The model integrates a Bidirectional Mamba (BiMamba) and an Efficient Frequency-Time Gating (EFTG) module. The EFTG module combines point-wise and depthwise convolutions with a learnable frequency-domain filter for effective feature extraction, while the BiMamba module captures long-range temporal dependencies through bidirectional processing. 82b74c512771ebec8386bbbcf757496e38157d5c.title: UIGM: Segmentation-Constrained Flow Matching Model for Ultrasound Data Augmentation
82b74c512771ebec8386bbbcf757496e38157d5c.abstract: The scarcity of annotated data is a critical bottleneck in applying deep learning to ultrasound (US) imaging, a problem exacerbated by the modality's dynamic, operator-dependent nature. While generative models offer a promising data augmentation solution, they often focus on perceptual fidelity, failing to guarantee the anatomical plausibility required for downstream tasks like segmentation. To bridge this gap, we introduce the Ultrasound Image Generative Model (UIGM), a novel framework that introduces the use of a segmentationconstrained flow-matching process, further optimized with a non-uniform timestep sampling strategy to boost training efficiency. UIGM not only synthesizes US images efficiently but also explicitly enforces anatomical consistency by integrating a segmentation loss into the generation process. 81e2060ac990c9383e1bbbc7d7674f8ba7faaf9a.title: A Novel Radiopathomic Signature for Oncotype Dx® Prediction in Breast Cancer
81e2060ac990c9383e1bbbc7d7674f8ba7faaf9a.abstract: The Oncotype DX® Recurrence Score (RS) is essential for guiding adjuvant chemotherapy decisions in early-stage ER+/HER2- breast cancer, but it is costly, centralized, and not always accessible. This study developed a radiopathomic approach to estimate RS from routinely available data. A radiomic model trained on MRI using LightGBM achieved an AUC of 0.74 on an external test set, while the pathomic model using ElasticNet reached an AUC of 0.74 in cross-validation. While multimodal fusion improved discrimination in 20 paired cases (AUC $=0.74$; balanced accuracy $=0.77$). Integration with Ki67 and PGR within a nomogram further enhanced prediction (AUC $=0.76$). High specificity and NPV (0.93 and 0.88, respectively) supported the reliable identification of lowrisk patients, potentially helping reduce unnecessary chemotherapy. 81d5200470539acf8ba5835086b3a6be64254c34.title: Knowledge-Aware Multi-Source Domain Adaptation Network for Osteoporosis Diagnosis from Ultrasonic Radio Frequency Signals
81d5200470539acf8ba5835086b3a6be64254c34.abstract: Ultrasonic radio frequency (RF) signal can be utilized in the diagnosis of osteoporosis (OP), thereby assisting healthcare professionals in enhancing the screening rates. However, the heterogeneity of the data collected from different centers can significantly affect the accuracy performance of the model, resulting in lower generalization performance in the target domain. We propose a knowledge-aware unsupervised domain adaptation network guided by knowledge perception that considers both common features and domain-specific features. We employ maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) loss to mitigate distribution discrepancies between various domains. In addition, major clinical risk factors (MCRF) are embedded in domain-specific feature extractors to better extract domain-invariant features. We collect in-house datasets from three distinct centers. Our model demonstrates promising results in both

81895398d078711687cab23a6cac25c97ab437be.title: WAVE-VNET: Enhancing Medical Image Segmentation with Wavelet Transformer
81895398d078711687cab23a6cac25c97ab437be.abstract: Transformer-based models, renowned for their ability to learn long-range information, have recently shown outstanding ca-pabilities in the fields of computer vision and medical image analysis. However, a common limitation in these models is their tendency towards excessive down-sampling, which often results in the loss of high-frequency information. To over-come this limitation, this paper proposes a new method, called Wave-VNet, for efficient and accurate segmentation for medi-cal images. This method employs tokenized image patches in a Transformer-based, V-shaped Encoder-Decoder structure, enriched with skip connections to enhance local-global se-mantic feature learning. 815a5b92d0fae3681bb6bfaba15cc892899c696e.title: Cross-Attention Fusion of Structural and Deformation-Based Mri Features for Alzheimer's Disease Classification
815a5b92d0fae3681bb6bfaba15cc892899c696e.abstract: Accurate assessment of Alzheimer's disease (AD) using neuroimaging is important for understanding disease progression and supporting clinical research. Structural MRI (sMRI) is widely used for this purpose, but most deep learning approaches primarily rely on intensity-based features, which may not fully capture subtle morphological variations. Jacobian determinant maps (JSM) provide complementary information by describing localized brain deformations; however, conventional multimodal fusion strategies such as early or late fusion may not fully capture the interactions between these modalities. To address this, we explore a cross-attention fusion approach that explicitly models the relationship between sMRI intensity and JSM-derived deformation features for AD classification. Using data from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), we compare cross-attention with pairwise s

80961cad32f106171447377bcb539e8ba915324a.title: Multimodal MRI Report Findings Supervised Brain Lesion Segmentation with Substructures
80961cad32f106171447377bcb539e8ba915324a.abstract: Report-supervised (RSuper) learning seeks to alleviate the need for dense tumor voxel labels with constraints derived from radiology reports (e.g., volumes, counts, sizes, locations). In MRI studies of brain tumors, however, we often involve multi-parametric scans and substructures. Here, finegrained modality/parameter-wise reports are usually provided along with global findings and are correlated with different substructures. Moreover, the reports often describe only the largest lesion and provide qualitative or uncertain cues (“mild,” “possible”). Classical RSuper losses (e.g., sum volume consistency) can over-constrain or hallucinate unreported findings under such incompleteness, and are unable to utilize these hierarchical findings or exploit the priors of varied lesion types in a merged dataset. 7ffe2c018877f58225468a6b49b625f88d58da01.title: A Comparison of Deep Learning Models for Automatic Left-Ventricular Segmentation in 3D Echocardiography
7ffe2c018877f58225468a6b49b625f88d58da01.abstract: Echocardiography is a non-invasive, non-ionizing, and cost-effective medical imaging modality that uses ultrasound waves to evaluate cardiac function. Left ventricle (LV) analysis is crucial for diagnosing cardiac diseases. Segmentation of the LV from echocardiography images is a challenging, time-consuming process requiring manual contouring from experts and is prone to inter-observer variability. Five different deep-learning models are evaluated for automatic LV segmentation from 3D echocardiography. The models were compared using overlap and distance metrics: Dice score, Jaccard index, and Hausdorff distance. Volumetric analysis was used to examine the accuracy of the predictions from the deep learning models against the expert-annotated ground truth volumes. The comparison between these models provides a foundation for further development of accurate and efficient automated LV segmen

7fabc41f8553bde9c07cc77e34ec62ebe1a3e396.title: Multimodal Optical Imaging Platform for Quantitative Burn Assessment
7fabc41f8553bde9c07cc77e34ec62ebe1a3e396.abstract: Accurate assessment of burn severity at injury onset remains a major clinical challenge due to the lack of objective methods for detecting subsurface tissue damage. This limitation is critical in battlefield and mass-casualty settings, where rapid and reliable evaluation of burn depth is essential for triage and surgical decision-making. We present a multimodal optical imaging framework that establishes the foundation for a compact, low-size, weight, and power (low-SWaP) field-deployable device for quantitative burn assessment. The system integrates broadband hyperspectral imaging (VSWIR, $400-2100 ~\text{nm}$) with laser speckle contrast imaging to jointly evaluate biochemical composition and microvascular perfusion.
