7f99d2a95ebb18e05dba9e9db0f03ffe58e4ee63.title: Learning Time-Varying Co-Fluctuation Patterns from FMRI for Neurological Disease Diagnosis
7f99d2a95ebb18e05dba9e9db0f03ffe58e4ee63.abstract: Advances in brain imaging have become critical for the early detection of neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer's Disease. Recent studies have demonstrated the potential of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to model complex interactions among brain regions, thereby improving diagnostic accuracy. However, most existing GNN approaches rely on static, node-based functional connectivity representations, which fail to capture more realistic functional connections at the edge level and their dynamics. Motivated by recent neuroscientific findings suggesting that cognitive processes emerge from moment-to-moment, edge-centric interactions in fMRI BOLD signals, we propose a novel GNN framework driven by time-varying edge co-fluctuation representations. It explicitly models temporal co-fluctuation patterns between brain regions and can be integrated with existing GNN architectures to enhance dia

7f0c4fdadad3557e972fd2b9aa1ceaa1966f5500.title: A Cascaded Yolo-Based Framework for Robust Cervical Cell Detection in Pap Smear Images
7f0c4fdadad3557e972fd2b9aa1ceaa1966f5500.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major global health burden, where early detection through cytological screening is critical for improving outcomes. However, Pap smear analysis is often manual, time-consuming, and prone to inter-observer variability. Although deep learning offers promise for automating cytology analysis, challenges such as limited data, class imbalance, staining variability, and overlapping cells hinder reliable model development. In this work, we address these challenges in the RIVA Cytology Challenge, which focuses on nucleus localization in Pap smear images. We propose a cascaded detection framework using multi-dataset pretraining followed by domain-specific finetuning. A YOLO11x model is pretrained on a harmonized multi-dataset collection and then finetuned on the RIVA dataset. During inference, a class-aware pipeline with test-time augmentations and nucleus-centering refin

7e08ece919ad527cf849be7d97242cc7feac8b2b.title: Attention-Based Multiple Instance Learning for Predominant Growth Pattern Prediction in Lung Adenocarcinoma WSI Using Foundation Models
7e08ece919ad527cf849be7d97242cc7feac8b2b.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) grading depends on accurately identifying growth patterns, which are indicators of prognosis and can influence treatment decisions. Common deep learning approaches to determine the predominant pattern rely on patch-level classification or segmentation, requiring extensive annotations. This study proposes an attention-based multiple instance learning (ABMIL) framework to predict the predominant LUAD growth pattern at the whole slide level to reduce annotation burden. Our approach integrates pretrained pathology foundation models as patch encoders, used either frozen or fine-tuned on annotated patches, to extract discriminative features that are aggregated through attention mechanisms. Experiments show that fine-tuned encoders improve performance, with Prov-GigaPath achieving the highest agreement $(\kappa=0.699)$ under ABMIL. Compared to simple patch-aggregation

7dac429b64b40201892458e2a3a7b57a7f0f0512.title: Hierarchical Frequency Regularization for Out-Of-Distribution Detection in Generative Models for Medical Images
7dac429b64b40201892458e2a3a7b57a7f0f0512.abstract: Robust deployment of deep learning models in applications such as medical imaging is of critical importance. Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection is essential in this regard, as it can identify samples that can mislead models into overconfident yet erroneous results. Existing generative approaches, such as Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), often rely on low-level image statistics, limiting their ability to distinguish OOD samples. We propose a hierarchical frequency regularization framework that improves robustness by enforcing consistency across high and low frequency feature representations. Experiments on histological, CT, and MRI data show that combining both frequency components achieves the most stable performance, with AUC 0.989 on histology and competitive results 0.732 and 0.740 for abdominal CT and brain MRI, respectively. The proposed method enhances generalization under distrib

7bfbcf9e0e7da4b0da614516df9e2871eeb22e04.title: SpectroXAI: Quantitative Explainability Consistency for EEG-Based Spectrogram Imaging in Alzheimer's Disease Classification
7bfbcf9e0e7da4b0da614516df9e2871eeb22e04.abstract: Deep learning has achieved notable success in diagnosing neurological disorders from electroencephalographic (EEG) signals; however, interpretability and reliability remain critical challenges. This work introduces SpectroXAI, a unified framework that transforms multichannel EEG recordings into spectrograms and classifies them using a 19-channel ResNet-18 architecture. Dual-mode explainability is achieved through Grad-CAM++ and SHAP for spatial and channel-level attribution. Furthermore, to quantify explanation reliability, Intersection over Union (IoU) and Spearman's rank correlation have been used to measure crossmethod consistency. The proposed SpectroXAI is evaluated on the OpenNeuro dataset (ds004504) and achieves 90% accuracy, an F1-score of 0.909, and consistent attribution agreement ($\text{IoU}=0.48 \pm 0.09; \rho=0.23 \pm 0.05$). These results demonstrate that SpectroXAI enable

7bda49a9b00fe09521ddf772c2a0617060d3ff9a.title: A Deep Learning Framework for Glomeruli Segmentation with Boundary Attention
7bda49a9b00fe09521ddf772c2a0617060d3ff9a.abstract: Accurate detection and segmentation of glomeruli in kidney tissue are essential for diagnostic applications. Traditional deep learning methods primarily rely on semantic segmentation, which often fails to precisely delineate adjacent glomeruli. To address this challenge, we propose a novel glomerulus detection and segmentation model that emphasises boundary separation. Leveraging pathology foundation models, the proposed U-Net–based architecture incorporates a specialised attention decoder designed to highlight critical regions and improve instance-level segmentation. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our approach surpasses state-of-the-art methods in both Dice score and Intersection over Union (IoU), indicating superior performance in glomerular delineation.

7bd1d6cd23d1525cad6f8328bf9673a836c2253d.title: Distribution-Based Brain Connectivity Graph Representations for Classification
7bd1d6cd23d1525cad6f8328bf9673a836c2253d.abstract: Graph-based modeling of the human brain connectome from resting-state fMRI data has become a widely adopted approach in neuroimaging. Region-to-region connectivity is typically estimated using Pearson correlation between timeseries region averages, then used as edge weight in the corresponding brain graph. Instead of scalar edge weights, here, we use a vector of quantiles of distribution-valued edges from a voxel clustering-based statistical estimator. Using three resting-state datasets for classification tasks (patient diagnosis and fluid intelligence quantiles, total $N=293$), we compare the performance of graph representations with distributionvalued edges to that of scalar-valued edges, with six different classifiers - tree ensembles, graph neural networks, and a CNN-XGBoost approach. On metrics of accuracy, Matthews Correlation Coefficient, and AUC, our distribution-valued represent

7bc414e5f269acd4984c3a8be335ed0339165263.title: Separation of Epileptic Foci and Background Sources Using Heterogeneous Source Model with Poisson Wavelet Expansion
7bc414e5f269acd4984c3a8be335ed0339165263.abstract: Magnetoencephalography (MEG) inverse problem is a method that estimates neural currents from the magnetic field measured outside the head, which is essentially used in the diagnosis of epilepsy. Although a single equivalent current dipole (ECD) fitting is usually used in clinical practice, the localization result is incorrect if multiple foci and/or background activities exist other than epileptic discharges. In this paper, we propose a heterogeneous source model that combines two models to distinguish multiple foci from the background activities: one model expresses the localized and multiple foci using Poisson wavelets mapped from a sphere to a cortical surface, and the other model consists of the elemental dipoles on a mesh grid for the background activities. We applied the proposed method to clinical data from an epilepsy patient and showed that multiple sites with spatial extent and

7b67707dee0e35dea9c6d1e7be079fc7a704121f.title: TopoGate: Quality-Aware Topology-Stabilized Gated Fusion for Longitudinal Low-Dose CT New-Lesion Prediction
7b67707dee0e35dea9c6d1e7be079fc7a704121f.abstract: Longitudinal low-dose CT follow-ups vary in noise, reconstruction kernels, and registration quality. These differences destabilize subtraction images and can trigger false “newlesion” alarms. We present TopoGate, a lightweight model that combines the follow-up appearance view with the subtraction view and controls their influence through a learned, quality-aware gate. The gate is driven by three case-specific signals: CT appearance quality, registration consistency, and stability of anatomical topology measured with topological metrics. On the NLST-New-Lesion-LongCT cohort comprising 152 pairs from 122 patients, TopoGate improves discrimination and calibration over single-view baselines, achieving an area under the ROC curve of 0.65 with a standard deviation of 0.05 and a Brier score of 0.14. Removing corrupted or low-quality pairs, identified by the quality scores, further increases the

794563007ae479c431e33859b0e4ca0ec801f5ed.title: Hospital-Specific Bias in Patch-Based Pathology Models
794563007ae479c431e33859b0e4ca0ec801f5ed.abstract: Pathology foundation models (PFMs) achieve strong performance on diverse histopathology tasks, but their sensitivity to hospital-specific domain shifts remains underexplored. We systematically evaluate state-of-the-art PFMs on TCGA patch-level datasets and introduce a lightweight adversarial adaptor to remove hospital-related domain information from latent representations. Experiments show that, while disease classification accuracy is largely maintained, the adaptor effectively reduces hospital-specific bias, as confirmed by t-SNE visualizations. Our study establishes a benchmark for assessing cross-hospital robustness in PFMs and provides a practical strategy for enhancing generalization under heterogeneous clinical settings. Our code is available at https://github.com/MengRes/pfm_domain_bias.

7930c718f9c420964321bc68e88e389787e5e40a.title: Predictive Modeling of Mood Using Functional Network Connectivity: Differential Impacts in Exercise + Smart and Control Groups
7930c718f9c420964321bc68e88e389787e5e40a.abstract: Accurate mood prediction is essential for understanding brain health dynamics and developing interventions, particularly among young adult populations such as undergraduate students. This study explores the use of static functional network connectivity (sFNC) measures from resting-state fMRI (rs-fMRI) data to predict a composite mood index reflecting anxiety, depression, and stress. An autoencoder was employed to capture nonlinear relationships among mood variables, followed by Gaussian process regression (GPR) to predict the composite index at baseline and post-intervention, as well as changes over time. The model demonstrated strong predictive performance, with $R^{2}$ values of 0.60 (baseline), 0.81 (post-intervention), and 0.64 (change). 792f78916ee5ecbb8827c6bf303f50fe6cbc1668.title: SFENet: Shallow Feature Excitation for Retinal Vessel Segmentation
792f78916ee5ecbb8827c6bf303f50fe6cbc1668.abstract: Retinal vessel segmentation is crucial for ophthalmic diagnosis, yet deploying deep learning models on mobile devices remains challenging due to high computational complexity. We propose a lightweight framework, SFENet, that achieves accurate segmentation with minimal resource requirements. Unlike traditional U-Net-based models that rely on deep, computationally intensive encoders, SFENet employs a streamlined single-branch architecture and emphasizes shallow features. Its core innovations include three modules: a hierarchical receptive field module (HRFM) for efficient multi-scale feature extraction, a feature refinement module (FRM) for enhancing vessel detail through dual-branch fusion, and a spatial context mining module (SCMM) for modeling long-range dependencies to ensure vessel continuity. This design significantly reduces model parameters and inference time while maintaining high

78a78a4fdcab469190562623b5fa55c40d26abb1.title: GIG-NET: Cascaded Graph-in-Graph Framework for Molecular Subtype Classification based on Multi-Modal Fusion in Glioma
78a78a4fdcab469190562623b5fa55c40d26abb1.abstract: The molecular diagnosis of $O^{6}$-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGMT) is a critical biomarker for evaluating the prognosis and therapeutic response in glioma patients. However, current machine learning and deep learning methods for predicting MGMT status from multi-modal data suffer from limited classification accuracy and insufficient interpretability of inter-modal relationships. To overcome these limitations, a novel Graph-in-Graph Network (GiG-Net) is proposed to jointly enhance predictive performance and cross-modal explainability. The proposed framework constructs a Position-wise Multi-modal Fusion Graph (PMFG) to model correlations among MRI sequences and radiomic features, followed by a Spatial Relation Graph (SRG) that integrates fused multi-modal representations to capture spatial dependencies. Experimental results on the public dataset (UCSF-PDGM) demonstrate that GiG-

77761f8dfc517e0bd66f1af88831af9338b6a68e.title: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection Framework for Coronary Artery Lesions in CTCA
77761f8dfc517e0bd66f1af88831af9338b6a68e.abstract: Coronary artery disease is a leading cause of mortality world-wide, emphasizing the need for accurate and efficient detection methods. Current deep learning approaches for coronary lesion detection in computed tomography coronary angiog-raphy (CTCA) rely on large labeled datasets for supervised learning, limiting scalability. This study proposes an unsu-pervised framework for coronary lesion detection in CTCA. Using vessel linearization, we generated small linear volume patches from CTCA and trained a deep autoencoder model, MemAE, exclusively on normal patches to detect anomalies based on reconstruction error without lesion location labels. Results on a public dataset demonstrate high accuracy, achieving 97.5% on per-patient average reconstruction error and 85% using the number of patches with high reconstruction error, offering a scalable and accessible solution.

775777ad557fae65301952a272ee5e0fca82afec.title: Visualization Guided Retinal Fluid Segmentation of Optical Coherence Tomography B-Scans
775777ad557fae65301952a272ee5e0fca82afec.abstract: Vision loss remains a critical global health issue, with conditions such as diabetic macular edema and age-related macular degeneration often detected only after substantial retinal damage. Early retinal fluid accumulation is a key biomarker, and Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) provides noninvasive, high-resolution retinal imaging essential for diagnosis. Accurate segmentation of retinal structures is crucial, yet recent conventional deep learning approaches often do not provide satisfactory performance because fluid regions occupy a small portion of the image, leading to inefficient computation and reduced accuracy. We propose CLAVIS, a novel plug-and-play pipeline that leverages CLAssification outputs to generate VIsualizations and guide Segmentation, generating more precise maps of the fluid regions. 7724a17b51c440c5f1fcbb504310ece9a2624b10.title: Human-Aligned Learning of Interpretable Biomarkers for Lung Ultrasound Diagnosis
7724a17b51c440c5f1fcbb504310ece9a2624b10.abstract: Lung ultrasound (LUS) offers rapid, radiation-free bedside imaging, yet automated interpretation remains constrained by the opacity of end-to-end deep learning models. We propose a framework that explicitly aligns learned representations with human clinical reasoning by supervising models to predict interpretable visual biomarkers - clinician-recognized patterns such as A-lines, B-lines, and pleural irregularities - prior to diagnostic inference. This biomarker-aligned representation serves as a compact, semantically meaningful intermediate space for downstream tasks including lungseverity scoring, S/F ratio estimation, and disease classification. On a dataset of 189 patients (718 LUS videos), models trained via biomarker alignment outperform conventional task-specific networks while maintaining interpretability. 75bc9fa72412ff08e8d215e1b5e47061648bcce1.title: F2UE-NET: An Uncertainty-Driven Dynamic Expert Network for Long-Tail Retinal Disease Classification
75bc9fa72412ff08e8d215e1b5e47061648bcce1.abstract: The automatic diagnosis of retinal diseases presents a significant challenge in medical image analysis, primarily due to the long-tail distribution in existing retinal datasets. This imbalance creates substantial difficulties in model training and performance. To address this issue, we propose an uncertainty-driven dynamic expert network for long-tail retinal disease classification, called $\mathrm{F}^{2}\text{UE}$ -Net. Specifically, we apply Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) technology to fine-tune the foundation model, enhancing its feature extraction capabilities and overall performance. Additionally, we introduce an uncertainty-driven dynamic expert participation strategy, which assigns appropriate weights to different categories during training, ensuring high accuracy even for rare, tail-end diseases. 75b2c9b30f1542b048e873d3bc1b6c16157e0ed1.title: Morphogenetic Field Loss for Unified Medical Image Segmentation
75b2c9b30f1542b048e873d3bc1b6c16157e0ed1.abstract: Training medical segmentation networks hinges on our ability to find good minimizer of highly non-convex loss functions, yet the way different losses sculpt this landscape remains poorly understood. Classical objectives such as crossentropy, Dice, and Tversky act as static point wise penalties, offering little insight into how anatomical structure and uncertainty influence optimization. In this work, we reinterpret supervision through the lens of reaction-diffusion dynamics and introduce Morphogenetic Field Loss (MFLoss), which evolves predictions and ground truth as interacting morphogenetic fields before measuring their discrepancy. This view yields smoother, more topology-aware minima that generalize across organs, lesions, layers, instruments, and brain tissue, while remaining fully compatible with standard backpropagation and architectures. 7587969c259b37c8416dec3cc32033b634884b20.title: WEAKLY SUPERVISED SEGMENTATION AND CLASSIFICATION OF ALPHA-SYNUCLEIN AGGREGATES IN BRIGHTFIELD MIDBRAIN IMAGES
7587969c259b37c8416dec3cc32033b634884b20.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder associated with the accumulation of misfolded alpha-synuclein aggregates, forming Lewy bodies and neuritic shape used for pathology diagnostics. Automatic analysis of immunohistochemistry histopathological images with Deep Learning provides a promising tool for better understanding the spatial organization of these aggregates. In this study, we develop an automated image processing pipeline to segment and classify these aggregates in whole-slide images (WSIs) of midbrain tissue from PD and incidental Lewy Body Disease (iLBD) cases based on weakly supervised segmentation, robust to immunohistochemical labelling variability, with a ResNet50 classifier. Our approach allows to differentiate between major aggregate morphologies, including Lewy bodies and neurites with a balanced accuracy of 80 %. This framework paves the way for large-s

74a5f00982a9ee0fe9e8c3a204928e63dd720455.title: Evaluating Data Augmentation Strategies for Robust Cross-Dataset Generalization in Wound Classification
74a5f00982a9ee0fe9e8c3a204928e63dd720455.abstract: This study investigates the impact of data augmentation strategies on the cross-dataset generalization of deep learning models for wound classification. Using the AZH dataset for model training, we implemented and optimized various augmentation strategies-categorized as photometric, geometric, elastic, cutout, and automated methods (RandAugment and TrivialAugmentWide)-to enhance model robustness. Each augmentation's parameters were tuned using Optuna to maximize performance. The optimized augmentations were then evaluated on the Medetec dataset to analyze generalization performance across datasets. Results indicate that photometric and cutout transformations, particularly when combined, significantly improve cross-dataset accuracy and F1-scores. 744795238d90c08e44dd1e43fc0aa85f96a65d31.title: Multicenter Radiomic Feature-Based Prediction of PD-L1 Status in Lung Cancer Using Multimodal PET/CT
744795238d90c08e44dd1e43fc0aa85f96a65d31.abstract: With the growing utilization of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), there is an urgent need to identify biomarkers that can stratify patients into responders and non-responders based on programmed death-ligand (PD-L1) expression. The aim of this study is to determine the feasibility of building imaging-based predictive biomarkers for PD-L1 and system-atically evaluating a combination of several machine learning algorithms. A retrospective, multicenter study was conducted involving 467 advanced NSCLC patients eligible for ICIs across four various centers (France, China, Greece and Switzerland). Radiomic features derived from pretreatment PET/CT scans were used to construct predictive models for PD-L1 expression. 73300273ade55b85f1b87932910e1780a78108d3.title: Graphtrack: Automated Longitudinal Lesion Tracking in Ct Via Local-Global Reasoning With Contrastive and Graph Learning
73300273ade55b85f1b87932910e1780a78108d3.abstract: Accurate lesion tracking in longitudinal CT scans is essential for streamlining treatment response and disease progression evaluation in oncology, but current clinical workflows remain largely manual and variable. We propose GraphTrack, a two-stage deep learning framework that unifies local and global reasoning for automated lesion correspondence. First, a self-supervised 3D Masked Autoencoder (3DMAE) pretrains transferable lesion representations, fine-tuned within a 3D Siamese Neural Network (3DSNN) via contrastive learning for pairwise similarity estimation. Then, these features are integrated into an Edge Graph Attention Network (EdgeGAT) with similarity-based curriculum learning to model spatial, temporal, and morphological dependencies. 70565a9e6ee8f9d5547f2015e771bc78d319b0e3.title: Fusion of Dwi Image and Clinical Variables for Stroke Outcome Prediction Using Tabular Transformer
70565a9e6ee8f9d5547f2015e771bc78d319b0e3.abstract: Ischemic stroke is a major cause of global disability, making outcome prediction crucial for effective management. In this study, we propose an approach using a tabular transformer to fuse diffusion weighted MRI and clinical variables for stroke outcome prediction. Radiomics are employed to extract quantitative features from regions of interest drawn on early diffusion weighted MRI acquired at acute stage in intensive care unit. The 3-month modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score serves as the ground truth for forecasting patient outcomes. Performance of the proposed model was evaluated on a private database encompassing 119 exams of stroke patients treated with thrombectomy (66% of which had a favorable prognosis). The proposed fusion approach achieves strong predictive performance, with an AUC of 0.75 and an accuracy of 0.72. Furthermore, analyzing feature importance contributed to a deeper

6fccafc17346de78de49b6d46408bc58db169f6d.title: Task-Aware Functional Hypergraph Learning for Brain State Classification via Information Bottleneck
6fccafc17346de78de49b6d46408bc58db169f6d.abstract: Functional connectivity networks (FCNs) are widely used in fMRI-based brain analysis. While most existing studies represent FCNs using graphs, traditional graph structures primarily focus on pairwise connections, overlooking higher-order relationships. Additionally, many methods construct graphs or hypergraphs independently of downstream tasks, which can result in suboptimal representations that fail to capture task-relevant structures. To address these limitations, we propose a novel approach that integrates task-specific information directly into the hypergraph construction process. Our method employs a learnable groupwise mask to construct a groupwise hypergraph structure across all subjects. To retain task-related brain regions and filter out irrelevant ones, we introduce an information bottleneck constraint to optimize our framework. Furthermore, to capture personalized information,

6f28278013dfc50722d9704fb904351345c2c5c5.title: Cardiac Output Prediction From Echocardiograms: Self-Supervised Learning with Limited Data
6f28278013dfc50722d9704fb904351345c2c5c5.abstract: Cardiac Output (CO) is a key parameter in the diagnosis and management of cardiovascular diseases. However, its accurate measurement requires right-heart catheterization, an invasive and time-consuming procedure, motivating the development of reliable non-invasive alternatives using echocardiography. In this work, we propose a self-supervised learning (SSL) pretraining strategy based on SimCLR to improve CO prediction from apical four-chamber echocardiographic videos. The pretraining is performed using the same limited dataset available for the downstream task, demonstrating the potential of SSL even under data scarcity. Our results show that SSL mitigates overfitting and improves representation learning, achieving an average Pearson correlation of 0.41 on the test set and outperforming PanEcho, a model trained on over one million echocardiographic exams.

6f28200f99348c44f2248fc3b1c5e7ec7bd05b9f.title: Wavelet-Based Scale-Wise Functional Connectivity Revealed Modulations Due to a $\beta$-Tau Proteins in Alzheimer's Disease
6f28200f99348c44f2248fc3b1c5e7ec7bd05b9f.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by the accumulation of amyloid- $\beta$ ($\mathrm{A} \beta$) and tau proteins, which disrupt the brain's functional connectome. To investigate such alterations, we analyzed functional MRI data from 248 individuals across the AD spectrum using a wavelet transform-based framework. Static functional connectivity matrices were derived at multiple frequency scales and used as input for AI models to address two classification tasks: i) cognitively unimpaired $\mathrm{A} \beta$-tau -vs cognitively impaired $\mathrm{A} \beta$-tau+, and ii) cognitively unimpaired $\mathrm{A} \beta$-tau+ vs cognitively impaired $\mathrm{A} \beta$-tau−. Deep learning models outperformed traditional machine learning approaches, while saliency maps revealed key brain networks, including the default mode, salience, limbic, and somatomotor, as critical to task discrimination. 6ede3c5f22fcdf907473d3e781d9028d8a883287.title: POCKETLV: A Point-of-Care Echocardiography Dataset for Deep Learning Image Processing of the Left Ventricle
6ede3c5f22fcdf907473d3e781d9028d8a883287.abstract: Cardiac disease remains the primary cause of mortality worldwide. Waiting times for standard echocardiography are lengthening due to growing needs of ageing populations and shortage of trained sonographers. Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) has emerged as a portable, cost-effective alternative, allowing quicker evaluation while waiting for traditional scans to rule out life-threatening pathology. POCUS is often used by clinicians without full echocardiography training. In addition, POCUS images are of lower quality and only used for qualitative cardiac evaluation, particularly left-ventricular systolic function. Deep learning could enhance its capabilities, but no public POCUS dataset currently exists to support it. 6de5a3da732ae2961e3f58a60e66cb62f455e995.title: Deepsrs: Enhancing Stimulated Raman Scattering Imaging Through Multi-Stage Deep Learning for Super-Resolution and Denoising
6de5a3da732ae2961e3f58a60e66cb62f455e995.abstract: DeepSRS is a multi-stage deep learning framework designed to enhance Stimulated Raman Scattering (SRS) microscopy images by addressing both denoising and super-resolution challenges. The pipeline combines an autoencoder-based spectral denoiser with fine-tuned generative models—namely GAN and diffusion architectures—to achieve rapid, high-fidelity reconstruction. DeepSRS attains up to fourfold lateral superresolution, markedly improving signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), structural similarity, and perceptual quality metrics. This integrated approach expands the analytical capabilities of nonlinear optical imaging and opens new avenues for biochemical visualization, histological interpretation, and quantitative microscopy in both research and clinical settings.

6d438f34abc33d5e0e6d0011c979e5c2b3a78894.title: MO-CTranS: A Unified Multi-Organ Segmentation Model Learning from Multiple Heterogeneously Labelled Datasets
6d438f34abc33d5e0e6d0011c979e5c2b3a78894.abstract: Multi-organ segmentation holds paramount significance in many clinical tasks. In practice, compared to large fully annotated datasets, multiple small datasets are often more accessible and organs are not labelled consistently. Normally, an individual model is trained for each of these datasets, which is not an effective way of using data for model learning. It remains challenging to train a single model that can robustly learn from several partially labelled datasets due to label conflict and data imbalance problems. We propose MO-CTranS: a single model that can overcome such problems. MO-CTranS contains a CNN-based encoder and a Transformer-based decoder, which are connected in a multi-resolution manner. 6cd8390b1856426f4dd97424defaac57d6eac72a.title: DA-GMGENet: A Domain Adaptation Framework for 3D CT-Based ECE Identification in Head and Neck Cancer
6cd8390b1856426f4dd97424defaac57d6eac72a.abstract: Identification of lymph node Extracapsular Extension (ECE) is crucial for the diagnosis and clinical decision making of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). Despite the advancements of automatic ECE identification, the effect of adversary during transferring the developed model to different environments may still cause instability in the performance metrics. The aim of this study is to develop a model which can perform under adversary and reduce the discrepancy between the source and target domain. Here, we introduce Domain Adaptation enhanced Gradient Mapping Guided Explainable Network (DA-GMGENet) which leverages an automatic ECE identification from unlabeled target dataset as well as ensures the transfer ability of the model by increasing the robustness under worst case domain shift. Evaluation on a public dataset gives the best AUC of 78.1% and sensitivity of 71.6% compared

6c19c6a224c715d2b5a6c37c31b7c4c1f04b8092.title: Functional-Positional Context Embedding in Graph Neural Networks for Improved Parkinson's Disease Diagnosis
6c19c6a224c715d2b5a6c37c31b7c4c1f04b8092.abstract: Graph neural networks for fMRI data often emphasize region-to-region similarities but neglect important factors like hemispheric asymmetry and functional grouping. We introduce a novel framework integrating Functional and Positional Context Embedding with Hemispheric Asymmetry Features to enhance early-stage Parkinson's Disease classification. Our approach refines graph representations of functional connectivity, yielding improved detection of subtle pathological patterns. These findings underscore the value of neuroscience-informed design in brain connectivity analysis.

6b97ca7c7586879f2c91b260e135cbd99d7dcf93.title: CODE: A SELF-SUPERVISED CONSISTENCY MODEL FRAMEWORK FOR MRI DENOISING
6b97ca7c7586879f2c91b260e135cbd99d7dcf93.abstract: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is great for visualizing soft tissues and quantitative assessment of tissue properties, but its acquisitions are often limited by signal noise originating from the patient's thermal and physiological processes, motion, and hardware limitations/imperfections. We propose CoDe, a self-supervised consistency model (CM) framework that achieves efficient one-step MRI denoising. Our approach consists of two components: a noise estimation model that predicts the noise level of the input image and a CM performing one-step denoising to recover clean images. Additionally, we introduce a Random Matrix Theory (RMT)-based regularization that leverages physical noise statistics to enhance structural fidelity. Experiments on public brain and in-house prostate diffusion MRI datasets demonstrate that CoDe achieves superior image quality compared with existing methods while

6a55184b822c10fc4d5d100b408658c666a91c86.title: From Volumes to Slices: Computationally Efficient Contrastive Learning for Sequential Abdominal CT Analysis
6a55184b822c10fc4d5d100b408658c666a91c86.abstract: The requirement for expert annotations limits the effectiveness of deep learning for medical image analysis. Although 3D self-supervised methods like volume contrast learning (VoCo) are powerful and partially address the labeling scarcity issue, their high computational cost and memory consumption are barriers. We propose 2D-VoCo, an efficient adaptation of the VoCo framework for slice-level self-supervised pre-training that learns spatial-semantic features from unlabeled 2D CT slices via contrastive learning. The pre-trained CNN backbone is then integrated into a CNN-LSTM architecture to classify multi-organ injuries. In the RSNA 2023 Abdominal Trauma dataset, 2D-VoCo pretraining significantly improves mAP, precision, recall, and RSNA score over training from scratch. Our framework provides a practical method to reduce the dependency on labeled data and enhance model performance in clin

6a44b28a474786a92598f3c820b40e8d529a7dad.title: Uncertainty Analysis in Intravascular Oct Segmentation
6a44b28a474786a92598f3c820b40e8d529a7dad.abstract: Integrating uncertainty quantification (UQ) into optical coherence tomography (OCT) segmentation could enhance model reliability and clinical interpretability. Using an ensemble-based model, we estimated pixelwise entropy as a measure of uncertainty and compared it to segmentation accuracy and inter-observer variability. Higher entropy was associated with lower accuracy: uncertain predictions had lower Dice scores and larger measurement errors, particularly in complex structures. Regions of annotator disagreement coincided with elevated model uncertainty. Entropy-based UQ thus provides an interpretable confidence measure, supporting selective human review and more trustworthy AI-assisted OCT analysis.

67ce077ea44a3c96ea7ea4674fd6534caf0e68e6.title: Foundation Model-Guided Iteratively Prompting and Pseudo-Labeling for Partially Labeled Medical Image Segmentation
67ce077ea44a3c96ea7ea4674fd6534caf0e68e6.abstract: Automated medical image segmentation has achieved remarkable progress with fully labeled data. However, sitespecific clinical priorities and the high cost of manual annotation often yield scans with only a subset of organs labeled, leading to the partially labeled problem that degrades performance. To address this issue, we propose IPnP, an Iteratively Prompting and Pseudo-labeling framework, for partially labeled medical image segmentation. IPnP iteratively generates and refines pseudo-labels for unlabeled organs through collaboration between a trainable segmentation network (specialist) and a frozen foundation model (generalist), progressively recovering full-organ supervision. On the public dataset AMOS with the simulated partial-label setting, IPnP consistently improves segmentation performance over prior methods and approaches the performance of the fully labeled reference. We furth

67c05128aae919bca677638d34ae95d6eb2b4727.title: All-Subtype Cataract Classification and Grading in AS-OCT via a Unified Multi-Task Framework
67c05128aae919bca677638d34ae95d6eb2b4727.abstract: Automated cataract grading based on Anterior Segment Optical Coherence Tomography (AS-OCT) plays a key role in objective diagnosis. However, current approaches are restricted to single-subtype analysis, limiting their clinical applicability. We propose a unified multitask framework that concurrently performs lens subregion segmentation and severity grading for cortical, nuclear, and posterior subcapsular cataracts. The framework integrates three modules: an Implicit Boundary Rendering (IBR) module for sub-pixel boundary refinement, a Laplacian Feature Masking (LFM) module for subregion-specific feature separation, and a Multi-Granularity Experts Fusion (MGEF) module for adaptive feature integration. Experiments on 2,088 AS-OCT images demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, improving IoU by up to 4 % and grading accuracy by 3-10 % compared with existing models.

67baa1d588f5fbdf310a5c57f860e58454b3d92e.title: A BI-OBJECTIVE BUDGETED SET-COVER FORMULATION FOR OPTIMISINGINVERSE-GEOMETRY X-RAY CT ARCHITECTURES
67baa1d588f5fbdf310a5c57f860e58454b3d92e.abstract: Current X ray computed tomography uses cone beam and fan beam architectures guided by clinical requirements. We investigate inverse geometry CT (IGCT), which flips the standard acquisition paradigm by replacing a single source and a large detector with multiple sources and a small detector. For practical realisation and in order to limit acquisition time, we focus on configurations with a small detector and a limited number of sources, which leads to truncation artefacts and insufficient angular coverage for some voxels. To mitigate these artefacts, we focus on optimising the spatial placement of a fixed budget of sources for imaging an organ of interest. We cast the problem as a linear integer program based on budgeted set cover, with a bi-objective, hierarchical structure. Finally, we present an approximation framework based on a stochastic algorithm to efficiently solve this problem.

6785576e31db748e1a41e0a057f51e5997dbfd00.title: HAGD: Hierarchical Anatomical-Guided Diffusion for Synthetic CT Generation from CBCT
6785576e31db748e1a41e0a057f51e5997dbfd00.abstract: Acquiring high-quality synthetic computed tomography (sCT) images from cone-beam CT is crucial for accurate dose calculation in the field of adaptive radiotherapy. However, existing sCT generation methods based on diffusion models often struggle to preserve anatomical structures, especially when the anatomical structure of the input CBCT and ground-truth CT differs in shape. To address this, we propose a Hierarchical Anatomical-Guided Diffusion (HAGD) framework that captures both global semantic information and local textural details for anatomical-aware sCT generation. We first introduce a dual-branch encoder to simultaneously extract features from coarse structural masks and fine segmentation maps. Secondly, a hierarchical fusion module is proposed to integrate these multiscale features into the conditional diffusion model, using concatenation or attention-gated fusion. Experiments on

6754ef110e60a81dacf8b99a24209e5ab89ef938.title: SEGMENTATION CONFIDENCE FOR ARBITRARY CNNS
6754ef110e60a81dacf8b99a24209e5ab89ef938.abstract: Convolutional neural networks (CNN) are widely used for medical image segmentation. However, they lack an inherent measure of confidence. Existing methods for estimating prediction uncertainty often require a custom network architecture and/or dedicated training setups and need to be trained from scratch. In addition, the deduction of a single confidence score per input from the uncertainty maps is not always straightforward. In this study, we explore voxel-based uncertainty estimation methods that can be added to existing segmentation pipelines without training from scratch. We also propose a novel method to estimate a single confidence score from the uncertainty maps. Our evaluations on different ROIs and modalities suggest that our confidence score can predict segmentation performance in unseen data.

670d0e59f89d4868f161b5d7b3fef9bc000dc197.title: Hybrid Resnet-Unetr for Semi-Supervised Fetal Cardiac Segmentation and CHD Classification
670d0e59f89d4868f161b5d7b3fef9bc000dc197.abstract: We present a multi-task framework for simultaneous fetal cardiac structure segmentation (14 classes, 4 views) and congenital heart disease (CHD) classification (7 pathologies) from prenatal ultrasound, developed for the FETUS 2026 Challenge at ISBI. Our approach introduces a hybrid architecture combining a fully trainable ResNet-50 encoder with a UNETR-style decoder enhanced by deep supervision at four levels and a boundary detection head that fuses contour features into the decoding path. Classification is performed through a multi-scale attention pooling and a morphological feature head. We demonstrated that a two-phase trainable general-purpose framework can outperform a domain specific foundation model under label scarcity obtaining segmentation metrics of Dice = 73.32 and NSD = 48.76, while for classification Macro F1 = 32.64, with a score of 52.16/80., achieving first place in the

658d9e7e96e700520f8e4f05e42ac979af214a07.title: A Multi-Modal Variational Hypergraph Autoencoder for Structural-Functional Brain Connectivity Analysis
658d9e7e96e700520f8e4f05e42ac979af214a07.abstract: Brain connectivity analysis offers critical insights on understanding and classifying neurological disorders. However, conventional graph neural networks (GNNs) used in existing studies are limited to pairwise connections, and fail to capture higher-order interactions among brain regions. To address this gap, we propose a Multi-Modal Variational Hypergraph Autoencoder (MVHGAE) that integrates both structural connectivity (SC) and functional connectivity (FC) within a unified hypergraph representation. The variational formulation enables probabilistic latent encoding of brain connectivity patterns, facilitating more robust and generalizable representations across subjects. Unlike generic Hypergraph Neural Networks (HGNNs), the proposed architecture incorporates dynamic node-edge weighting and deterministic feature fusion for enhanced stability. Experimental evaluations on resting-state fu

64f8430952dfcb6adbab229193d1654424b201c3.title: Classifying Coronary Artery Calcification Risk using Radiomics from Non-Gated CT Scans
64f8430952dfcb6adbab229193d1654424b201c3.abstract: Opportunistic coronary artery calcification (CAC) scoring using chest computed tomography (CT) scans is a valuable tool for predicting cardiovascular event risk. Despite over 15 million chest CT scans performed annually, routine CAC scoring remains limited due to the manual labor involved. Although deep learning algorithms have shown promise in segmenting CAC lesions for risk evaluation, widespread adoption is still lacking because of the costs associated with these technologies and the difficulties in integrating them into existing clinical workflows. In this study, we propose a pipeline for CAC segmentation and risk classification. We first train a segmentation model on gated CT scans and subsequently fine-tune it using a smaller dataset of non-gated scans. We employ TotalSegmentator to cone down non-gated scans, simulating the field of view typical of gated CT scans. Radiomic features

64a047c9ee53af6916563b605461259b933ec66a.title: RDTE-UNet: A Boundary and Detail Aware UNet for Precise Medical Image Segmentation
64a047c9ee53af6916563b605461259b933ec66a.abstract: Medical image segmentation is essential for computer-assisted diagnosis and treatment planning, yet substantial anatomical variability and boundary ambiguity hinder reliable delineation of fine structures. We propose RDTE-UNet, a segmentation network that unifies local modeling with global context to strengthen boundary delineation and detail preservation. RDTE-UNet employs a hybrid ResBlock detail-aware Transformer backbone and three modules: ASBE for adaptive boundary enhancement, HVDA for fine-grained feature modeling, and EulerFF for fusion weighting guided by Euler's formula. Together, these components improve structural consistency and boundary accuracy across morphology, orientation, and scale. On Synapse and BUSI dataset, RDTE-UNet has achieved a comparable level in terms of segmentation accuracy and boundary quality. 11https://github.com/TantalumKevin/RDTE-UNet

6432470c674335d3135abc78cdd6cc498f148230.title: CROSS-MODAL FINE-TUNING OF 3D CONVOLUTIONAL FOUNDATION MODELS FOR ADHD CLASSIFICATION WITH LOW-RANK ADAPTATION
6432470c674335d3135abc78cdd6cc498f148230.abstract: Early diagnosis of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children plays a crucial role in improving outcomes in education and mental health. Diagnosing ADHD using neuroimaging data, however, remains challenging due to heterogeneous presentations and overlapping symptoms with other conditions. To address this, we propose a novel parameter-efficient transfer learning approach that adapts a large-scale 3D convolutional foundation model, pre-trained on CT images, to an MRI-based ADHD classification task. Our method introduces Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) in 3D by factorizing 3D convolutional kernels into 2D low-rank updates, dramatically reducing trainable parameters while achieving superior performance. In a five-fold cross-validated evaluation on a public diffusion MRI database, our 3D LoRA fine-tuning strategy achieved state-of-the-art results, with one model variant reaching 7

63ec8583eedf4153e3bd2ad91eba681b23f78e91.title: Useful Nonrobust Features are Ubiquitous in Biomedical Images
63ec8583eedf4153e3bd2ad91eba681b23f78e91.abstract: We study whether deep networks for medical imaging learn useful nonrobust features - predictive input patterns that are not human interpretable and highly susceptible to small adversarial perturbations - and how these features impact test performance. We show that models trained only on nonrobust features achieve well-above-chance accuracy across five MedMNIST classification tasks, confirming their predictive value in-distribution. Conversely, adversarially trained models that primarily rely on robust features sacrifice indistribution accuracy but yield markedly better performance under controlled distribution shifts (MedMNIST-C). Overall, nonrobust features boost standard accuracy yet degrade out-of-distribution performance, revealing a practical robustnessaccuracy trade-off in medical imaging classification tasks that should be tailored to the requirements of the deployment setting.

63df01408d59840e92a53bfb57251d683729638a.title: Survival Modeling from Whole Slide Images Via Patch-Level Graph Clustering and Mixture Density Experts
63df01408d59840e92a53bfb57251d683729638a.abstract: We present a modular framework for predicting cancerspecific survival from whole-slide pathology images (WSIs). The approach integrates four main components: (i) Quantile-Based Patch Filtering, which employs quantile-based thresholding to identify prognostically informative tissue regions; (ii) Graph Regularized Patch Clustering using $k$-NN graph to model phenotype-level heterogeneity through spatial-morphological coherence; (iii) Hierarchical Feature Aggregation for learning intra- and inter-cluster dependencies; and (iv) an Expert Guided Mixture Density Modeling module to estimate complex survival distributions using Gaussian distributions. The proposed model achieves a concordance index of $0.653 \pm 0.037$ on TCGA-LUAD, $0.719 \pm 0.011$ on TCGA-KIRC, and $0.733 \pm 0.037$ on TCGA-BRCA, surpassing current state-of-the-art methods.

63d477770a614914c10e15692acc052d25c9a5d5.title: Cross-Modal Image Learning for HER2 Status Detection From H&E Histopathology Images
63d477770a614914c10e15692acc052d25c9a5d5.abstract: Human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor 2 (HER2) status plays a key role in predicting breast cancer outcomes and guiding targeted treatments. The current clinical standard, Immunohistochemistry (IHC), provides reliable results but depends on specialized reagents, extra processing time, and advanced laboratory facilities, making it less accessible in many settings. This work introduces a cross-modal image learning framework that can automatically determine HER2 status directly from routine Hematoxylin and Eosin (H&E) stained whole-slide images, reducing the need for IHC images. Our model learns from paired H&E-IHC samples to capture subtle tissue structures and patterns in H&E images that reflect HER2 expression. We evaluate our approach on the BCI dataset and compare it qualitatively with IHC-based scoring. Our method performs inference solely on H&Estained slides yet achieves superior p

63b626e5debc3e636866c5faa73952b606e53433.title: Unbalanced Optimal Transport for Robust Longitudinal Lesion Evolution with Registration-Aware and Appearance-Guided Priors
63b626e5debc3e636866c5faa73952b606e53433.abstract: Evaluating lesion evolution in longitudinal CT scans of cancer patients is essential for assessing treatment response, yet establishing reliable lesion correspondence across time remains challenging. Standard bipartite matchers, which rely on geometric proximity, struggle when lesions appear, disappear, merge, or split. We propose a registration-aware matcher based on unbalanced optimal transport (UOT) that accommodates unequal lesion mass and adapts priors to patient-level tumor-load changes. Our transport cost blends (i) size-normalized geometry, (ii) local registration trust from the deformation-field Jacobian, and (iii) optional patch-level appearance consistency. The resulting transport plan is sparsified by relative pruning, yielding one-to-one matches as well as new, disappearing, merging, and splitting lesions without retraining or heuristic rules. 63663431daac59ea1208ddb11965a2a651138c3a.title: Mobile Augmented Reality for Hip Osteotomy Planning: Integration with 3D Slicer and Pilot Evaluation
63663431daac59ea1208ddb11965a2a651138c3a.abstract: This paper presents a smartphone-based Augmented Reality (AR) system designed to support hip osteotomy planning through interactive three-dimensional (3D) visualization. The mobile application integrates 3D Slicer and Unity, enabling seamless transfer and real-time interaction with segmented anatomical models on standard smartphones. The system allows clinicians to visualize, align, and perform virtual osteotomy planning without requiring specialized hardware or complex setup. To identify the femoral head pivot point, an Iterative Closest Point (ICP)-based approach was implemented to demonstrate alignment feasibility. Initial evaluation by clinicians and biomedical engineers indicated good anatomical visualization and usability. The system's portability and low-cost implementation make it well suited for point-of-care use and for extending advanced 3D visualization tools to low-resource

63346e3e3e508f27c02edb55dddf31b93c854b40.title: Semi-Supervised Medical Image Classification with Neighborhood Adaptive Attention
63346e3e3e508f27c02edb55dddf31b93c854b40.abstract: Semi-supervised learning utilize unlabeled data to improve model performance, which is of great significance in medical imaging tasks. However, due to the high inter class similarity and large intra class variance in medical data, this still poses challenges. To address these challenges, a neighborhood adaptive attention (NAA) mechanism is introduced, which extends to surrounding attributes based on mutual correlation, considers the lesion area and its highly correlated pathological attributes, enabling the model to learn additional semantic information and improve diagnostic performance. Unlike previous semi-supervised frameworks, sample information below the threshold is not discarded. In contrast, class imbalance comparison loss (CICL) is constructed by combining the information of samples above and below the threshold. Our method has been evaluated in challenging medical image classi

62969fbad9de54d17812328d06b6262eb0bb3302.title: Quantitative Evaluation of Explanation Quality in Fetal Ultrasound Quality Criterion Detection Using Saliency Maps
62969fbad9de54d17812328d06b6262eb0bb3302.abstract: Reliability and interpretability are crucial for deploying deep learning models in medical imaging, where decisions directly influence patient care. In fetal ultrasound, accurate detection and understanding of biometric quality criterions are vital for diagnostic quality. Although saliency-based methods like Grad-CAM provide visual explanations, their clinical use is limited by the absence of quantitative measures of explanation quality. This work presents a systematic framework for evaluating and validating explanations in fetal ultrasound quality criterion detection. A DenseNet-121 classifier identifies key quality quality criterions, while Grad-CAM and its variants generate saliency maps. We introduce a hybrid quality score that combines region-reduction analysis, perturbation-based robustness, and graph-based superpixel similarity with reference annotations to assign reliable quantit

6279ea54f428b1804cfc812292069122face50d6.title: Cross-Domain Vision-Language Transfer Learning for Surgical Drain Detection in Real-World Postoperative Images
6279ea54f428b1804cfc812292069122face50d6.abstract: Accurate detection of surgical drains in postoperative patientsubmitted images is vital for monitoring recovery and preventing complications. We present a transfer learning approach using vision models pretrained with natural language supervision to identify drains in real-world surgical images. Multiple architectures are fine-tuned on a diverse dataset of patient-submitted photos. Results highlight model performance trade-offs and provide insights toward developing automated systems for postoperative surgical site monitoring.

626827dd6131afce3bfd3475f81a2e4f91d4c7de.title: Label Uncertainty for Ultrasound Segmentation
626827dd6131afce3bfd3475f81a2e4f91d4c7de.abstract: Inter-observer variability in medical imaging introduces label uncertainty, particularly in modalities requiring subjective interpretation such as lung ultrasound (LUS). We propose a confidence-aware framework for segmentation that incorporates expert-provided per-pixel confidence scores during both labeling and model training. Instead of treating annotations as absolute ground truth, we capture radiologists' uncertainty as a first-class learning signal to model inherent aleatoric uncertainty. Using a novel confidence-annotated LUS dataset, we evaluate segmentation models trained with varying confidence thresholds and show that incorporating label confidence improves both segmentation and downstream clinical performance - including estimation of the S/F oxygenation ratio and prediction of 30-day readmission. Models trained using a 60% confidence threshold outperform conventional training

6193320bdc3ce8f7a52154cb7db18c72938f185b.title: Direction-Guided Watershed for Adherent Cell Instance Segmentation
6193320bdc3ce8f7a52154cb7db18c72938f185b.abstract: Accurate segmentation of adherent cells remains a critical challenge in computational pathology. While relation-based modeling excels at pixel-wise prediction, its reliance on watershed post-processing renders it susceptible to noise, potentially leading to over- or under-segmentation in complex adherent regions. To address this, we introduce directional guidance to augment the watershed algorithm via two complementary modules: a Directional Disparity Boundary Discernment (DDBD) module and an Oriented-Attentive Watershed Augmentation (OAWA) module. Together with high-gradient pixel screening, DDBD forms a dual-cue edge screening by assessing directional disparity, effectively discriminating true boundaries from noise. OAWA then accentuates these valid boundaries by weighting the neighborhoods along their dominant gradient directions, guiding the watershed to focus on salient ridges. Exte

6182003edce4bf567080f6f6bcff40209435b741.title: Heart Sounds Spectrogram: An Efficient Detection Tool for Depression
6182003edce4bf567080f6f6bcff40209435b741.abstract: Depression, a major mental health disorder, significantly affects individuals' quality of life and societal productivity. Early detection is critical in mitigating its impact on mental and physical health. This paper introduces a novel framework for depression detection based on heart sound spectrogram analysis. Heart sound recordings were segmented into uniform intervals and transformed into spectrograms, capturing essential acoustic properties associated with depression. Pre-trained deep learning models, including EfficientNetB0, ResNet-50, and VGG-19, were fine-tuned to classify depression using these spectrograms. Experimental results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed framework, with EfficientNetB0 achieving a classification accuracy of 94 % on training and 87.06 % on the test set. This study highlights the potential of heart sound analysis as a non-invasive, cost-

6103fc2ab7ebb24cc951c688604194abdee6817a.title: A Unified Deep Learning Pipeline for Placental Morphometric and Phenotypic Mapping in Gestational Diabetes
6103fc2ab7ebb24cc951c688604194abdee6817a.abstract: This study investigated morphometric differences in placentas from gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) pregnancies by integrating deep learning with quantitative statistical analysis. Whole slide images (WSIs) of placentas from four pathological groups: small-for-gestational-age (SGA), appropriate-for-gestational-age (AGA), large-for-gestational-age (LGA), and non-GDM pregnancies were analyzed to evaluate cell type distributions, morphology, and connectivity. A state-of-the-art benchmark model was used for comparison. This pipeline produced plausible cell maps and revealed significant cell-type-specific differences across groups. SGA placentas showed reduced vascular myocyte connectivity, and AGA placentas maintained robust cellular interactions. LGA and non-GDM placentas showed intermediate or compensatory remodeling patterns. These results highlight the potential of morphometric analys

60ffcaf430eef37a44f342ff80c069180578ffa8.title: Joint Segmentation and Grading with Iterative Optimization for Multimodal Glaucoma Diagnosis
60ffcaf430eef37a44f342ff80c069180578ffa8.abstract: Accurate diagnosis of glaucoma is challenging, as earlystage changes are subtle and often lack clear structural or appearance cues. Most existing approaches rely on a single modality, such as fundus or optical coherence tomography (OCT), capturing only partial pathological information and often missing early disease progression. In this paper, we propose an iterative multimodal optimization model (IMO) for joint segmentation and grading. IMO integrates fundus and OCT features through a mid-level fusion strategy, enhanced by a cross-modal feature alignment (CMFA) module to reduce modality discrepancies. An iterative refinement decoder progressively optimizes the multimodal features through a denoising diffusion mechanism, enabling fine-grained segmentation of the optic disc and cup while supporting accurate glaucoma grading. Extensive experiments show that our method effectively integrate

60deb1e0a1c3842a4fc4fdb27193d24b51246532.title: Semi-Supervised Learning for Congenital Heart Disease Prediction in Fetal Echocardiography
60deb1e0a1c3842a4fc4fdb27193d24b51246532.abstract: Fetal echocardiography is widely used for prenatal congenital heart disease (CHD) screening, but automated analysis is difficult due to strong speckle noise, large view variation, and severe class imbalance. This challenge evaluates semisupervised anatomical segmentation and multi-label CHD classification, and the final ranking is a weighted combination of classification score, segmentation score, and processing time. We propose a two-stage pipeline. We first segment viewspecific cardiac structures to obtain an anatomical mask. We then perform multi-label CHD classification with a patch-andglobal framework using a self-supervised Vision Transformer backbone. The predicted mask guides region-of-interest patch sampling and provides weak conditioning features, while view-aware constraints suppress view-incompatible labels to reduce false positives. Experiments are conducted on 2,500 ultraso

608ecdd8a5036ff4358ac72931f9642ca0847657.title: A Unified Multi-Task Learning Framework for Ultrasound Image Analysis
608ecdd8a5036ff4358ac72931f9642ca0847657.abstract: Ultrasound imaging involves diverse anatomical targets and variable acquisition settings, which complicates the creation of broadly applicable analytical tools. Conventional deep learning approaches are often narrowly tailored to individual tasks, which restricts their potential to serve as versatile foundation models in clinical contexts. In response, the Foundation Model Challenge for Ultrasound Image Analysis (FMC_UIA) 2026 establishes a comprehensive benchmark aggregating 27 distinct tasks-including segmentation, classification, detection, and regression. This paper describes our proposed solution for FMC_UIA 2026, which adopts a unified Multi-Head Multi-Task Learning (MH-MTL) architecture with hard parameter sharing. A MiT-B5 backbone pre-trained on ImageNet provides rich feature representations. For different tasks, we use multiple task heads for prediction, and we use a routing me

60170f6f1c4cc3deb29ae85b76ced8f64ab46ada.title: Joint Multiscale Image Learning for Segmentation in Macroscopic and Microscopic Pathology Images
60170f6f1c4cc3deb29ae85b76ced8f64ab46ada.abstract: Image segmentation at both macroscopic and microscopic level is important in digital pathology. In these images, visually similar regions within the same image often share semantic characteristics, offering an opportunity for intra-image reference learning. We propose a novel binary segmentation framework using a joint multiscale image learning strategy. Our approach builds upon a whole image segmentation model and introduces a complementary part level module that enables mutual referencing among image regions. By computing the feature similarity, each target part image identifies its corresponding reference part images. Cross-attention is then applied between the target and reference part images to exchange information. This strategy not only enhances segmentation consistency but also increases the effective training sample size, improving generalization in small datasets. The proposed

5fc8754dfbd56d5e8f9ef65b309223026f944747.title: Adaptive Gradient Domain Normalization for One-Sided Unsupervised Medical Image Synthesis
5fc8754dfbd56d5e8f9ef65b309223026f944747.abstract: Unsupervised image-to-image translation plays a crucial role in medical imaging, enabling data harmonization and crossmodality synthesis without paired data. Existing approaches, including CycleGAN, UNIT, and CUT, often fail to preserve fine anatomical details, limiting their applicability for clinical use. In this work, we develop a novel one-sided unsupervised image-to-image translation method - Adaptive Normalized Gradient Field (AdaNGF) - which enforces structural consistency throughout the translation process. We adapt the normalization of the gradient field of the generated image to match the target gradient magnitude distribution, encouraging the generator towards anatomically-sound outputs with appropriate preservation or suppression of local gradient alignment. 5f88c542a21be3d157b143c6b418a75436dab6ee.title: Multi-Scale Attention Framework with Transformer Architecture for Explainable Chest X-Ray Report Generation
5f88c542a21be3d157b143c6b418a75436dab6ee.abstract: Automated chest X-ray (CXR) report generation addresses the critical shortage of radiologists while improving diagnostic efficiency. We propose an enhanced deep learning framework integrating multi-scale attention mechanisms with transformer-based architectures for clinically accurate and explainable radiology report generation. Our model employs EfficientNetB3 with spatial and channel attention modules, coupled with a multi-layer transformer decoder optimized for medical text generation. Comprehensive experiments on the MIMIC-CXR dataset demonstrate superior performance (BLEU-1: 0.418, BLEU-4: 0.195, ROUGE-L: 0.321) while providing interpretable attention visualizations highlighting diagnostically relevant regions. The integrated explainability framework makes our approach suitable for clinical deployment and decision support systems.

5ef9beff915a3916597ce47712d47e05a84c627e.title: Making 3D Diffusion Easier: Autocalibration-Signal-Conditioned Diffusion Model for Dynamic Mri Reconstruction
5ef9beff915a3916597ce47712d47e05a84c627e.abstract: Highly accelerated dynamic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reconstruction is urgently needed to enable timeefficient and patient-friendly imaging. Diffusion models show great promise with their flexibility and robustness at high acceleration factors. However, the complexity and instability of high-dimensional diffusion often force existing approaches to decompose the natural 3D spatiotemporal problem into multiple 2D sub-problems, limiting their ability to capture the full 3D data distribution. In this work, we propose DiffACS, an autocalibration-signal (ACS)conditioned 3D diffusion model that bridges this gap by incorporating ACS information into the diffusion process via the element-wise cross-attention. 5ea7227a6ec1f2874b2fee8c8e5c7b410a493b44.title: Medvisiochat: A Multimodal Large Language Model Framework for Interpretable Diagnosis with Visual Grounding in CXRs
5ea7227a6ec1f2874b2fee8c8e5c7b410a493b44.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have enhanced the interpretability of disease diagnosis, leading to more accurate outcomes and improved patient understanding. A key advancement is visual grounding, linking textual information with medical images like chest x-rays (CXRs) for deeper analysis. This approach combines visual details with expert medical language, enabling MLLMs to detect patterns and disease indicators effectively. However, challenges persist, particularly in multi-category classification and precise visual grounding in CXRs. To address this, we introduce MedVisioChat, an MLLM with visual grounding capabilities for seamless integration of medical images and diagnoses. Pre-trained on large datasets and fine-tuned with specific GPT-4 Turbo instructions, MedVisioChat aims to provide accurate, interactive diagnostics, demonstrating superiority over existing models and pro

5e1cd0bdeb7b199fd8bf5219bd61e5a26e364676.title: Cross-Harmonic MPI Restoration via Generative Models
5e1cd0bdeb7b199fd8bf5219bd61e5a26e364676.abstract: Magnetic Particle Imaging (MPI) offers high-sensitivity, radiation-free biomedical imaging by detecting the nonlinear response of superparamagnetic nanoparticles. However, a fundamental trade-off limits its potential: while higher-order harmonics encode fine spatial details, their rapid signal decay severely compromises the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), especially at low particle concentrations. We propose a generative restoration framework to dissociate spatial resolution from this intrinsic SNR degradation. Instead of relying on noisy high-harmonic measurements, our approach reconstructs high-fidelity images by learning a mapping from robust, low-harmonic inputs to high-harmonic targets. By employing diffusion and flow-based models, we capture the statistical transformation between these signal domains. Rather than struggling with highly corrupted measurements, our approach capitalizes

5dcb9a7265605060704aa69fe67d47eba0dca9cc.title: BEFNet: Boundary-Enhanced Fusion Network for Early Esophageal Cancer Segmentation
5dcb9a7265605060704aa69fe67d47eba0dca9cc.abstract: Accurate segmentation of Early Esophageal Cancer (EEC) lesions is critical for clinical diagnosis and treatment planning. However, this task remains challenging due to the poorly defined boundaries of such lesions. To address this issue, we propose BEFNet, a novel segmentation network tailored for EEC. The main contributions of this work are threefold: (1) We design a Boundary Enhancement Module (BEM) that extracts and refines ambiguous lesion boundaries from multiscale backbone features. (2) We introduce a Dynamic Focusing and Mining Module (DFMM) to hierarchically integrate encoder features at different stages, effectively mitigating the semantic gap between shallow and deep layers. (3) We develop a Boundary-aware Contextual Attention Module (BCAM) to comprehensively fuse all decoder features with boundary priors for precise final prediction. Extensive experiments on a challenging publ

5c830767b122766552fa657a20d606f1d1fdb3d4.title: DeltaSegment: Multifidelity Medical Image Segmentation via Change Detection
5c830767b122766552fa657a20d606f1d1fdb3d4.abstract: We propose DeltaSegment, a lightweight, data-efficient framework for medical image segmentation that leverages multifidelity modeling and change detection. Differences between low-fidelity and high-fidelity images enable learning from fewer labeled samples. For each original, high-fidelity input image, we generate a coarse-grained, color-quantized version as a low-fidelity input. These paired inputs are then processed by a Semi-Siamese neural network trained end-to-end to predict segmentation maps, encouraging focus on salient morphological differences and boundary details critical for accurate segmentation. DeltaSegment achieves relative improvements of 1.3% in Dice and 2.3% in IoU on GlaS, 1.5% in Dice and 2.4% in IoU on MoNuSeg, and 1.3% in Dice and 1.7% in IoU on TNBC, demonstrating a simple yet effective approach that harnesses multifidelity change detection as a paradigm for small-

5c1b3ddf951519df50de0103a71d28863cc43d62.title: Abdominal Segmentation and Blood Vessel Detection in CTA Scans for Diep Reconstruction Procedures
5c1b3ddf951519df50de0103a71d28863cc43d62.abstract: Deep Inferior Epigastric Perforator (DIEP) flap reconstruction requires precise identification of perforator vessels traversing the abdominal muscle to supply the fat and skin tissues. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) reveals contrast-enhanced blood vessels critical for the DIEP surgical harvesting selection. CTA annotation is time-consuming and expertise-dependent, requiring clinicians to trace small perforator vessels through hundreds of image slices. We present an end-to-end automated pipeline that receives raw CTA scans and performs ROI extraction, deep learning multi-class segmentation and detection of perforation points. The pipeline achieves effective segmentation with reliable detection of critical anatomical landmarks. It can reduce pre-operative preparation time while maintaining clinical accuracy for improved surgical planning and navigation.

5bc7631f6330ad53e950d6a12d273b9a01c4a39d.title: Generative AI for Overcoming Rf Data Inaccessibility in Quantitative Ultrasound Imaging
5bc7631f6330ad53e950d6a12d273b9a01c4a39d.abstract: Quantitative ultrasound (QUS) imaging enables noninvasive tissue characterization using frequency-dependent parameters derived from raw radiofrequency (RF) data. However, the limited accessibility to RF data, particularly in commercial scanners, restricts its clinical use. This study adapts a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) to synthesize RF data from conventional B-mode images, addressing this limitation. A large paired dataset of B-mode and RF signals acquired from 152 patients with benign and malignant breast lesions was used for training and evaluation. Quantitative pixel-level metrics were employed to assess reconstruction fidelity, while histograms of QUS parametric map mean-values as well as the attenuation coefficient estimates derived from the original and synthetic RF data were analyzed for distributional agreement. The synthesized RF data showed close similari

5b4f2b8cbac44978393ba48388cac4804dec7632.title: CP-MIL: Class Prototype-Based Multiple Instance Learning for Lung Cancer Subtype Classification and Interpretability in Whole Slide Images
5b4f2b8cbac44978393ba48388cac4804dec7632.abstract: Accurate subtype classification of lung cancer from whole slide images (WSIs) remains difficult due to subtle morphological overlap between subtypes and the computational burden of gigapixel pathology data. We propose CP-MIL (Class Prototype-based Multiple Instance Learning), an end-to-end framework that integrates contextaware instance modeling with class prototype learning for accurate and interpretable slide-level predictions. From WSI patch embeddings, CP-MIL performs lightweight dimensionality reduction to obtain compact, discriminative features. An Instance Attention (IA) module generates a slide-level context vector through attention pooling and feeds this information back to patch embeddings to create contextualized representations. Using these embeddings, the Prototype Learning and Aggregation (PLA) module learns class-specific prototypes and assesses evidential support via cosi

59f400dbccf48e6d22ca3229e52c9153c1691511.title: Beyond the Last Scan: The Role of Longitudinal Neuroimaging in Predicting Conversion to Alzheimer's Disease at Different Stages
59f400dbccf48e6d22ca3229e52c9153c1691511.abstract: The application of deep learning models to neuroimaging data has proven to be a powerful approach for understanding and predicting the progression of Alzheimer's disease (AD). A critical factor in improving prediction accuracy lies in in-corporating longitudinal information into these models. Previous approaches integrated longitudinal neuroimaging data from time steps in the future, and evaluated their re-sults on a single heterogeneous group of MCI subjects, con-taining MCI converters (MCI-C) at different stages of disease progression. In this study, we investigate the impact of incorporating past longitudinal neuroimaging information into deep learning models to predict the conversion from mild cognitive im-pairment (MCI) to Alzheimer's disease, and we evaluate our results for different MCI groups with converters at different stages of the disease. We demonstrate that incorporating pa

593a646b87f4815d461c3f67f06122c13fa3c842.title: Patchsurg: Leveraging Synthetic Datasets for High-Fidelity Depth Estimation in Surgery
593a646b87f4815d461c3f67f06122c13fa3c842.abstract: Acquiring accurate real-world monocular depth data in surgery is often infeasible. Widely used synthetic datasets can provide accurate ground truth labels, however, these do not reflect variabilities in real-world surgery. To address this limitation, we aim to leverage high-fidelity synthetic depth data and transfer this understanding to diverse surgical dataset. To achieve this, we introduce a novel efficient teacher-student architecture, namely “PatchSurg”. Our PatchSurg exploits the structural details in synthetic datasets and transfers it to realworld cases by mitigating the domain gap between synthetic and real-world data, using a detail and scale disentangling technique. Furthermore, we utilise a pose prediction network that processes temporally adjacent frames to enhance temporal consistency in depth estimation. In terms of root mean squared error, our novel PatchSurg method achie

57a5cce9b55a9aa1581b86d620b5c4feeffa75e6.title: DINOV3-Guided Cross Fusion Framework for Semantic-Aware CT Generation From MRI and CBCT
57a5cce9b55a9aa1581b86d620b5c4feeffa75e6.abstract: Generating synthetic CT images from CBCT or MRI has a potential for efficient radiation dose planning and adaptive radiotherapy. However, existing CNN-based models lack global semantic understanding, while Transformers often overfit small medical datasets due to high model capacity and weak inductive bias. To address these limitations, we propose a DINOv3-Guided Cross Fusion (DGCF) framework that integrates a frozen self-supervised DINOv3 Transformer with a trainable CNN encoder-decoder. It hierarchically fuses global representation of Transformer and local features of CNN via a learnable cross fusion module, achieving balanced local appearance and contextual representation. Furthermore, we introduce a Multi-Level DINOv3 Perceptual (MLDP) loss that encourages semantic similarity between synthetic CT and the ground truth in DINOv3's feature space.
