5744defd7d63267bf03be4669a140ace1a100466.title: Rethinking Slide-Level Adaptation of Pathology Foundation Models
5744defd7d63267bf03be4669a140ace1a100466.abstract: The emergence of pathology foundation models (PFMs) has transformed histopathological image analysis, replacing conventional image encoders pretrained on natural images and becoming the mainstream feature extractor for patches in whole slide images (WSIs). To perform slide-level analysis, multiple instance learning (MIL) remains the dominant paradigm. However, such approaches rely on task-specific slide-level representations, which often lack generality and carry a risk of feature overfitting. Another simple way is to directly aggregate patch features into a slide representation via training-free pooling methods. Nevertheless, before the advent of PFMs, such approaches generally performed poorly. In this work, we demonstrate that task-agnostic slide representations, aggregated via mean pooling of PFM-derived patch features, can successfully support a wide range of WSI classification simp

5736207a30feedcec8a24259d5de341ee0e0ee37.title: DPANet: Dual-Path Prior-Guided Attention Network for Few-Shot Intravascular Ultrasound Segmentation
5736207a30feedcec8a24259d5de341ee0e0ee37.abstract: Intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) is a key modality for early detection of coronary artery disease, enabling the assessment of vessel morphology and plaque burden by delineating the lumen and the external elastic membrane (EEM). However, low contrast, blurred boundaries between lumen and EEM, and scarce expert annotations make accurate IVUS segmentation difficult. We propose DPANet, a Dual-Path Prior-guided Attention Network for Few-Shot IVUS Segmentation. DPANet combines (1) a prior-guided difference reconstruction path that independently segments the lumen and lumen+EEM regions, then recovers the EEM via set difference to sharpen boundaries in low-contrast areas; and (2) an Iterative Prototype Refinement (IPR) module whose Cross-Attention Aggregation Module (CAAM) dynamically aligns prototypes with spatial features, improving generalisation under few-shot supervision. Experiments on a pr

545ca1f2d8c6603db820408129298a7aca83345a.title: GAZE2REPORT: RADIOLOGY REPORT GENERATION VIA VISUAL-GAZE PROMPT TUNING OF LLMS
545ca1f2d8c6603db820408129298a7aca83345a.abstract: Existing deep learning methods for radiology report generation enhance diagnostic efficiency but often overlook physician-informed medical priors. This leads to a suboptimal alignment between the structured explanations and disease manifestations. Eye gaze data provides critical insights into a radiologist's visual attention, enhancing the relevance and interpretability of extracted features while aligning with human decision-making processes. However, despite its promising potential, the integration of eye gaze information into AI-driven medical imaging workflows is impeded by challenges such as the complexity of multimodal data fusion and the high cost of gaze acquisition, particularly its absence during inference, limiting its practical applicability in real-world clinical settings. To address these issues, we introduce Gaze2Report, a framework which leverages a scanpath prediction mo

54594fe4179f64000c316c027a404a7cc6a43caa.title: An Attentive Representative Sample Selection Strategy Combined with Balanced Batch Training for Skin Lesion Segmentation
54594fe4179f64000c316c027a404a7cc6a43caa.abstract: An often overlooked problem in medical image segmentation research is the effective selection of training subsets to annotate from a complete set of unlabelled data. Many studies select their training sets at random, which may lead to suboptimal model performance, especially in the minimal supervision setting where each training image has a profound effect on performance outcomes. This work aims to address this issue. We use prototypical contrasting learning and clustering to extract representative and diverse samples for annotation. We improve upon prior works with a bespoke cluster-based image selection process. Additionally, we introduce the concept of unsupervised balanced batch dataloading to medical image segmentation, which aims to improve model learning with minimally annotated data. 537d67c33c3eecf79a43e3ace5cfffe9fcdf1d1d.title: Pulmofusion: Advancing Pulmonary Health with Efficient Multi-Modal Fusion
537d67c33c3eecf79a43e3ace5cfffe9fcdf1d1d.abstract: Traditional remote spirometry lacks the precision required for effective pulmonary monitoring. We present a novel, non-invasive approach using multimodal predictive models that integrate RGB or thermal video data with patient meta-data. Our method leverages energy-efficient Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) for the regression of Peak Expiratory Flow (PEF) and classification of Forced Expiratory Volume (FEVl) and Forced Vital Capacity (FVC), using lightweight CNNs to overcome SNN limitations in regression tasks. Multimodal data integration is improved with a Multi-Head Attention Layer, and we employ K-Fold validation and en-semble learning to boost robustness. Using thermal data, our SNN models achieve 92% ± 2% accuracy on a breathing-cycle basis and 99.5% ± 0.5% patient-wise. 5370da6239224f6abd19c2170e25ee652b9f7a72.title: Enhancing Mammogram-Based Breast Cancer Prediction From Pretrained Vision-Language Models: the Role of Soft Prompts and Bidirectional Fusion
5370da6239224f6abd19c2170e25ee652b9f7a72.abstract: Recent advances in vision-language models (VLMs) such as CLIP and BLIP have demonstrated strong generalization in visual reasoning tasks. However, their potential for medical image analysis, especially breast cancer prediction from mammograms, remains underexplored. This study investigates how a pretrained VLM can be adapted for full mammographic classification. Unlike prior approaches that rely on costly region-of-interest (ROI) annotations, we process entire mammograms and adapt a general-purpose VLM (EVACLIP) using soft prompts, selective fine-tuning, and bidirectional fusion strategies. We compare different fusion methods, including Concatenation, Gated-Residual, Cross-Modal, Co-Weighted and Bi-Attention. Experiments on the CBISDDSM dataset show that bidirectional fusion methods consistently outperform other fusion approaches, while providing enhanced explainability through improved

535566c35f6a05ae738045f845afe98a8db589be.title: RAA-MIL: A Novel Framework for Classification of Oral Cytology
535566c35f6a05ae738045f845afe98a8db589be.abstract: Cytology is a valuable tool for early detection of oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC). However, manual examination of cytology whole slide images (WSIs) is slow, subjective, and depends heavily on expert pathologists. To address this, we introduce the first weakly supervised deep learning framework for patient-level diagnosis of oral cytology whole slide images, leveraging the newly released Oral Cytology Dataset [1], which provides annotated cytology WSIs from ten medical centres across India. Each patient case is represented as a bag of cytology patches and assigned a diagnosis label (Healthy, Benign, Oral Potentially Malignant Disorders (OPMD), OSCC) by an in-house expert pathologist. These patient-level weak labels form a new extension to the dataset. We evaluate a baseline multiple-instance learning (MIL) model and a proposed Region-Affinity Attention MIL (RAA-MIL) that models spat

52e0101d6ef5d9e1e017134f8294aa28efdbbec0.title: Frugal-Combat: An Ultra-Low-Sample Diffusion MRI Harmonization Method
52e0101d6ef5d9e1e017134f8294aa28efdbbec0.abstract: MRI is highly sensitive to site-specific acquisition conditions (e.g., scanner models, protocols). To avoid unwanted biases, multicentric studies require a harmonization step to mitigate these scanner-specific effects. One widely used method is ComBat, which has proven effective when a sufficiently large number of subjects per site, preferably healthy controls (HC), are available to ensure reliable statistical estimation. In clinical practice, however, sites want to scan very few HC subjects, making a blind application of ComBat unreliable and potentially leading to erroneous harmonization. We introduce Frugal-ComBat, a Bayesian method that leverages well-populated third-party sites to augment a given site's population by integrating information from a broader community. 52d888b12e4eb1aa89a3ff58a56467af42d150f4.title: Disdiff: Self-Supervised Segmentation on Histopathology Images Using Diffusion Models and Distance Maps
52d888b12e4eb1aa89a3ff58a56467af42d150f4.abstract: Histopathological image segmentation is crucial for clinical diagnosis, but obtaining high-quality annotations is timeconsuming and labor-intensive. To improve segmentation performance while reducing annotation dependence, this paper presents DisDiff, a novel two-stage self-supervised framework leveraging diffusion models for nuclei segmentation without pseudo-labels. In the first stage, a Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM) with Perception Prioritized (P2) weighting learns robust features from unlabeled images. In the second stage, pretrained weights are transferred to a U-Net enhanced with Efficient Multi-scale Attention (EMA) and distance map post-processing for effective nuclei separation. 5183faa11148509868907492bf987d7c75d6814f.title: Unified Ultrasound Intelligence Toward an End-to-End Agentic System
5183faa11148509868907492bf987d7c75d6814f.abstract: Clinical ultrasound analysis demands models that generalize across heterogeneous organs, views, and devices, while supporting interpretable workflow-level analysis. Existing methods often rely on task-wise adaptation, and joint learning may be unstable due to cross-task interference, making it hard to deliver workflow-level outputs in practice. To address these challenges, we present USTri, a tri-stage ultrasound intelligence pipeline for unified multi-organ, multi-task analysis. Stage I trains a universal generalist USGen on different domains to learn broad, transferable priors that are robust to device and protocol variability. To better handle domain shifts and reach task-aligned performance while preserving ultrasound shared knowledge, Stage II builds USpec by keeping USGen frozen and finetuning dataset-specific heads. 517c3e2fc5e5c863b1c202a109b0f9ea4ca5269c.title: Conformal Coronary Calcification Volume Estimation with Conditional Coverage via Histogram Clustering
517c3e2fc5e5c863b1c202a109b0f9ea4ca5269c.abstract: Incidental detection and quantification of coronary calcium in CT scans could lead to the early introduction of lifesaving clinical interventions. However, over-reporting could negatively affect patient wellbeing and unnecessarily burden the medical system. Therefore, careful considerations should be taken when automatically reporting coronary calcium scores. A cluster-based conditional conformal prediction framework is proposed to provide score intervals with calibrated coverage from trained segmentation networks without retraining. The proposed method was tuned and used to calibrate predictive intervals for 3D UNet models (deterministic, MCDropout and deep ensemble) reaching similar coverage with better triage metrics compared to conventional conformal prediction. 50e21ce79e751c36ad53e354f7f473205c8c55f6.title: Knee Joint Registration Based on Chart and Learnable Superpoint Match
50e21ce79e751c36ad53e354f7f473205c8c55f6.abstract: Registration between the segmented and captured point clouds of the knee is the basic for the alignment of preoperative images with intraoperative patient in total knee arthroplasty navigation. The state-of-the-art point cloud registration methods uniformly or randomly select superpoints to employ a coarse-to-fine registration strategy. Due to the uneven density of shape features in different parts for the knee joint, this selection cannot fully utilize the topological information of bone point cloud. Moreover, the relatively low overlap between the preoperative complete point cloud and the intraoperative partial point cloud makes the accurate registration hard. A point cloud registration method based on chart and learnable superpoint match is proposed in this paper. 50090a65d0d7c0f4fd2200315dcce9f9fe722cdb.title: Semi-Supervised Carotid Plaque Segmentation with Multi-Scale Deep Supervision and Consistency Learning for Multi-View Vulnerable Plaque Classification
50090a65d0d7c0f4fd2200315dcce9f9fe722cdb.abstract: Carotid plaque vulnerability is closely associated with cerebrovascular events, making accurate plaque analysis important for clinical risk assessment. In this study, we propose a framework for automated carotid ultrasound plaque analysis integrating semi-supervised segmentation and classification. A multi-scale deeply supervised dual-view DenseNet model with a UniMatch-based semi-supervised strategy was used for plaque segmentation, enabling effective utilization of labeled and unlabeled data. Radiomic features extracted from plaque, lumen, and union regions were used for vulnerable plaque classification with TabPFN and semi-supervised training. 4fabcae1e31bcbd298e721e8b7759b284c72e744.title: Latent Diffusion-Based Visual-Textual Fusion for Survival and Recurrence Prediction of Colorectal Liver Metastases
4fabcae1e31bcbd298e721e8b7759b284c72e744.abstract: Colorectal cancer is one of the most prevalent malignancies worldwide, with liver metastases (CLM) critically impacting patient outcomes. Current prediction models for CLM typically rely on whole slide images (WSIs) and clinical data, rather than fully integrating heterogeneous data sources such as pathology reports, which limits their ability to predict patient outcomes accurately. We introduce a novel multimodal framework for the survival and recurrence prediction of CLM that leverages latent diffusion models (LDMs) and large language models (LLMs), combining visual and textual information. Our approach integrates dual-resolution WSIs with detailed pathology reports to predict critical clinical endpoints, namely Time-to-Recurrence (TTR) and overall survival (OS). 4ea334e5659699161d46485296439c8c3234521b.title: Unified PET Image Enhancement for Diverse Degradation Levels with Mixture-Of-Experts and Dynamic Prompts
4ea334e5659699161d46485296439c8c3234521b.abstract: Positron Emission Tomography (PET) images often suffer from suboptimal quality due to physical constraints and clinical trade-offs, such as radiation dose and scanning time. Thus, PET image enhancement using deep learning is of great importance. However, most existing methods are designed to handle a single degradation level and lack the flexibility to adapt to varying degrees of image degradation. Inspired by this direction, this paper proposes a unified model for enhancing PET images under various degradation conditions, including varying doses and scanning times. 4e03745d0d643187b0e34fe1f34c1726b9db8085.title: Multi-Task Ensemble Learning for Endoscopic Ulcerative Colitis Severity Grading
4e03745d0d643187b0e34fe1f34c1726b9db8085.abstract: Accurate endoscopic grading of Ulcerative Colitis (UC) is critical for clinical decision-making but remains subjective. We present our solution for the IEEE ISBI 2026 EndoUC Challenge, addressing Mayo Endoscopic Score (MES) classification (4 classes) and UCEIS score classification (9 classes). Our approach combines a ConvNeXt-Base backbone with multitask auxiliary supervision using UCEIS sub-component annotations, a Class-Distance Weighted Cross-Entropy (CDW-CE) loss respecting ordinal structure, and 5-fold ensemble with 7-variant test-time augmentation. 4d0dbe19c8f24041adc837dda4bcacdc4f236ba7.title: Medical Small Object Detection Algorithm Based on Multi-Scale Frequency Domain Enhancement and Cross-Attention Fusion
4d0dbe19c8f24041adc837dda4bcacdc4f236ba7.abstract: Medical Small Object Detection (MSOD) can assist in lesion localization, cell identification, and drug development. While deep learning-based methods have made progress in this field in recent years, they still face significant limitations in detection accuracy and speed. 4cb76757dd7e2a7e3d2c9381020cd6f6b6d9f856.title: Federated Few-Shot Segmentation for Rare Brain Tumours via Weighted Aggregation and Prototype-Guided Adaptation
4cb76757dd7e2a7e3d2c9381020cd6f6b6d9f856.abstract: Brain tumour segmentation is a fundamental task for neurooncological diagnosis and treatment planning. However, the scarcity of annotated data for rarer tumour types such as metastases limits the applicability of deep learning models. 4c9d3c9ed5dc98dfa07953758171223335784ce3.title: Beyond Dichotomization: Ordinal Prediction of Functional Stroke Outcomes from 4D CTP and Clinical Metadata Using Deep Learning
4c9d3c9ed5dc98dfa07953758171223335784ce3.abstract: Predicting functional outcomes after acute ischemic stroke is critical for prognosis and treatment planning, as it could help identify patients most likely to benefit from interventions. These outcomes are typically measured by the 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS90), a seven-level disability score. However, most deep learning models for functional outcome prediction reduce this to a binary variable, losing information about intermediate recovery levels and limiting clinical interpretability. So far, only a few studies have attempted to model the full mRS90 range using multiclass classification, ignoring the ordered nature of the scale. 4c61d3b6a6ed308ba4461e27691307a325f59a4e.title: Bonnet: Ultra-Fast Whole-Body Bone Segmentation from CT Scans
4c61d3b6a6ed308ba4461e27691307a325f59a4e.abstract: This work proposes Bonnet, an ultra-fast sparse-volume pipeline for whole-body bone segmentation from CT scans. 4beb38174b6eed1b6a492747008e34e7a8c171b2.title: Artifact Correction and Quality Assessment via Perceptual Contrastive Learning on Diffusion MRI
4beb38174b6eed1b6a492747008e34e7a8c171b2.abstract: Diffusion MRI is crucial for examining the microstructure of brain tissues, which are often affected by artifacts such as ghosting and motion distortions that hinder analysis. This work proposes a novel framework for joint artifact correction and quality assessment based on perceptual contrast. This framework integrates two stages of artifact correction and no-reference quality evaluation at the 3D layer level. In the first stage, we utilize an enhanced 3D U-Net architecture with Leaky ReLU activation and trilinear up-sampling. A hybrid perceptual loss function combining NMAE and HaarPSI is employed to effectively correct artifacts across 4D DWI data, yielding high-fidelity images. In the second stage, we construct a pseudo-reference by extracting low-level voxel-level similarity features and high-level perceptual features from the pre- and post-corrected data. Support Vector Machine tec

4b730406bfe0a00816b43a97de736994ca958766.title: Preserving Anatomical Continuity: Three-Stage Pipeline for Colon Segmentation in 3D Abdominal CT Scans
4b730406bfe0a00816b43a97de736994ca958766.abstract: Accurate colon segmentation from CT images is essential for colorectal disease analysis, yet deep learning based methods often produce disconnected predictions due to complex anatomy. This study introduces a three-stage, topologypreserving segmentation pipeline to address this issue. The first stage performs initial deep learning-based segmentation, followed by centreline bridging to reconnect disjoint regions and a reconstruction stage to refine continuity. Evaluations on TotalSegmentator and RAOS datasets using overlap, distance and topology-based metrics demonstrate improved structural consistency while maintaining segmentation accuracy. The proposed method enhances topological integrity, enabling more reliable colon segmentation for clinical and research applications.

4aafa5feec58f05e00ba4b9b81be01c7e2a69833.title: Uncertainty-Guided Generation of Dark-Field Radiographs
4aafa5feec58f05e00ba4b9b81be01c7e2a69833.abstract: X-ray dark-field radiography provides complementary diagnostic information to conventional attenuation imaging by visualizing microstructural tissue changes through small-angle scattering. However, the limited availability of such data poses challenges for developing robust deep learning models. In this work, we present the first framework for generating dark-field images directly from standard attenuation chest X-rays using an Uncertainty-Guided Progressive Generative Adversarial Network. The model incorporates both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty to improve interpretability and reliability. Experiments demonstrate high structural fidelity of the generated images, with consistent improvement of quantitative metrics across stages. Furthermore, out-of-distribution evaluation confirms that the proposed model generalizes well. Our results indicate that uncertainty-guided generative mode

4a65292bd0bb081e419e5b09c95937afb3b11f0f.title: Brain Topology-Driven Graph Structure Learning for Functional Brain Network-Based Major Depressive Disorder Diagnosis
4a65292bd0bb081e419e5b09c95937afb3b11f0f.abstract: Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging is widely used to analyze abnormal brain activity in Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) by modeling the brain as a graph. Recent graph-based approaches employ graph structure learning (GSL), which adaptively infers connectivity among brain regions from data, aiming to identify subtle disease-related alterations. However, existing GSL methods rarely account for an essential characteristic of brain organization, the smallworld network, which reflects local specialization and efficient global integration. Motivated by this limitation, we propose the Small-world Pattern Aware Reconstructed networK (SPARK), a dual-geometry GSL framework designed to incorporate this property into learned structures. SPARK first enriches node representations through biased random walks, capturing multi-scale dependencies across regions. Building on these represen

4a4fc2c0e617ba9b76ce54263b8ada34ac25c094.title: Toward Modality-Robust Brain Tumor Segmentation: Distilling Foundation Models for Incomplete Mri Scans
4a4fc2c0e617ba9b76ce54263b8ada34ac25c094.abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) plays a critical role in brain tumor diagnosis and segmentation. Recent medical foundation models have demonstrated strong performance in full-modality brain tumor segmentation by jointly utilizing multiple MRI sequences. However, in clinical practice, missing modalities caused by patient motion, contrast agent intolerance, or acquisition constraints often lead to degraded segmentation accuracy. To address this issue, we propose TSFMD, a two-stage framework for brain Tumor Segmentation under missing-modality conditions via Foundation Model Distillation. In the first stage, the student model is pre-trained under the guidance of BrainSegFounder using a Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA)-based distillation strategy. In the second stage, the student model is finetuned for tumor segmentation. Extensive experiments on the BraTS2020 dataset demonstrate that our met

49a71bee1e5f2265e7d13ea977c456efd50a603f.title: Quantitative and Qualitative Assessment of Generative AI for Cross-Modal CT-to-MRI Translation in Spine Imaging
49a71bee1e5f2265e7d13ea977c456efd50a603f.abstract: The application of Generative AI for cross-modal image-to-image translation holds significant potential in emergency care, particularly for spinal pathologies such as Cauda Equina Syndrome, where timely MRI access is often critical yet not always accessible. In such cases, synthetic MRI translated from the more readily available CT imaging could provide an interim solution to support clinical assessment. This study compares five generative methods for CT-to-MRI translation through both quantitative analysis using standard computer vision metrics and expert qualitative evaluation via a blinded randomised survey. The survey, delivered through a custom-designed web application, examined radiologists' perceptions of image quality, anatomical fidelity and diagnostic confidence. The findings reveal a clear disconnect between quantitative performance and clinical opinion, as models achieving th

4991d00f33168b740a77b1681936e188eb5d196f.title: DINO-MambaSeg: A Foundation-Guided Network for Patchy Atrophy Segmentation
4991d00f33168b740a77b1681936e188eb5d196f.abstract: Pathological myopia (PM) is a leading cause of irreversible vision loss, where patchy chorioretinal atrophy (PA) serves as a crucial biomarker of disease progression. Accurate segmentation of PA lesions remains challenging due to low contrast, irregular morphology, and limited annotations. To address these issues, we propose DINO-MambaSeg, a novel segmentation framework driven by foundation models. Our method integrates a frozen DINOv3 encoder with a hybrid Mamba-ASPP module for joint global-local feature refinement. Furthermore, we incorporate an optic disc exclusion prior into the loss function to suppress false positives and enhance anatomical plausibility. We also construct PA-Fundus, a new pixel-level annotated dataset dedicated to PA lesions. Extensive experiments on PA-Fundus demonstrate that DINO-MambaSeg achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and robustness, validating the effective

49166ebaebf449f4d81111b0c8186039d798e728.title: TA-MIR: Text Aggregation for Multimodal Feature Representation in Medical Image Registration
49166ebaebf449f4d81111b0c8186039d798e728.abstract: The aggregation of multimodal features in medical image registration remains underexplored, limiting the performance of current models in capturing complex anatomical relationships. Traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) often overlook the rich semantic information available from text, while existing approaches lack effective methods to combine spatial and contextual cues. In this paper, we propose Text Aggregation for Medical Image Registration (TA-MIR), a novel framework that enhances encoder-decoder architecture by incorporating anatomical text embeddings throughout the registration process. By employing large kernel blocks for improved receptive fields in U-Net and fusion blocks at each level, our model effectively integrates image features with semantic text information. Extensive experiments on three brain MRI datasets-OASIS, IXI, and LPBA40-demonstrate that our approach

4909e6a0db571f50ae51b51de2a5731af09050c0.title: End-to-End Mandibular Reconstruction with Integrated Repositioning and Completion Networks
4909e6a0db571f50ae51b51de2a5731af09050c0.abstract: Patients with mandibular defects require mandibular reconstruction surgery to restore both physiological function and facial morphology. Accurate preoperative planning relies on a complete mandible in its correct anatomical position. However, existing methods primarily focus on morphological completion, without considering anatomical repositioning, which can result in significant issues if the defective mandible is left in a compensatory malposition. This paper presents a novel end-to-end framework that jointly performs mandible repositioning and morphological completion. In the repositioning stage, we predict rigid transformations to restore the displaced mandible to its anatomically correct location. The completion stage then restores the repositioned mandible to its complete morphology. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method surpasses state-of-the-art approaches, showing st

48c6ac99e3ab5fff812567245181db545cb246e5.title: CSMAE : Cataract Surgical Masked Autoencoder (MAE) Based Pre-Training
48c6ac99e3ab5fff812567245181db545cb246e5.abstract: Automated analysis of surgical videos is crucial for improving surgical training, workflow optimization, and postoperative assessment. We introduce a CSMAE, Masked Autoencoder (MAE)-based pretraining approach, specifically developed for Cataract Surgery video analysis, where instead of randomly selecting tokens for Masking, they are selected based on spatiotemporal importance of the token. We created a large dataset of cataract surgery videos to improve the model's learning efficiency and expand its robustness in low-data regime. Our pre-trained model can be easily adapted for specific downstream tasks via fine-tuning, serving as a robust backbone for further analysis. Through rigorous testing on downstream steprecognition task on two Cataract surgery video datasets, D99 and Cataract-101our approach surpasses current state-of-the-art self-supervised pre-training and adapter-based transfe

48b2864c059e2002a0b06c061d0755e5faf206dc.title: Is Long Range Sequential Modeling Necessary for Colorectal Tumor Segmentation?
48b2864c059e2002a0b06c061d0755e5faf206dc.abstract: Segmentation of colorectal cancer (CRC) tumors in 3D medical imaging is both complex and clinically critical, providing vital support for effective radiation therapy planning and survival outcome assessment. Recently, 3D volumetric segmentation architectures incorporating long-range sequence modeling mechanisms, such as Transformers and Mamba, have gained attention for their capacity to achieve high accuracy in 3D medical image segmentation. In this work, we evaluate the effectiveness of these global token modeling techniques by pitting them against our proposed MambaOutUNet within the context of our newly introduced colorectal tumor segmentation dataset (CTS-204). Our findings suggest that robust local token interactions can outperform long-range modeling techniques in cases where the region of interest is small and anatomically complex, proposing a potential shift in 3D tumor segmentat

486d52299d6d9988d7dd26eb60913db367948c6c.title: Radiomics-Integrated Deep Learning With Hierarchical Loss for Osteosarcoma Histology Classification
486d52299d6d9988d7dd26eb60913db367948c6c.abstract: Osteosarcoma (OS) is an aggressive primary bone malignancy. Accurate histopathological assessment of viable versus non-viable tumor regions after neoadjuvant chemotherapy is critical for prognosis and treatment planning, yet manual evaluation remains labor-intensive, subjective, and prone to inter-observer variability. Recent advances in digital pathology have enabled automated necrosis quantification. Evaluating on test data, independently sampled on patientlevel, revealed that the deep learning model performance dropped significantly from the tile-level generalization ability reported in previous studies. First, this work proposes the use of radiomic features as additional input in model training. We show that, despite that they are derived from the images, such a multimodal input effectively improved the classification performance, in addition to its added benefits in interpretability

47abe1b357ae260b07f2d9a8624f6a6c477b1ae3.title: Illuminating Uncertainty: A Trifocal Fine-Grained and Transformer-Like Axial Attention Framework for Pulmonary Vascular Segmentation
47abe1b357ae260b07f2d9a8624f6a6c477b1ae3.abstract: Pulmonary artery segmentation has recently emerged as a novel biomarker for lung diseases, necessitating accurate and efficient automatic segmentation methods. However, in none contrast enhanced CT (NECT) scans, the low tissue contrast poses a persistent challenge for accurately delineating multibranch structures and small pulmonary arteries, particularly in complex pulmonary conditions. In this work, we introduce IFSAttUNet, a trifocal fine-grained attention framework enhanced by transformer-like triple-axis multi-head attention. This method provides an explicit measure for “uncertain” or “hard-to-recognize” regions, thereby guiding the network's focus toward artery boundaries. Moreover, IFSAttUNet features a lightweight architecture capable of capturing global dependencies effectively. Our empirical results demonstrate that IFSAttUNet outperforms state-of-the-art Gaussian-based fuzzy a

476de03185c366b1da8aa2b91876931aa3425e82.title: Hybrid-Projection with Subspace Recycling for Sequential and Limited-Angle CT: A Training-Free Baseline for Biomedical Imaging
476de03185c366b1da8aa2b91876931aa3425e82.abstract: Modern CT workflows in biomedical imaging increasingly involve sequences of closely related reconstruction tasks: repeated exams, multi-slice stacks, dynamic series, and geometry-constrained limited-angle acquisitions. While deep learning and unrolled variational networks have shown strong performance for sparse-view and low-dose CT, they rely on training data, protocol-specific tuning, and careful safeguards for robustness, which motivates fast, interpretable, training-free baselines that exploit sequential structure. We study hybrid-projection-based reconstruction with subspace recycling for 2D parallel-beam CT. Building on existing HyBR/HyBRrecycle solvers, we reuse Krylov subspaces across systems with shared geometry and couple this with practical parameterchoice rules: discrepancy principles with known or estimated noise, and stabilized weighted GCV. Using a unified testbed with sta

474dd9a0ae179921bc139dd9dd7ea8a6e2946bf7.title: An Automated Pipeline for Processing and Analysis of Clinical Fetal Diffusion Mri
474dd9a0ae179921bc139dd9dd7ea8a6e2946bf7.abstract: In this work, we present an automated pipeline for processing diffusion MRI (dMRI) data acquired in fetuses in clinical routine. In-vivo fetal dMRI provides critical insight into brain development but is challenging due to motion, low SNR ratio, and artifacts. These challenges are prominent in the clinical routine, with additional constraints on the duration of the scanning session. Existing state-of-the-art pipelines are designed for high-quality research acquisition protocols that are not feasible in routine clinical practice. We introduce a comprehensive framework that integrates robust opensource tools to handle clinical fetal dMRI, performing motion correction, anatomical standardization, and diffusion tensor estimation. The pipeline is complemented by an extended set of anatomical parcellations for the dHCP fetal atlas, enabling detailed regional analysis. Applied to a large clinic

470db98ac46a441b68b6c847085897987b5b959d.title: Numerical Framework for Deep Learning Photoacoustics Image Reconstruction
470db98ac46a441b68b6c847085897987b5b959d.abstract: Photoacoustic imaging (PAI) combines pulsed optical excitation with ultrasound detection to produce high-contrast molecular and structural images of biological tissues. Conventional PAI systems rely on high-energy pulsed lasers that, despite their excellent performance, remain bulky, costly, and constrained by strict safety requirements, limiting their clinical translation. This work explores the use of pulsed semiconductor diodes as a compact, low-cost, and portable alternative. Although these sources exhibit lower peak power and reduced fluence, advanced computational approaches can compensate for these limitations. We present a numerical framework that integrates realistic optical and acoustic simulations with deep learning reconstruction to enhance image quality under low-fluence conditions. The framework accounts for light propagation, transducer response, and acoustic field effects

46eb60c0251c6a83b15fca09a3013b2393db4830.title: PnP-SAF: A Plug-and-Play Semantic-Attribute Fusion Framework for Data-Efficient Medical Image Diagnosis
46eb60c0251c6a83b15fca09a3013b2393db4830.abstract: In recent years, deep learning has achieved remarkable success in medical diagnosis. However, its performance is often limited by small medical datasets, leading to overfitting and poor generalization. Accurate diagnosis also depends on non-image semantic attributes (e.g., age, sex, lifestyle factors), which provide critical complementary context. To address these challenges, we present PnP-SAF, a plug-andplay Semantic-Attribute Fusion framework that enhances data-efficient medical image diagnosis. PnP-SAF can be seamlessly integrated into both CNN- and Transformer-based architectures, enabling effective fusion of semantic attributes with image features in a flexible manner. Extensive experiments on the ODIR and PAD-UFES-20 datasets demonstrate that PnP-SAF mitigates overfitting, improves generalization, and significantly boosts diagnostic accuracy, highlighting its robustness and practi

462278211f714cf5e8744610711d5b04390f6351.title: Attention-Based Tracking of Ultrasound Frames for Prostate Biopsy Navigation Using a Zonal Representation
462278211f714cf5e8744610711d5b04390f6351.abstract: Computer-assistance improves the accuracy of transrectal prostate biopsy procedures through the fusion of real-time 2D ultrasound images with a reference volume. In this study, we propose a method to remove ambiguity in estimating the sign of out-of-plane parameters of the relative transformation between two consecutive ultrasound images based on the efficient integration of a prostate zonal representation into the model. This avoids the need for systematic and costly resampling of slices. Two variants of a ResNet-based model, with and without self-attention, were trained and evaluated on simulated 2D ultrasound streams from the clinical data of 97 patients, each patient being associated with a reference volume acquired in a standardized manner. The results are very encouraging and demonstrate both the computational efficiency of this method and the value of self-attention for realistic

459d06f8f4a977c3db0cec43f380ae51d5d763fc.title: Bridging Foundation and Domain-Specific Models for Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
459d06f8f4a977c3db0cec43f380ae51d5d763fc.abstract: Segmentation plays a crucial role in medical image analysis. Although deep learning models have achieved remarkable results in automatic image segmentation, their training typically demands large amounts of annotated data, which are costly and time-consuming to obtain. Recently, the Segment Anything Model (SAM) has demonstrated strong zero-shot performance in image segmentation. Nevertheless, its effectiveness can be limited in specialized tasks like medical image segmentation that demand deep domain-specific knowledge. To address these limitations, we propose a semi-supervised learning (SSL) model for medical image segmentation that integrates SAM with a domain-specific network to enable effective learning of both scarce labelled and unlabelled data. The domain-specific network comprises a U-Net encoder with a modified decoder. Furthermore, a knowledge fusion module is introduced to ena

441105f2439d91fc6ed25f8299ed496c0e1e5796.title: OpenEEG: Uncertainty-Aware Open Set Learning for EEG-Based Brain Disorders Diagnosis
441105f2439d91fc6ed25f8299ed496c0e1e5796.abstract: Deep learning models for EEG-based brain disorder diagnosis have shown promise, but their clinical utility is hampered by the restrictive closed-set assumption and an inability to quantify predictive uncertainty. This limitation leads to overconfident misclassifications of both unseen disorders and challenging known cases, posing significant safety risks. To address these issues, we propose OpenEEG, an uncertainty-aware open-set learning framework designed to simultaneously reject unknown disease categories and quantify the epistemic uncertainty of its predictions. OpenEEG integrates a Transformer backbone with a UA-Classifier based on evidential deep learning, which learns a Dirichlet distribution over class predictions to derive uncertainty scores. We validate our framework on multiple public EEG datasets under subjectindependent splits. The results demonstrate that OpenEEG substantial

4300f9b4bff502f762b860099e61fc0312ffa0ff.title: Exploring Xeno-Learning for Brain Image Synthesis: An Image-to-Image Translation Approach to Cross-Species Knowledge Transfer
4300f9b4bff502f762b860099e61fc0312ffa0ff.abstract: Despite an abundance of high-quality mouse neuroimaging data, anatomical divergence from humans limits how findings from this data can be translated into clinical insights or applications. In this work, we present a proof-of-concept for a deep learning-driven image-to-image translation framework that translates parcellations of 23 common regions between mouse and human brain MRI datasets. Our model utilizes species-specific pre-trained autoencoders with principal component analysis dimensionality reduction coupled with a multi-layer perceptron that learns mappings from mouse to human latent encodings. Moreover, a novel objective function enforces the latent mapping to maintain realism and volume correlation of common regions between the input mouse image and the translated human image. Our results demonstrate that the proposed method produces realistic and varied human brain parcellation

41f3961416dc1cf04d2a928fdf7db23c6dde051b.title: State-of-the-Art Stroke Lesion Segmentation at 1/1000th of Parameters
41f3961416dc1cf04d2a928fdf7db23c6dde051b.abstract: Efficient and accurate whole-brain lesion segmentation re-mains a challenge in medical image analysis. In this work, we revisit MeshNet, a parameter-efficient segmentation model, and introduce a novel multi-scale dilation pattern with an encoder-decoder structure. This innovation enables capturing broad contextual information and fine-grained details without traditional downsampling, upsampling, or skip-connections. Unlike previous approaches processing subvolumes or slices, we operate directly on whole-brain 2563 MRI volumes. Evaluations on the Aphasia Recovery Cohort (ARC) dataset demonstrate that MeshNet achieves superior or comparable DICE scores to state-of-the-art architectures such as Med-NeXt and U-MAMBA at 1/1000th of parameters. Our results validate MeshNet's strong balance of efficiency and performance, making it particularly suitable for resource-limited environments such as

41022c6ebe8a37078ba749872a7bc7f8aa38a189.title: Segmentation and Diagnosis of Fetal Heart Ultrasound Based on Anatomical Structure Priors and Dual-Threshold Guided Semi-Supervised Learning
41022c6ebe8a37078ba749872a7bc7f8aa38a189.abstract: Aiming at the problems of scarce labeled data, complex anatomical structures and insufficient boundary accuracy in intelligent diagnosis of fetal congenital heart disease, this paper proposes a fetal heart ultrasound segmentation and diagnosis algorithm fusing anatomical structure prior and semi-supervised learning. Its innovations include three aspects: designing an Anatomical Structure Query-based Segmentation Decoder to embed medical prior into global feature learning; proposing a View-Aware Connected Component Loss to dynamically constrain the connected domain morphology of anatomical structures and suppress false positives and structural fragmentation; putting forward a Dual-Threshold Guided Semi-Supervised Classification Learning strategy to maximize the value of unlabeled data and alleviate class imbalance and pseudo-label noise. 40ba616ee50f4e00b511724638282f9972d67bca.title: Time-Embedding U-Net for Temporally Consistent Left Ventricular Segmentation in 3D Echocardiography
40ba616ee50f4e00b511724638282f9972d67bca.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) echocardiography is an inherently noisy modality, but allows for capture of temporally complex cardiac motions. Existing segmentation methods often treat cardiac frames independently, resulting in inconsistent delineations across the cardiac cycle, reduced segmentation accuracy, and, in turn, impacting the estimation of key clinical metrics. To address this, our work introduces temporal positional embeddings based on the cardiac cycle to improve 3D echocardiography segmentation. By encoding cardiac phase information into sinusoidal functions, we inject temporal embeddings into the bottleneck and decoder of a U-Net. Our approach (TU-Net) outperforms state-of-the-art models, including nnU-Net and Transformer baselines, UNETR and SwinUNETR. TU-Net achieved a Dice score of 84.7% along with improved temporal consistency, evaluated over two test cases with 18 and 16 fram

3ffcd40d3ad09e2f9323197eed17aafa4e7cde38.title: Line Artifact Removal Over Medical X-Ray Images via Joint Dictionaries Sparse Decomposition with Structured Incoherence
3ffcd40d3ad09e2f9323197eed17aafa4e7cde38.abstract: Line artifact is one of several artifacts that can affect the image quality of X-ray digital radiography. It appears as a sequence of a bright line followed by a darker one with variable intensity over the image. Extracting this artifact is challenging since it can remove some of the medical content and worsen the image quality. In this paper, we present a new line artifact suppression method based on a joint sparse dictionary model where the clinical content dictionary is learned with an incoherence penalty with respect to the artifact model. Tests on a large X-ray dataset show better estimation performance compared to the state-of-the-art methods.

3fd1a236255d01b6d7b3a5c2139d8c4040527e3a.title: View-Guided Multi-Task Learning for Fetal Cardiac Segmentation and CHD Classification
3fd1a236255d01b6d7b3a5c2139d8c4040527e3a.abstract: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is a major cause of infant morbidity and mortality, and fetal ultrasound is the standard modality for prenatal screening. The FETUS Challenge (ISBI 2026) focuses on the joint tasks of fetal cardiac structure segmentation and CHD-related multi-label classification across standard cardiac views under a semi-supervised learning (SSL) setting. We present a view-guided framework with separate models for segmentation and classification, both augmented with an auxiliary standard-view prediction head. To further exploit anatomical information, we introduce a view-specific geometric classifier that derives explicit geometric features from segmentation masks to capture cardiac structural relationships. On the validation leaderboard, our method (team CHDkiller) achieved an overall score of 52.54 (F1 44.54, DSC 81.34, NSD 63.08), compared with the baseline score of 40.

3fccd95f6793c465c6fb02e7735255c2430dbd82.title: Towards Universal Ultrasound Analysis: Parameter-Efficient Foundation Model With Task-Aware Routing for Heterogeneous Multi-Task Learning
3fccd95f6793c465c6fb02e7735255c2430dbd82.abstract: Developing a universal foundation model for ultrasound imaging is inherently challenging due to severe speckle noise, diverse acquisition protocols, and the semantic gap between heterogeneous clinical tasks. Traditional multi-task learning often suffers from negative transfer when simultaneously optimizing dense (i.e., segmentation, detection) and global (i.e., classification, regression) predictions. In this paper, we propose UltraTAR, a parameter-efficient Task-Aware Routing framework that won 1st Place in the Foundation Model Challenge for Ultrasound Image Analysis (FMC-UIA) 2026. Instead of full fine-tuning, we leverage a frozen Vision Foundation Model (VFM) adapted via Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) to preserve robust pre-trained representations while injecting lightweight task-specific knowledge. To overcome the architectural disconnect between single-scale foundation features and dive

3f8c89063bb50695537057868cdd087dd8013337.title: DBCoreset: A Density-Based Coreset Algorithm for Computationally Efficient Chest X-Ray Diagnosis
3f8c89063bb50695537057868cdd087dd8013337.abstract: Coreset generation is a data reduction method that facilitates efficient deep learning training. A good coreset can achieve comparable performance using a much smaller number of training samples. However, traditional coreset methods exhibit density bias. This bias leads to poor representation of subregions that are sparsely populated by data points within a class. To solve this, we propose a novel Density-based Coreset Generation algorithm to facilitate computationally efficient chest x-ray diagnosis. We first partition the feature space into fine-grained, clinically-relevant miniclusters utilizing density. We then introduce a scoring-based selection mechanism. It helps in finding out the representative datapoints to eventually train a classifier model. Furthermore, we enforce a minimum inclusion criterion for every minicluster. This step aims to mitigate density bias so that coverage of

3f79a0a98075efbfacc8d7c794fb5be7506f5e15.title: Healthy Counterfactual Generation with Denoising Diffusion Bridge Models
3f79a0a98075efbfacc8d7c794fb5be7506f5e15.abstract: Generating healthy counterfactuals from pathological images holds significant promise in anomaly detection or for application of analysis tools designed for healthy scans. These counterfactuals should represent what a patient's scan would plausibly look like in the absence of pathology, preserving individual anatomical characteristics while modifying only the pathological regions. Denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) can generate healthy counterfactuals by training on solely healthy data, with the assumption that a partial denoising process will be unable to model disease regions - and will instead reconstruct a closely matched healthy counterpart. More recent methods have incorporated synthetic pathological images to better guide the diffusion process, but it remains challenging to effectively balances the removal of anomalies with the retention of subject-specific features.

3eafd65eacdbe1ccedc4a40a9ce5a5046e68aa5a.title: Feature Invariance Via Interpretable Ablation for Single-Source Domain Generalization in X-Ray Angiography Segmentation
3eafd65eacdbe1ccedc4a40a9ce5a5046e68aa5a.abstract: Generalizability of X-ray Coronary Angiography (XCA) vessel segmentation models faces challenges due to differences in patient demographics and imaging conditions that result in domain shifts. Current Single-source Domain Generalization (SDG) methods addressing this shift are largely augmentation-based, which aim to introduce variety during training, however, without directly probing which features are being learned. We present a post-hoc analysis to understand this behavior, particularly in the first-layer channels, which encode the low-level features in a convolutional network. We conduct the analysis across six XCA datasets (one source, five out-of-distribution (OOD)) to characterize and probe granular per-channel features for our task of XCA vessel segmentation. 3eaf0c33328007ace360c2bc9960d6e6146bf5e3.title: Distance Weighted Ordinal Modeling for Ulcerative Colitis Severity Assessment in Endoscopy
3eaf0c33328007ace360c2bc9960d6e6146bf5e3.abstract: In this work, we detail our submission to the EndoCV ISBI Challenge for Ulcerative Colitis (UC) grading, covering Mayo Endoscopic Score (MES) classification, Ulcerative Colitis Endoscopic Index of Severity (UCEIS) prediction, and structured caption generation. Our method utilizes a large-scale self-supervised ResNet-50 backbone pretrained on 5 million endoscopic images to capture domain-relevant representations. To effectively model the hierarchical nature of disease severity, we adopt an ordinal-aware framework incorporating a modified class distance weighted loss with adjacent class emphasis. For UCEIS, we prioritize clinical interpretability by predicting individual components which subsequently inform rule based caption synthesis. 3e3f35187aa71ff2d05cb6530305f412b072308c.title: Personalized Federated Learning with Residual Fisher Information for Medical Image Segmentation
3e3f35187aa71ff2d05cb6530305f412b072308c.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple clients (institutions) to collaboratively train machine learning models without sharing their private data. To address the challenge of data heterogeneity across clients, personalized federated learning (pFL) aims to learn customized models for each client. In this work, we propose pFL -ResFIM, a novel pFL framework that achieves client-adaptive personalization at the parameter level. Specifically, we introduce a new metric, Residual Fisher Information Matrix (ResFIM), to quantify the sensitivity of model parameters to domain discrepancies. To estimate ResFIM for each client model under privacy constraints, we employ a spectral transfer strategy that generates simulated data reflecting the domain styles of different clients. 3ddc8294823eb0b51332fe9d3cf7a632a4dbe8e5.title: Spatiotemporal Learning with Context-Aware Video Tubelets for Ultrasound Video Analysis
3ddc8294823eb0b51332fe9d3cf7a632a4dbe8e5.abstract: Computer-aided pathology detection algorithms for video-based imaging modalities must accurately interpret complex spatiotemporal information by integrating findings across multiple frames. Current state-of-the-art methods operate by classifying on video sub-volumes (tubelets), but they often lose global spatial context by focusing only on local re-gions within detection ROIs. Here we propose a lightweight framework for tubelet -based object detection and video clas-sification that preserves both global spatial context and fine spatiotemporal features. To address the loss of global context, we embed tubelet location, size, and confidence as inputs to the classifier. Additionally, we use ROI -aligned feature maps from a pre-trained detection model, leveraging learned feature representations to increase the receptive field and reduce computational complexity. 3d3b11f48d7ea8f79d0826f039b57f448b798aa4.title: When are Diffusion Priors Helpful in Sparse Reconstruction? A Study with Sparse-view CT
3d3b11f48d7ea8f79d0826f039b57f448b798aa4.abstract: Diffusion models demonstrate state-of-the-art performance on image generation, and are gaining traction for sparse medical image reconstruction tasks. However, compared to classical reconstruction algorithms relying on simple ana-lytical priors, diffusion models have the dangerous property of producing realistic looking results even when incorrect, particularly with few observations. We investigate the utility of diffusion models as priors for image reconstruction by varying the number of observations and comparing their performance to classical priors (sparse and Tikhonov regularization) using pixel-based, structural, and downstream metrics. We make comparisons on low-dose chest wall computed tomography (CT) for fat mass quantification. 3d1859b8fca08633110818d1e21a8f1090a6686f.title: Protostage-NET: A Clinically Guided Foundation Model With Prototypical Learning for Automated Amd Grading From Oct Images
3d1859b8fca08633110818d1e21a8f1090a6686f.abstract: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a major cause of vision loss, where accurate staging is essential for treatment. However, most recent approaches for OCT images remain limited to binary classification and do not capture the full clinical spectrum of the disease. To address this gap, we propose ProtoStage-Net, an explainable foundation model framework for fine-grained AMD staging. Our method leverages the DINOv2 vision foundation model as a backbone, fully fine-tuned for OCT data, and introduces two clinically inspired attention mechanisms: the Clinically Guided Channel Attention (CGCA) module, which emphasizes diseaserelevant feature channels, and the Lesion Localization Module (LLM), which highlights pathological retinal regions. 3d0e7625466c6dabc6bf99e3bd811c3f683dc6aa.title: Distilling Knowledge from Multiple Foundation Models for Accurate and Efficient Spatial Gene Expression Prediction
3d0e7625466c6dabc6bf99e3bd811c3f683dc6aa.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables spatially resolved profiling of gene expression within tissue, but experimental assays remain costly and labor-intensive. We propose a lightweight knowledge distillation framework that predicts spatial gene expression from hematoxylin and eosin-stained (H&E) histology through multi-teacher distillation from diverse pathology foundation models (FM). The student model, leveraging efficiently distilled pathological feature representations, is further integrated into a downstream spatial gene expression prediction pipeline. We evaluate the method on large-scale H&E-ST repositories spanning multiple tissue cohorts and demonstrate that the distilled student model consistently matches or exceeds end-to-end model training and raw feature concatenation baselines in predictive accuracy and shows robust generalizability when tested on unseen cohorts, with signif

3d03c8098f6fc0f913be4d23bd09fd779a31b792.title: Eosinophil Counting with Green Learning
3d03c8098f6fc0f913be4d23bd09fd779a31b792.abstract: Quantifying eosinophils in gastrointestinal (GI) biopsies is critical for diagnosing eosinophilic esophagitis. The gold standard, manual counting by pathologists, is laborious, timeconsuming, and suffers from significant variability between physicians. Although deep learning (DL) models have automated this process with high accuracy, they often operate as black boxes, lacking transparency and interpretability. Furthermore, these neural networks require substantial computational resources for training and inference. This paper introduces a novel Green Learning (GL) framework for eosinophil counting, prioritizing transparency and computational efficiency. Our pipeline diverges from backpropagation-based DL. 3c61522b656355ddf2795c3f6f51b4d0663cec1a.title: Deep Learning-Based DR Screening from Oct Using Layer-Aware Thickness and Texture Maps
3c61522b656355ddf2795c3f6f51b4d0663cec1a.abstract: Early detection of retinal disease is vital because structural damage can progress without symptoms and lead to irreversible vision loss. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) is well suited to this need since it resolves the retina into discrete layers with micrometer precision. Focusing on diabetic retinopathy (DR), we propose a pipeline that converts OCT layer segmentation into a pixel-aligned thickness image and fuses it with normalized grayscale intensity and local binary pattern (LBP) microtexture as a three-channel input to a compact transformer optimized end to end. The classifier learns complementary evidence from all three channels and, without pretraining, surpasses competitive convolutional neural network (CNN) and transformer baselines with accuracy $99.12 \% \pm 1.99 \%$, specificity $99.33 \% \pm 2.11 \%$, sensitivity $98.95 \% \pm 2.22 \%$, F1 score $99.20 \% \pm 1.78 \%$, a

3ae6ca19cb977a1fec1497ba47c1addf9e8887b9.title: Meso-Regions: 4D Segmentation of Early Contrast Enhancement Biomarkers for Pleural Mesothelioma Diagnosis
3ae6ca19cb977a1fec1497ba47c1addf9e8887b9.abstract: Pleural mesothelioma is an aggressive cancer often diagnosed late due to the lack of reliable non-invasive biomarkers. Early Contrast Enhancement (ECE) observed in Dynamic Contrast-Enhanced MRI (DCE-MRI) is a promising biomarker characterized by a peak in mean signal intensity within 270 seconds in pleural regions, achieving a malignancy classification accuracy of 0.83. However, it depends on manual ROI annotation, limiting clinical adoption. We present Meso-Regions, an automated pipeline that detects ECE-positive regions as 4D segmentation masks in DCE-MRI. The method integrates motion correction, pleural-region segmentation, automatic ROI placement, and patient-level classification based on temporal mean-intensity curves. Applied to 56 patient scans (20 for training and 36 for testing), the approach achieved a malignancy classification accuracy of 0.60, showing high concordance in mali

3a5e3a4b55ff8a9ea506bfb692411112d0aa5289.title: Train for Stain: Adapting for Diverse H&E Staining Profiles Across Centers in Classification of Mitotic Figures (Glioma-MDC 2025)
3a5e3a4b55ff8a9ea506bfb692411112d0aa5289.abstract: Mitotic figure detection is an important aspect of grading for many forms of cancer however, there can be very high interrater variability. With the emergence of computational digital pathology, there is great potential for this classification task to be carried out objectively and consistently by a data-driven approach. However, this process is somewhat hampered by the diversity of cellular characteristics across cancer sites and the size of the domain shift between datasets originating from different centers. Building upon a previously developed classifier for H&E stained samples (HPVNet), this study aims to see if the established practices to minimize the impact of domain shift by stain variation can be minimized through a range of augmentation approaches and fine-tuning. 39f4581fd45c90fb111d4e544b8fd9130111171f.title: Automated, Vendor-Agnostic Measurement of Myocardial Tissue Velocities in Echocardiography
39f4581fd45c90fb111d4e544b8fd9130111171f.abstract: In this study, we present a vendor-agnostic, deep learning-based system for the automated analysis of transthoracic pulsed-wave tissue Doppler imaging (TDI), which decouples image acquisition from interpretation and enables centralized, fleet-wide analysis across devices. The model ingests standard TDI from heterogeneous ultrasound systems and automatically extracts key diagnostic markerspeak systolic velocity $(S^{\prime}$), early diastolic velocity $(e^{\prime}$), and late diastolic/atrial contraction velocity $(a^{\prime}$) using a single, unified pipeline. Conceptually, this harmonizes measurements across vendors and sites, improving consistency, comparability, and longitudinal tracking without devicespecific calibration or tooling. 39eaf7e1333003b1c2f998cefe0f20a43eab354b.title: MAGNET: Mask Guided Network with EMA Teacher for Joint Carotid Segmentation and Plaque Classification
39eaf7e1333003b1c2f998cefe0f20a43eab354b.abstract: Automated carotid plaque assessment via ultrasound (US) is clinically vital yet remains challenging due to scarce expert annotations and significant data heterogeneity. In this paper, we propose MAGNET, a Mask-Guided Network with an EMA Teacher, designed for joint semi-supervised plaque/vessel segmentation and vulnerability classification in the CSV 2026 Challenge. MAGNET features a ConvNeXtbased dual-task architecture integrated with a mask-guided classification head. This module integrates plaque probability maps and morphological cues, such as size and shape derived from segmentation predictions, to improve risk reasoning and suppress background noise. To address label scarcity, we adopt a Mean Teacher-based semi-supervised learning strategy with confidence-weighted consistency regularization to leverage unlabeled data effectively. 395a033bd962f0129bbd6348b300ade13c2519bf.title: Synthetic Artifact Generation for Training of Mri Denoising Networks
395a033bd962f0129bbd6348b300ade13c2519bf.abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of patients with cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) is challenged by susceptibility artifacts. We propose a simulation-to-learning framework for artifact suppression in cine MRI. Subjectspecific digital phantoms were derived from the ACDC dataset by encoding proton density (PD), longitudinal relaxation (T1), transverse relaxation (T2), effective transverse relaxation (T2*), and off-resonance ($\Delta \omega$). Susceptibility effects were modeled as randomized dipole perturbations applied to the off-resonance map, yielding perfectly paired-MRI images artifact-free and artifact-present. MRI reconstruction was conducted with KomaMRI. In order to remove artifacts effects, approximately 32,500 paired images were generated to train a Residual U-Net. 3951cd7ceff364b28bf57a8446165543d9889bc1.title: Context-Aware LSTM for 3D Medical Image Localisation
3951cd7ceff364b28bf57a8446165543d9889bc1.abstract: Medical images contain higher spatial correlation between data points compared to natural images. In this work we exploit this feature to develop a localisation network for application in 3D medical imaging data. Long-Short-term memory layers, are used to learn the distinct pattern in the organ anatomy which we propose will robustly localize organs and also deformations in organs caused by tumors that disrupt typical patterns/appearance. Our network achieves an average precision of 89% for fetal heart localisation on echocardiogram data, 83% for tumor localisation on the BraTS 2021 dataset and 80% for prostrate localisation on the Promise12 dataset. With a trainable parameter size (3.2M parameters) comparable to MobileNet-V2 for slice localisation and less than 10M for 3D we present a computationally efficient network for 3D localisation on medical data. 390c0a088e314c654ffb1247726ab457a28ab8f4.title: Explainsegnet: Interpretable Segmentation for Alzheimer's Diagnosis
390c0a088e314c654ffb1247726ab457a28ab8f4.abstract: This study focuses on enhancing the accuracy of predicting Alzheimer's disease, mild cognitive impairment, and normal control cases. We leverage the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) dataset- comprising 3D structural magnetic resonance imaging brain scans, for our method development and evaluation. Our analysis utilizes a residual 3D convolutional neural network (equipped with 4 attention layers). The core contributions of our work are twofold: firstly, we have innovatively integrated clinical expertise into the initialization of the attention layer's weights through whole-brain segmentation technique; secondly, we have employed various state-of-the-art model interpretation techniques. 38cf0a18364ecb3e271b88c3dc11418b7d646fff.title: Risk-RAM: An Interpretable Deep Survival Prediction Model for COVID-19 Prognosis Using Chest X-Ray Images
38cf0a18364ecb3e271b88c3dc11418b7d646fff.abstract: COVID-19 has strained global public health, necessitating accurate diagnosis and intervention to control disease spread and reduce mortality rates. This paper introduces an inter-pretable method Risk-RAM for survival prediction model designed specifically for improved understanding and trust in prognosis using chest X-ray (CXR) images. Our approach produces regional interpretable outcomes that effectively capture essential disease features while focusing on rare but critical abnormal regions. The predictive results provide enhanced clarity and transparency through risk area localization, enabling clinicians to make informed decisions regarding COVID-19 diagnosis with a better understanding of prognostic insights. 384034ba311ca0f60f1c188e303ec2ff2a235b3b.title: ATRI-Net: A Multimodal and Multifocal Fusion Network for Embryo Euploidy Prediction
384034ba311ca0f60f1c188e303ec2ff2a235b3b.abstract: Selecting euploid embryos during in vitro fertilization (IVF) is crucial for successful implantation, yet conventional preimplantation genetic testing (PGT) is invasive and costly. To overcome these challenges, we have developed ATRI-Net, a high-performance multimodal model designed to predict whether embryos are euploid based on time-lapse videos of embryonic development captured at multiple focal planes, alongside patients' clinical data. ATRI-Net utilizes the Dynamic Multi-Focal Local Space Relation Aggregator (DYMFLSRA) module to fuse multifocal information at each developmental stage of the embryo, employs the UniFormerV2 video understanding model to extract spatiotemporal information, and integrates video features with clinical data using an efficient mutan modality fusion module for prediction. 376550131337f4fb1b755709b6d1b51e9b9ca088.title: CephRes-MHNet: A Multi-Head Residual Network for Accurate and Robust Cephalometric Landmark Detection
376550131337f4fb1b755709b6d1b51e9b9ca088.abstract: Accurate localization of cephalometric landmarks from 2D lateral skull X-rays is vital for orthodontic diagnosis and treatment. Manual annotation is time-consuming and error-prone, whereas automated approaches often struggle with low contrast and anatomical complexity. This paper introduces CephRes-MHNet, a multi-head residual convolutional network for robust and efficient cephalometric landmark detection. The architecture integrates residual encoding, dual-attention mechanisms, and multi-head decoders to enhance contextual reasoning and anatomical precision. Trained on the Aariz Cephalometric dataset of 1,000 radiographs, CephResMHNet achieved a mean radial error (MRE) of 1.23 mm and a success detection rate (SDR) @ 2.0 mm of 85.5 %, outperforming all evaluated models. 37040d91d62ad1fe00c68e1344e1d090e5d83e0a.title: From Intensity to Anatomy: Optimizing nnU-Net for MR-to-CT Translation on SynthRAD2025
37040d91d62ad1fe00c68e1344e1d090e5d83e0a.abstract: Magnetic resonance (MR) to computed tomography (CT) translation enables a non-ionizing alternative for radiotherapy planning and longitudinal disease monitoring. The SynthRAD2025 dataset provides a large-scale benchmark to evaluate cross-modality synthesis methods across anatomical regions. Building upon the nnU-Net framework, this work revisits its design for image synthesis and proposes key optimizations to establish a strong new baseline. We integrate architectural refinements, a two-stage fine-tuning strategy, and an optimized Anatomical Feature-Prioritized (AFP) loss that leverages pre-trained segmentation features to enhance anatomical fidelity. Best practices for AFP supervision are detailed, including segmentation model configuration and layer selection. 35dc211c0f61f92bdd2c531e44ef7c45465812d8.title: Segmentation of Cardiovascular Structures from Screening Non-contrast CT Calcium Score Images Using the Tuned CardioNC-Segmentator on Virtual CTA Images
35dc211c0f61f92bdd2c531e44ef7c45465812d8.abstract: In this work, we outline the development of a deep learning-based segmentation network aimed at automatically segmenting heart chambers using virtual CT angiography (VCT A) data. Inspired by the structure and methodology of TotalSegmentator, our approach leverages nnU-Net architecture, optimized for the precise delineation of anatomical structures in volumetric medical images. The model is trained on a dataset (N=51) of non-contrast CT calcium score (CTCS) scans, annotated with ground truth segmentations of the heart's atria and ventricles. The integration of virtual CT angiography as a pre-processing step enhances the visibility of cardiac structures, such as large blood pools and adipose and muscle tissues, aiding the model's ability to discern complex boundary regions. 35d959c8e3426cf59356f9f4348b15afc6e054bb.title: Machine Learning-Based Polysomnography Data Analysis for ADHD Diagnosis: A Focus on Sleep Stage-Based Biomarkers
35d959c8e3426cf59356f9f4348b15afc6e054bb.abstract: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) significantly impacts children and adults worldwide, posing challenges in neurodevelopmental diagnostics. This study aimed to improve ADHD diagnostic accuracy by identifying sleep stage-based biomarkers for ADHD through the analysis of polysomnography (PSG) recordings, including EEG, EOG, EMG, and ECG signals across five sleep stages. Our analysis included 20,294 epochs for ADHD and 19,968 epochs for non-ADHD from 48 patients. We applied graph metrics, particularly the average shortest path length, to quantify the efficiency of information transfer within brain networks and other physiological systems. We employed nested cross-validation to ensure robust model training and evaluation, with an outer 5-fold cross-validation and an inner GridSearchCV for hyperparameter tuning and model selection. 35ce51a1c99bd1693b238798166b4c0d43218219.title: A Multimodal Deep Learning Framework for Prostate Cancer Risk Prediction Integrating Biparametric MRI, Radiology Reports, and Clinical Biomarkers
35ce51a1c99bd1693b238798166b4c0d43218219.abstract: Accurate prostate cancer risk stratification requires integration of heterogeneous clinical data sources that exhibit variable quality and complementary diagnostic information. We propose EFNet-SAF (Expert Fusion Network with Staged Adaptive Fusion), a multimodal framework that integrates Biparametric MRI (DWI, T2-weighted), radiology reports, and clinical biomarkers (e.g.,PSA, Age) through an instance-specific adaptive approach. The architecture employs modality-specific expert networks trained independently with pretrained encoders, followed by adaptive fusion that learns patient-specific modality importance. Hierarchical imaging processing exploits spatial correspondence between DWI and T2 sequences, while clinical biomarkers are incorporated through a learned weighting mechanism. Evaluated on 73 prostate cancer cases using 5 -fold cross-validation, EFNet-SAF achieved an AUROC of $0.9

35a42436ed79848cc29fe662e577525779fb5764.title: Structural Self-Supervision for Label-Free Aortic Dissection Triage on Non-Contrast CT
35a42436ed79848cc29fe662e577525779fb5764.abstract: Effective triage of aortic abnormalities on non-contrast CT (NCCT) is critical for emergency care. Yet automated detection remains difficult due to low vessel–background contrast, resulting in unstable pseudo-segmentations and unreliable supervision. We address this by transforming pseudo-mask instability into a source of structural self-supervision. Instead of suppressing such variability, our framework leverages it to learn normative aortic anatomy and detect deviations indicative of pathology. It integrates three key modules: (1) Prompt-invariant Structural Embedding (PISE) enforces feature consistency across multiple SAM-based prompts; (2) Region-aware Disentanglement (RAD) isolates vessel-wall representations from surrounding tissues; (3) Consistency Evidence Map (CEM) provides transparent, radiologistaligned visualization of abnormal regions. On 363 multicenter NCCT scans, the prop

352f357a5d633a18405637710f1c8e48138195da.title: Otoscopy AI: Deeply Supervised Attention for Otoscopic Image Segmentation
352f357a5d633a18405637710f1c8e48138195da.abstract: Automatic segmentation of otoscopic images is a prevalent challenge and a focus of active research. Recent works in the field adopt convolutional neural networks (CNNs) because of their performance compared to traditional methods. In this paper, we introduce a novel deeply supervised attention (DSA) approach that integrates a deep supervision mechanism with a convolutional block attention module (CBAM) to enhance the model using high-level features from small and uncertain objects. The proposed approach improves the segmentation of 11 otoscopic features, including the tympanic membrane, the cerumen, and abnormalities. Our method is the first architecture to provide segmentation for such abnormalities, reaching 0.80 mAP on average, demonstrating $10-20 \%$ superior performance over existing state-of-the-art methods. 352c0149828ea7da6de92551d093e7b74022e3e2.title: Oculomix: Hierarchical Sampling for Retinal-Based Systemic Disease Prediction
352c0149828ea7da6de92551d093e7b74022e3e2.abstract: Oculomics — the concept of predicting systemic diseases, such as cardiovascular disease and dementia, through retinal imaging — has advanced rapidly due to the data efficiency of transformer-based foundation models like RETFound. Image-level mixed sample data augmentations, such as CutMix and MixUp, are frequently used for training transformers, yet these techniques perturb patient-specific attributes, such as medical comorbidity and clinical factors, since they only account for images and labels. To address this limitation, we propose a hierarchical sampling strategy, Oculomix, for mixed sample augmentations. Our method is based on two clinical priors. First (exam level), images acquired from the same patient at the same time point share the same attributes. 3512350c2cf96ea0da763255f7bdc7a48dc126ac.title: CGM-EEG: Cross-Gated Mamba for Spatio-Temporal Eeg Representation Learning
3512350c2cf96ea0da763255f7bdc7a48dc126ac.abstract: Accurate decoding of electroencephalography (EEG) signals is essential for advancing clinical diagnostics and brain-computer interface (BCI) applications. Although sequence-based models have shown promise in capturing long-range dependencies, they often struggle to represent the intricate spatio-temporal structure of EEG data. To address this limitation, we propose CGM-EEG (Cross-Gated Mamba for EEG Decoding), a fully Mamba-based dual-branch architecture that processes spatial and temporal features in parallel. To enhance feature interaction, our framework introduces a Cross-Gate Module (CGM) that enables each branch to integrate information from the other through a lightweight crossgated mechanism. 34f816790ee38cf81053382e38af93dee37833a5.title: Synthetic Dataset Generation and Validation for Robotic Surgery Instrument Segmentation
34f816790ee38cf81053382e38af93dee37833a5.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive workflow for generating and validating a synthetic dataset designed for robotic surgery instrument segmentation. A 3D reconstruction of the Da VinciTM robotic arms was refined and animated in Autodesk MayaTM through a fully automated Python-based pipeline capable of producing photorealistic, labeled video sequences. Each scene integrates randomized motion patterns, lighting variations, and synthetic blood textures to mimic intraoperative variability while preserving pixel-accurate ground truth masks. To validate the realism and effectiveness of the generated data, several segmentation models were trained under controlled ratios of real and synthetic data. 349a693d83541bde39d73082c2442972ad09b9a5.title: Quality Control for Medical Image Segmentation Under Domain Shift with Heteroscedastic Regression
349a693d83541bde39d73082c2442972ad09b9a5.abstract: Trustworthy medical image segmentation systems require robust quality control mechanisms so that inadequately segmented cases can be excluded from downstream processing. This need becomes particularly acute when inputs deviate from the training distribution, such as images from unseen pathologies or novel scanner types. We propose heteroscedastic regression as a new approach for this, explicitly modeling both the expected accuracy and the uncertainty in our estimate. This framework provides flexibility to perform failure detection with varying thresholds for segmentation quality and confidence. Moreover, it can be combined with a recently proposed adversarial training strategy to achieve OOD generalization. 33cb338c0a88b8a70d86018780fa01a8098b20ad.title: Dualclip: Joint Cortical-Subcortical Representation Learning for Neurodevelopmental Disorder Detection
33cb338c0a88b8a70d86018780fa01a8098b20ad.abstract: Early diagnosis of neurodevelopmental disorders is essential for understanding atypical brain development. Although structural MRI has become a widely used tool for disease diagnosis, existing 3D CNN-based methods often overlook the topological organization of the cortex, limiting recognition accuracy. In contrast, surface-based approaches typically ignore subcortical structures, preventing a comprehensive characterization of neurodevelopmental abnormalities. To address these limitations, we propose DualCLIP, a contrastive multimodal fusion framework that jointly learns cortical and subcortical structural representations. DualCLIP consists of two complementary modules: SurfCLIP, which integrates a cortical encoder and a text encoder, and VolCLIP, which combines a volumetric encoder with a text encoder.
