33ca72f2f1c202c39dad378e0bd464c7520bc307.title: QwenCLIP: Boosting Medical Vision-Language Model Pretraining via LLM Embeddings and Prompt Tuning
33ca72f2f1c202c39dad378e0bd464c7520bc307.abstract: Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining (CLIP) has demonstrated strong generalization for vision-language tasks in computer vision and medical domains, yet its text encoder accepts only up to 77 tokens, which limits its ability to represent long and information-rich radiology reports. Recent adaptations using domain-specific encoders, such as PubMedBERT or ClinicalBERT, mitigate this issue by leveraging medical corpora, but remain constrained by their limited input length (typically 512 tokens) and relatively shallow semantic understanding. To address these limitations, we propose QwenCLIP, a vision-language framework that replaces CLIP's text encoder with a large language model (LLM)-based embedding module (e.g., Qwen3-Embedding) and introduces learnable prompts to enhance cross-modal alignment. By leveraging the extended context window and richer representations of LLMs, QwenCLIP captur

33931b13dbdbb72466a579c86c8b763636f5b430.title: CRC-SAM: SAM-Based Multi-Modal Segmentation and Quantification of Colorectal Cancer in CT, Colonoscopy, and Histology Images
33931b13dbdbb72466a579c86c8b763636f5b430.abstract: We present CRC-SAM, a unified framework for colorectal cancer segmentation across colonoscopy, CT, and histopathology images. Unlike prior single-modality methods, CRC-SAM provides consistent, modality-agnostic segmentation throughout the clinical workflow. Built on MedSAM, it incorporates low-rank adaptation (LoRA) layers into a frozen encoder, enabling efficient domain transfer to underrepresented modalities with minimal trainable parameters. Experiments on MSD-Colon, CVC-ClinicDB, and EBHI-Seg demonstrate superior performance across modalities, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines and highlighting the effectiveness of lightweight LoRA adaptation for foundation-model-based colorectal cancer analysis.

329bf196da283bdec6fde0773290329aed08b144.title: Coordinative Learning with Ordinal and Relational Priors for Volumetric Medical Image Segmentation
329bf196da283bdec6fde0773290329aed08b144.abstract: Volumetric medical image segmentation presents unique challenges due to the inherent anatomical structure and limited availability of annotations. While recent methods have shown promise by contrasting spatial relationships between slices, they rely on hard binary thresholds to define positive and negative samples, thereby discarding valuable continuous information about anatomical similarity. Moreover, these methods overlook the global directional consistency of anatomical progression, resulting in distorted feature spaces that fail to capture the canonical anatomical manifold shared across patients. To address these limitations, we propose Coordinative Ordinal-Relational Anatomical Learning (CORAL) to capture both local and global structure in volumetric images. 328ec1b2bb6035ef9f7f0d2c0fc5fcec30c349be.title: CGDA: Clip-Guided Cross-Modal Dual-Alignment Framework for Early Alzheimer's Diagnosis
328ec1b2bb6035ef9f7f0d2c0fc5fcec30c349be.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive cognitive decline and brain atrophy, where early diagnosis is critical. But existing multimodal methods integrating structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) and clinical metadata often fail to align heterogeneous semantic levels effectively. To address this, we propose a CLIP-guided cross-modal dual-alignment framework (CGDA) for early AD diagnosis. First, CGDA employs a fine-tuned CLIP model to extract 2D sMRI features and textual embeddings, establishing general semantic alignment, then 3D sMRI encoder captures spatial context, while a text module encodes clinical metadata. Secondly, a dualalignment mechanism refines cross-modal correspondence by performing two critical alignments: 1) spatially aligning 3D anatomical features with metadata, 2) semantically fusing CLIP-derived features with 3D data

3232f42d5b788a4fe21b64dfb423cdf8c0e860d6.title: Bridging the Gap Between Conventional and CNN-Based Registration: Application to Mouse Brain Morphometry
3232f42d5b788a4fe21b64dfb423cdf8c0e860d6.abstract: Deformable image registration is a fundamental step in medical imaging. With the advent of deep learning, con-volutional neural networks (CNN) are investigated to per-form image registration. Despite enabling faster inference time, CNN-based registration methods still do not signifi-cantly surpass conventional approaches in accuracy. Here, we formulate the link between conventional and CNN-based registration methods. We highlight the interest in considering CNN-based registration methods as a conventional reg-istration approach for groupwise registration. Although the accuracy is not significantly improved compared to conventional registration, the regularization effect induced by the CNN-based formulation appears to be of great interest for morphometric group study.

31e188895bb92d0887253ea17a48c966eaa1856e.title: Benchmarking Detectors for the RIVA Cervical Cytology Challenge
31e188895bb92d0887253ea17a48c966eaa1856e.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a significant global health challenge, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. While the Pap smear is a highly effective screening tool, its manual evaluation is time-consuming and prone to human error. Recent deep learning advancements automate cytology tasks; however, early detectors often struggle with fine-grained classification and severe class imbalances, particularly for underrepresented lesions. In this paper, we present Team jht010312's benchmarking methodology and results for the ISBI 2026 RIVA Cervical Cytology Challenge. We evaluate multiple state-of-the-art object detection models on the RIVA dataset, including Co-DETR, D-FINE, EVA-02, Mask R-CNN, and RetinaNet. 31c87a8f78f9e303e6e92a69b221178f2774abf6.title: DENSE-GUIDED DEEP MOTION NETWORKS ACCOUNTED BY LARGE ROTATIONS TO IMPROVE MYOCARDIAL STRAIN ANALYSIS FROM ROUTINE CINE MRI
31c87a8f78f9e303e6e92a69b221178f2774abf6.abstract: Myocardial strain imaging provides a valuable tool for detecting subclinical left ventricular (LV) dysfunction and adding prognostic value in assessing various types of heart disease. Recent studies have utilized highly accurate strain-dedicated techniques, such as displacement encoding with stimulated echoes (DENSE), to train a deep learning (DL) framework to predict the myocardial displacements/deformations from routine cine balanced steady state free precession (bSSFP) images. However, these methods have shown limited performance in capturing the large rotational motion of the myocardium associated with twist and torsion over time, which are important aspects of myocardial mechanics. To address this gap, this paper introduces a novel DENSE-guided DL network that explicitly accounts for large rotational motion to further improve strain analysis of standard cine bSSFP images. 3192b6c368d14d8b0cbdaed96823614616a0e473.title: Beyond the Monitor: Mixed Reality Visualization and Multimodal AI for Enhanced Digital Pathology Workflow
3192b6c368d14d8b0cbdaed96823614616a0e473.abstract: Pathologists diagnose cancer using gigapixel whole-slide images (WSIs), but the current digital workflow is fragmented. These multiscale datasets often exceed $100,000 \times 100,000$ pixels, yet standard 2D monitors restrict the field of view. This disparity forces constant panning and zooming, which increases cognitive load and disrupts diagnostic momentum. We introduce PathVis, a mixed-reality platform for Apple Vision Pro that unifies this ecosystem into a single immersive environment. PathVis replaces indirect mouse navigation with embodied interaction, utilizing eye gaze, natural hand gestures, and voice commands to explore gigapixel data. 312eedb6c7933dad8ab8531d6927fae13eff81d7.title: CLEAR-MPI: Concentration Level Enhancement and Recovery in Magnetic Particle Imaging Reconstruction
312eedb6c7933dad8ab8531d6927fae13eff81d7.abstract: High-quality imaging in low-concentration scenarios is a key issue for promoting the future clinical application of MPI. To address this, the Low Concentration Reconstruction Challenge in Magnetic Particle Imaging (LCR-MPI) has been organized in association with ISBI in 2026. In this paper, we present Concentration Level Enhancement And Recovery in MPI reconstruction (CLEAR-MPI), integrating advantages of the sinogram-domain denosing and image-domain denosing. The dual-domain module uses the Swin Image Restoration (SwinIR) to extract features from sinogram domain and image domain. The sinogram-domain enhancement improves the stability of the conversion process, while image-domain refinement corrects residual artifacts and restores structural details. 30303779988eea5e08ab371d718d838f7e85d8fa.title: Explaining Digital Pathology Models Via Clustering Activations
30303779988eea5e08ab371d718d838f7e85d8fa.abstract: We present a clustering-based explainability technique for digital pathology models based on convolutional neural networks. Unlike commonly used methods based on saliency maps, such as occlusion, GradCAM, or relevance propagation, which highlight regions that contribute the most to the prediction for a single slide, our method shows the global behaviour of the model under consideration, while also providing more fine-grained information. The result clusters can be visualised not only to understand the model, but also to increase confidence in its operation, leading to faster adoption in clinical practice. We also evaluate the performance of our technique on an existing model for detecting prostate cancer, demonstrating its usefulness.

2eaccd5bc0a4c1ec7c119262fbefe05e58308484.title: ARMARecon: An ARMA Convolutional Filter Based Graph Neural Network for Neurodegenerative Dementias Classification
2eaccd5bc0a4c1ec7c119262fbefe05e58308484.abstract: Early detection of neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's Disease (AD) and Frontotemporal Dementia (FTD) is essential for reducing the risk of progression to severe disease stages. As AD and FTD propagate along white-matter regions in a global, graph-dependent manner, graph-based neural networks are well suited to capture these patterns. Hence, we introduce ARMARecon, a unified graph learning framework that integrates Autoregressive Moving Average (ARMA) graph filtering with a reconstruction-driven objective to enhance feature representation and improve classification accuracy. ARMARecon effectively models both local and global connectivity by leveraging 20-bin Fractional Anisotropy (FA) histogram features extracted from white-matter regions, while mitigating over-smoothing. 2ea2607cead682a2bcce50a5c298be82ca63735e.title: Weakly Supervised Counterfactual Spatio-Temporal Multiple Instance Learning for Inflammation Detection in Endoscopic Inflammatory Bowel Disease Assessment
2ea2607cead682a2bcce50a5c298be82ca63735e.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) significantly impacts patients' quality of life, and accurate endoscopic assessment is critical for effective management. Conventional deep learning methods require frame-level annotations, which are labor-intensive and impractical for large video datasets. We propose a weakly supervised counterfactual spatio-temporal attention multiple instance learning (CFSpatioMIL) framework that captures spatial and temporal dependencies using only video-level labels. To enhance robustness and interpretability, we introduce a top-$k$ instance loss to encourage attention on multiple discriminative frames, and a counterfactual consistency mechanism that enforces stable predictions when highly attended frames are removed or replaced. 2e672d0671e67e8300b0b63ad376309e703bcc5a.title: Deep Learning Analysis of Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocyte, High Endothelial Venule, and Tertiary Lymphoid Structures in Breast Cancer Histopathology Whole Slide Imaging
2e672d0671e67e8300b0b63ad376309e703bcc5a.abstract: Understanding the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) is crucial for predicting prognosis and guiding immunotherapy in breast cancer. In this work, we present a deep learning pipeline to jointly analyze tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs), high endothelial venules (HEVs), and tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) from whole slide images (WSIs). Our method integrates multi-modal histopathology data with advanced segmentation and classification models. Specifically, we use HoverNet to segment tumor and immune cells, followed by ResNet-50-based classification to identify immune cell types and generate spatial heatmaps via Gaussian smoothing. For HEV detection, we apply nnU-Netv2 with color normalization using ICC profiles and morphological post-processing to improve accuracy. The resulting masks enable quantitative assessment of immune infiltration patterns and vascular architecture. This

2ca68d5e84579ec415e3f2c1a04a232c4ef3d157.title: Fast, Unsupervised Framework for Registration Quality Assessment of Multi-Stain Histological Whole Slide Pairs
2ca68d5e84579ec415e3f2c1a04a232c4ef3d157.abstract: High-fidelity registration of histopathological whole slide images (WSIs), such as hematoxylin & eosin (H&E) and immunohistochemistry (IHC), is vital for integrated molecular analysis but challenging to evaluate without ground-truth (GT) annotations. Existing WSI-level assessments-using annotated landmarks or intensity-based similarity metrics-are often time-consuming, unreliable, and computationally intensive, limiting large-scale applicability. This study proposes a fast, unsupervised framework that jointly employs down-sampled tissue masks- and deformations-based metrics for registration quality assessment (RQA) of registered H&E and IHC WSI pairs. The masks-based metrics measure global structural correspondence, while the deformations-based metrics evaluate local smoothness, continuity, and transformation realism. 2c7891bc7004f8ec31461310729f631b3d083e14.title: HYPERBOLIC MODEL AGGREGATION FOR FEDERATED LEARNING IN FMRI
2c7891bc7004f8ec31461310729f631b3d083e14.abstract: The privacy-sensitive nature of clinical data often limits the use of machine learning in medical imaging applications, particularly for modalities with high acquisition costs such as functional MRI (fMRI). Federated learning mitigates data-sharing barriers by training site-specific models locally and aggregating weights centrally into a server model. However, small and heterogeneous per-site samples in medical imaging heighten the need for robust model-aggregation strategies. In this work, we introduce a federated aggregation scheme based on hyperbolic geometry to provide a robust and flexible approach to federated model weight integration. The proposed scheme is plug-and-play for standard federated learning loops. 2c225c5278f4d90d1f835016b47d9ccd68a3dd1a.title: Structured Regularization Using Approximate Morphology for Alzheimer's Disease Classification
2c225c5278f4d90d1f835016b47d9ccd68a3dd1a.abstract: Structured regularization allows machine learning models to consider spatial relationships among parameters, leading to results that generalize better and are more interpretable compared to norm penalties. In this study, we evaluated a novel structured regularization method that incorporates approximate morphology operators defined using harmonic mean-based fW-filters. We extended this method to multiclass classification and conducted experiments aimed at classifying magnetic resonance images (MRI) of subjects into four stages of Alzheimer's disease progression. The experimental results demonstrate that the novel structured regularization method not only performs better than standard sparse and structured regularization methods in terms of prediction accuracy (ACC), F1 scores, and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), but also produces interpretable coefficien

2c15e70fee0d3292c379711dd67f0fd1a7afe2b5.title: Atlas Construction and Validation Using Cone-Beam Computed Tomography Images of Healthy Adult Human Hands
2c15e70fee0d3292c379711dd67f0fd1a7afe2b5.abstract: Anatomical atlases provide standardized spatial references for comparing complex structures. This study develops a high-resolution anatomical atlas of healthy hand bones using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT), which provides enhanced spatial resolution and lower radiation dose compared to conventional CT. The atlas, constructed from CBCT bilateral scans of 18 healthy adult subjects (35 total hands), serves as a standardized spatial reference for bones in the carpal, metacarpal, and proximal phalangeal regions, where variations in individual scans can complicate analysis. An iterative registration and averaging process, coupled with image preprocessing, enabled the construction of the atlas. 2beb1a2a0b9ec667f2aadb2e1917b79e9ea7262d.title: Shortcut Learning in Glomerular AI: Adversarial Penalties Hurt, Entropy Helps
2beb1a2a0b9ec667f2aadb2e1917b79e9ea7262d.abstract: Stain variability is a pervasive source of distribution shift and potential shortcut learning in renal pathology AI. We ask whether lupus nephritis glomerular lesion classifiers exploit stain as a shortcut, and how to mitigate such bias without stain or site labels. We curate a multi-center, multi-stain dataset of 9,674 glomerular patches ($224 \times 224$) from 365 WSIs across three centers and four stains (PAS, H&E, Jones, Trichrome), labeled as proliferative vs. non-proliferative. We evaluate Bayesian CNN and ViT backbones with Monte Carlo dropout in three settings: (1) stain-only classification; (2) a dual-head model jointly predicting lesion and stain with supervised stain loss; and (3) a dual-head model with label-free stain regularization via entropy maximization on the stain head. 2ba0f54b486294e878f2b2d55468131edf429484.title: Expert Model Guided Visual Programming for Radiology Report Generation
2ba0f54b486294e878f2b2d55468131edf429484.abstract: Automated radiology report generation requires complex compositional reasoning to translate subtle visual findings into coherent diagnostic narratives. Current models often fail to capture fine-grained pathological details, leading to generic or factually inconsistent reports. To address these limitations, we propose an expert model guided visual programming framework. It decomposes radiological reasoning into specialized subtasks. Each subtask is executed by a domain-specific expert model. We use a two-stage progressive fine-tuning strategy to fine-tune the model. This architecture enables the vision-language model to leverage the precision of specialized medical vision tools while preserving strong language generation capabilities. 2b581d3bf746f72a10b0598d276a4e841d063989.title: YOLO-US: A Unified Multi-Task Foundation Framework for Generalist Ultrasound Image Analysis
2b581d3bf746f72a10b0598d276a4e841d063989.abstract: The inherent heterogeneity of Ultrasound (US) imaging impedes the development of generalizable medical models, whereas the clinical translation of Generalist Medical AI demands unified foundation models rather than task or organ-specific approaches. This study proposes YOLOUS, the official baseline for the FMC_UIA 2026 challenge, which enhances the YOLOv11 architecture with a custom C3_MViTBv3 backbone and lightweight MBTransformer blocks, achieving a balance between local texture extraction, global long-range dependency modeling, and computational efficiency. Shared multi-scale representations are dynamically routed to four decoupled, task-specific heads, which are optimized for segmentation, classification, detection, and biometric regression. 2aeed5e6e22cc4b03b4327c3b350f293a38206ab.title: MPIDS: Multi-Group Perturbation Based Individualized Differential Structural Brain Network
2aeed5e6e22cc4b03b4327c3b350f293a38206ab.abstract: MRI-based brain structural network plays a key role in understanding the organization architecture of the human brain. However, current structural brain networks are inferred only at the group-level, missing individual heterogeneity at the single subject level. In this study, we propose a multi-group perturbation based individualized differential structural brain network (MPIDS), which reveals subject-specific deviations from a reference group in structural correlations among brain regions, enabling precision capture of individual differences. Each group is sequentially used as the reference network, with perturbations introduced by incorporating subjects from other groups. 2acbd2753d43dd0c0310532afb229b36e38c82bf.title: Resection Margin Prediction in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma: A Multi-Modal Machine Learning Approach Integrating Clinical and Computed Tomography Radiomics Data
2acbd2753d43dd0c0310532afb229b36e38c82bf.abstract: We introduce an integrative machine learning model designed to improve the prediction of surgical margin status in patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Given the limitations of current predictive methods, we leverage both clinical and radiomics features across a retrospective dataset of 139 patients with available pre- and post-treatment CT imaging data. Our approach incorporates delta radiomics to quantify temporal changes in tumor morphology, providing a more dynamic perspective on disease progression. Our optimized model demonstrated superior classification performance compared to models based on single-feature groups alone. Additionally, we evaluated data availability across distinct time points to identify the most informative features for predicting surgical margin outcomes. 296f0148051b944ab23018eb4d687a8ec2a3d2e7.title: Data-Efficient Medical Segmentation Through Active Knowledge Distillation from a Sam Teacher
296f0148051b944ab23018eb4d687a8ec2a3d2e7.abstract: Large-scale foundation models such as SAM possess extensive visual knowledge, but their application to segmentation is hindered by their computational cost. Conversely, smaller, locally-hosted models like U-Net++ are efficient but require large labeled datasets. We propose an “active” domain knowledge distillation framework where a lightweight model, trained on limited labeled data, generates visual prompts (points and boxes) for a frozen general-purpose SAM “teacher”. In turn, SAM provides high-quality pseudo-labels from unlabeled data, which are then used to re-train the small model. Our method, using only 75% of labeled data, outperforms a fully-supervised U-Net++ trained on 100% of the data on two datasets. 2781ae2046d44039cba4560b94d7f332b37105b4.title: LAPVT: Local Attention-Guided Pyramid Vision Transformers for Retinal Disease Classification
2781ae2046d44039cba4560b94d7f332b37105b4.abstract: Preventable blindness remains a major global concern, intensified by the shortage of ophthalmologists, underscoring the need for automated diagnostic systems. This paper presents the Local Attention-Guided Pyramid Vision Transformer (LAPVT) framework for retinal disease classification from color fundus images. LAPVT integrates three key modules: the Pyramid Vision Transformer (PVT) encoder, the Local Attention Module (LAM), and the Global-Local Fusion Module (GLFM). The PVT encoder captures multi-scale and long-range dependencies, effectively representing both fine details and global context. The LAM refines low-level features to highlight subtle, disease-specific local patterns. The GLFM then fuses global contextual and locally attended features to emphasize critical pathological regions. 262c6ff61df2b7a46e83ca82e343f961630e4370.title: A Multimodal Cross-Attention Pathotranscriptome Integration for Enhanced Survival Prediction of Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma
262c6ff61df2b7a46e83ca82e343f961630e4370.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) accounts for a major part of cancer mortality, with survival outcomes highly dependent on early diagnosis. While many approaches have been proposed for OSCC survival prediction, they often rely on unimodal data, which may be suboptimal. In this study, we introduced a unified cross-attention-based deep learning framework that integrates whole-slide histopathology images (WSIs) and transcriptomic data from OSCC patients for survival prediction. The framework employed an autoencoder for transcriptomic feature extraction and a state-of-the-art pathology foundation model-evaluated across five alternatives-to derive WSI embeddings. These embeddings were subsequently integrated using cross-attention and concatenation within a Cox proportional hazards model. 25a545900ecada52679580fe1941fb2aae3fad8f.title: Sam-Peft: a Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning Framework Fusing Multi-Modal Mri for Prompt-Free Glioma Segmentation
25a545900ecada52679580fe1941fb2aae3fad8f.abstract: Accurate glioma delineation on multi-modal MRI is pivotal for clinical planning, yet remains difficult in practice: cross-site fusion of T1, T1Gd, T2, and FLAIR is brittle, routine pipelines lack manual point/box prompts, and fully fine-tuning large backbones is compute-intensive. In this paper, we present SAM-PEFT, a promptfree, parameter-efficient adaptation of the Segment Anything Model (SAM) for multi-modal MRI glioma segmentation. SAM-PEFT freezes the SAM backbone and adds: (i) a Multi-Modal Feature Adaptive Fusion (MFAM) for T1, T1Gd, T2, and FLAIR integration; (ii) a Lightweight Prompt Encoder (LPE) with efficient anatomical positional encoding to generate dense internal prompts; and (iii) TransMedAttention for fine-grained refinement. 25366d4b7e78073982a3d1abc15aebaa4128bdf2.title: Lasagna-U-Net: Revisiting U-Shape Architecture for Histopathology Image Segmentation
25366d4b7e78073982a3d1abc15aebaa4128bdf2.abstract: Histopathology images serve as the gold standard for clinical diagnosis, making their accurate analysis essential in medical practice. Although U-Net and its variants have been widely applied to histopathology image segmentation, most fail to effectively address the challenge of multi-scale lesion representation. In this paper, we propose Lasagna-U-Net, a novel U-Net variant that integrates convolutional neural network (CNN) and vision Transformer (ViT) within a unified U-shaped architecture. Two key modules-the multi-scale grouped convolution module and the grouped residual Transformer module-jointly enhance the model's capacity for local feature extraction and long-range dependency modeling. 2534dc8da8986921ce0daf4d7365387b66acaae1.title: Efficient 3D Attention for 3T to 7T Modality Conversion
2534dc8da8986921ce0daf4d7365387b66acaae1.abstract: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is a widely used, non-invasive diagnostic technique in modern medicine. 7T MRI scans offer enhanced tissue contrast, finer anatomical detail, a lower signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and a higher contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) compared to 3T scans, facilitating more accurate diagnoses. The availability of 7T scanners is mostly restricted to advanced medical centers, primarily research facilities, in developed countries, whereas 3T scanners are more widely accessible worldwide. While near-perfect pixel-level accuracy is essential for clinical applications, approximation-based methods can serve as practical alternatives when 7T scans are unavailable due to logistical or financial limitations. 2533a355160253fc9f4978582a97ad56eaeeaf39.title: Prompt-Guided Radiology Report Generation Utilizing SAM
2533a355160253fc9f4978582a97ad56eaeeaf39.abstract: Report generation models can effectively reduce the workload of radiologists by automatically analyzing images and generating reports. However, most reports generated by current model frameworks have many problems such as lack of completeness and misunderstanding, which affect radiologists’ willingness to adopt them. We develop a report generation model consisting of a target detection module, a feature extraction module, and a text generation module, which are used to detect lesions in images and generate lesion prompt boxes, fuse prompt features, and generate reports, respectively. 2527b2af2b97c1b9744cdef2a46197229447a0b7.title: Resource-Efficient Automatic Refinement of Segmentations via Weak Supervision from Light Feedback
2527b2af2b97c1b9744cdef2a46197229447a0b7.abstract: Delineating anatomical regions is a key task in medical image analysis. Manual segmentation achieves high accuracy but is labor-intensive and prone to variability, thus prompting the development of automated approaches. Recently, a breadth of foundation models has enabled automated segmentations across diverse anatomies and imaging modalities, but these may not always meet the clinical accuracy standards. While segmentation refinement strategies can improve performance, current methods depend on heavy user interactions or require fully supervised segmentations for training. Here, we present SCORE (Segmentation COrrection from Regional Evaluations), a weakly supervised framework that learns to refine mask predictions only using light feedback during training. 226aaa7566821900a2505982880a1353a997e3bc.title: TAPE: A Two-Stage Parameter-Efficient Adaptation Framework for Foundation Models in OCT-OCTa Analysis
226aaa7566821900a2505982880a1353a997e3bc.abstract: Automated analysis of optical coherence tomography (OCT) and OCT angiography (OCTA) images is critical for robust ophthalmic diagnosis. Existing mainstream methods trained from scratch rely heavily on massive data and model scale, thereby hindering their practical deployment in resourceconstrained clinical settings. Although transfer learning based on foundation models (FMs) is promising, it still faces significant challenges: domain shift and task misalignment. To address these, we propose TAPE: A Two-stage Adaptation Framework via Parameter-E fficient Fine-tuning, which strategically decouples adaptation into domain alignment and task fitting for downstream segmentation. 21c82cba1cfdf8c86733ce7125fb51b56632583d.title: Training Strategies for Increased Temporal Resolution in Clinical Cardiac-gated SPECT Studies with Deep Learning Denoising
21c82cba1cfdf8c86733ce7125fb51b56632583d.abstract: Cardiac-gated SPECT studies are limited to the use of a small number of gated frames due to high imaging noise in clinical acquisitions. Here we investigate three strategies for training a deep learning (DL) network for suppressing the elevated imaging noise when the number of gate frames is doubled from conventional clinical studies. These training strategies are aimed at addressing the challenge of a lack of ground truth images in clinical acquisitions for use as the learning target by a DL network. In the experiments we investigated these strategies with a set of 237 clinical acquisitions. The results indicate that the trained DL network can effectively suppress both the spatial and temporal variability in the reconstructed myocardium in the gated frames. 2100a10c63255f39c581d4faf3bb1ecdb7271966.title: Integrating Multi-Modal Fundus Photography for Precision Diagnosis in Ophthalmology
2100a10c63255f39c581d4faf3bb1ecdb7271966.abstract: In recent years, multi-modal fundus imaging has become crucial for comprehensive retinal assessment, since different imaging modalities provide complementary information about retinal structures and lesions. As two different imaging tools for diabetic retinopathy (DR) grading, color fundus photography (CFP) and infrared fundus photography (IFP) are highly-correlated and complementary in clinical applications. CFP offers rich color information, where as IFP captures pathological changes from deeper retinal layers. This complementarity is especially valuable in eyes with media opacities, such as cataract or vitreous haze, where CFP quality often degrades. 205510c50e62e5a8051ac6b0c828164ea6f24377.title: Dilation-Assisted Contrastive Learning for Corneal Nerve Segmentation in Corneal Confocal Microscopy
205510c50e62e5a8051ac6b0c828164ea6f24377.abstract: Accurate extraction of corneal nerves in corneal confocal microscopy images is essential for assessing morphological changes linked to various eye-related diseases. However, current segmentation methods struggle with distinguishing corneal nerves from visually similar structures. In this paper, we propose a dilation-assisted contrastive learning (Dicon) model. The proposed Dicon incorporates a dilation-guided positive pairing mechanism that leverages structural priors from ground truth to guide the model toward more precise extraction of corneal nerves. Additionally, we propose a selective feature amplification regularization strategy, which uses dilation masks to differentiate between foreground and background, thereby enhancing the model's ability to distinguish between visually similar structures while reinforcing the learning of corneal nerve features. 2019dc94992052249aa0ee92fc4af061c7dab4e9.title: OHIF -SAM2: Accelerating Radiology Workflows with Meta Segment Anything Model 2
2019dc94992052249aa0ee92fc4af061c7dab4e9.abstract: The release of Segment Anything Models (SAM1 and SAM2) by Meta has significantly impacted various domains, including medical imaging. However, existing applications of SAM for medical images primarily rely on standalone tools that require local installation and configuration, limiting accessibility and ease of use. In this work, we present a web-based extension of SAM2 integrated into the Open Health Imaging Foundation (OHIF) viewer. Our tool supports all SAM2 prompt types, including points and bounding boxes, and additionally enables text-based prompting through integration with the Grounding DINO. This web-based integration eliminates installation requirements, providing a more user-friendly interface. The implementation is open-source and available at https://github.com/CCI-Bonn/OHIF-SAM2.

1f567944f7b1e5ad6778d5492433ce1fd26072f8.abstract: In interventional radiology, Cone-Beam Computed Tomography (CBCT) is a helpful imaging modality that provides guidance to practicians during minimally invasive procedures. CBCT differs from traditional Computed Tomography (CT) due to its limited reconstructed field of view, specific artefacts, and the intra-arterial administration of contrast medium. While CT benefits from abundant publicly available annotated datasets, interventional CBCT data remain scarce and largely unannotated, with existing datasets focused primarily on radiotherapy applications. To address this limitation, we leverage a proprietary collection of unannotated interventional CBCT scans in conjunction with annotated CT data, employing domain adaptation techniques to bridge the modality gap and enhance liver segmentation performance on CBCT. 1f548d847bbe873da86030c8bd2f9bddb517c211.title: A View-Specific Dual-Task Framework for Fetal Heart Ultrasound Analysis
1f548d847bbe873da86030c8bd2f9bddb517c211.abstract: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is the leading cause of fetal morbidity and mortality worldwide. The accuracy of prenatal ultrasound screening heavily depends on expert interpretation of standard views, including the four-chamber (4 CH), left and right ventricular outflow tracts (LVOT/RVOT), and threevessel trachea (3VT) views. However, clinical practice faces critical challenges including a shortage of domain experts, insufficient multi-view annotated data, and difficulty in identifying subtle anatomical features. To address the limitations of the official baseline (lightweight UNet)-namely insufficient model capacity, multi-task feature conflicts, inadequate handling of class imbalance, and underutilization of multiscale information-this study proposes a deep learning optimization framework built upon a large-scale multi-view fetal ultrasound dataset. 1f25183cce3c6684dc4edcb7044d762310ad188e.abstract: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPMs) have recently gained prominence in the research community for generating synthetic samples of rare disease types to mitigate class imbalance in medical datasets. While DDPMs can produce visually convincing medical images, they often fail to preserve accurate anatomical structure and clinical fidelity, resulting in limited biological accuracy. To overcome these limitations, there are fine-tuning frameworks that integrate medical experts' evaluations of generated images into the DDPM training process using human-in-theloop reinforcement learning techniques; specifically, Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and Reinforcement Learning with Human Feedback (RLHF). Even though, RLHF is widely adopted, there is substantial computational overhead and classical DPO does not explicitly account for structural and perceptual aspects of the images. To

1daf4571b849781e2cb84839209fb32900fae3b5.title: A Physics-Informed and Mechanistically-Grounded Deep Learning Framework for Revealing Altered Structurefunction Coupling in Neurodegenerative Diseases
1daf4571b849781e2cb84839209fb32900fae3b5.abstract: Modern neuroimaging enables the study of structural connectivity (SC) and functional connectivity (FC) in vivo, yet how alterations in SC-FC coupling relate to neurodegenerative progression remains elusive. Here, we introduce KM-Net, a brain-inspired deep network that models grounded in Kuramoto oscillatory dynamics, which simulates how oscillatory synchrony emerges from the anatomical connectome. The model learns the dynamic coupling between SC and FC, providing an interpretable, biophysically grounded representation of whole-brain dynamics. Through large-scale evaluation across three independent neuroimaging cohorts (ADNI, PPMI, NIFD; participants >1300), KM-Net achieves state-of-the-art diagnostic performance, outperforming leading graph neural networks. 1dae2885c2d6a84d27f9caa73a6bae6a52d229c3.title: Intelligent Diagnosis of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease by Integrating CT Segmentation and Multi-Dimensional Representations
1dae2885c2d6a84d27f9caa73a6bae6a52d229c3.abstract: CT scans of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) show spatial heterogeneity, making precise characterization difficult with traditional methods. This study proposes a deep learning model with a “segmentation first, then diagnosis” cascade framework for intelligent COPD risk stratification. In the segmentation stage, an Attention-Spectral Dual-Module (ASDM) is introduced to integrate frequency and spatial domain features, combined with a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to optimize skip connections and enhance key feature extraction. A region-adaptive composite loss function is designed to improve lung parenchyma segmentation accuracy. In the diagnosis stage, a cross-dimensional feature fusion architecture is used, with 2D CNNs extracting local texture features and 3D CNNs capturing short-range spatiotemporal context. 1ce6e107724be7a2af87e89b158e9c43574013bd.title: DAPS: Diffusion-Based and Anatomical Prior-Guided CT Synthesis for Pet Attenuation Correction
1ce6e107724be7a2af87e89b158e9c43574013bd.abstract: Positron emission tomography (PET) is a functional imaging modality that is inherently susceptible to gamma-photon attenuation, necessitating correction for precise quantitative imaging. While computed tomography (CT)-based attenuation correction (AC) remains the gold standard, its reliance on CT elevates radiation exposure and creates a need for reliable AC methods in CT-free systems. In this study, we propose a CT-targeted Diffusion-based and Anatomical Priorguided Synthesis (DAPS) framework, which integrates three core components: 1) a deformable registration module for aligning a brain template with subject-specific PET images to generate anatomical prior; 2) a diffusion model that generates synthetic CT (sCT) images from non-AC PET images integrated with the prior; 3) a PET AC module that employs the sCT images to improve the AC performance. 1c531c733b65b5fbf4847c73af6acd5df4c80594.title: Self-Supervised Metric Learning for Gaussian Anomaly Detection in Fundus Images
1c531c733b65b5fbf4847c73af6acd5df4c80594.abstract: Anomaly detection in fundus images receives increasing interest in automated occular diseases screening. Instead of detecting a fixed range of diseases, based on provided labels during training, the global health status of a patient's retina is infered by focusing only on healthy fundus images, considered as samples from a normal class. Though promising, these methods need to be significantly improved before reaching clinical applications. On the one hand, multi-disease datasets providing fully healthy fundus images are rather small in size, due to the complexity of the labeling process. On the other hand, single-disease or few -disease datasets are large, but the scope of their normal class is limited as fundus images labeled as normal in these datasets might contain signs of other pathologies that were not taken into account during their constitution. 1b24a569b9bd05703a55ae15d221e3bcfe267ea7.title: A Geometric Multimodal Foundation Model Integrating BP-MRI and Clinical Reports in Prostate Cancer Classification
1b24a569b9bd05703a55ae15d221e3bcfe267ea7.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is one of the most common cancers in men worldwide. Bi-parametric MRI (bp-MRI) and clinical variables are crucial for PCa identification and improving treatment decisions. However, this process is subjective to expert interpretations. Furthermore, most existing computer-aided diagnosis methods focus on imaging-based models, overlooking the clinical context and suffering from data scarcity, limiting their ability to learn robust representations. We propose a geometric multimodal Foundation Model (FM), named MFM-Geom, that learns representations from bp-MRI and clinical reports, encoding visual findings and information from the context of clinical variables. In the representations classification head, the approach leverages symmetric positive definite (SPD) matrices and Riemannian deep learning to integrate imaging-text representations from a biomedical multimodal FM.

1a56c1b987d36dc17555fa8fd5db050a333eb8dc.title: Automatic Vertebrae Segmentation From Intraoperative 3D Point Clouds for Scoliosis Spine Surgery
1a56c1b987d36dc17555fa8fd5db050a333eb8dc.abstract: Accurate, real-time assessment of spinal alignment is essential in Posterior Spinal Fusion Surgery (PSFS) for scoliosis correction. Image-guided surgery systems rely on the registration of a preoperative spine model to intraoperative images. In this work, we tackle the segmentation of vertebrae from textured 3D point clouds acquired during the surgery without any radiation. We trained a Point Transformer v3 for vertebra segmentation, demonstrating a 14.2 % improvement over prior U-Net-based architectures on the cadaveric SpineDepth benchmark. To overcome the critical scarcity of real intraoperative data, we establish a semi-synthetic training paradigm incorporating the SpineDepth data with an augmented dataset derived from 49 real scoliosis cases, featuring synthesized surgical texture. On top of that, we demonstrate the clinical feasibility of this approach through a pilot evaluation on

1a30cb709dacb35fde59e1a5523da0f0c08d4a01.title: CT CONTRAST PHASE IDENTIFICATION BY PREDICTING THE TEMPORAL ANGLE USING CIRCULAR REGRESSION
1a30cb709dacb35fde59e1a5523da0f0c08d4a01.abstract: Contrast enhancement is widely used in computed tomogra-phy (CT) scans, where radiocontrast agents circulate through the bloodstream and accumulate in the vasculature, creating visual contrast between blood vessels and surrounding tissues. This work introduces a technique to predict the timing of contrast in a CT scan, a key factor influencing the contrast effect, using circular regression models. Specifically, we represent the contrast timing as unit vectors on a circle and employ 2D convolutional neural networks to predict it based on predefined anchor time points. Unlike previous methods that treat contrast timing as discrete phases, our approach is the first method that views it as a continuous variable, of-fering a more fine-grained understanding of contrast differences, particularly in relation to patient-specific vascular effects. We train the model on 877 CT scans and test it on

19ceae34f1aad0cb4e9209a26d94c225b80570a3.title: Cross-Modal Brain Mri Synthesis Via Contrastive Disentanglement and Conditional Diffusion
19ceae34f1aad0cb4e9209a26d94c225b80570a3.abstract: Cross-modal brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) synthesis remains challenging due to the complex interplay between anatomical structures and modality-specific contrast patterns. We propose a two-phase framework that separates anatomical and contrast representations through contrastive learning and conditional diffusion. Phase 1 uses contrastive disentanglement with dual projection heads to separate anatomy (patient-specific structure) from contrast (modality-specific appearance), reinforced by adversarial training. A learnable contrast bank stores modality prototypes independent of anatomical content. Phase 2 employs a conditional diffusion model that synthesizes target images by combining source anatomy features with target contrast codes from the bank. Training integrates anatomy-invariant and contrast-invariant contrastive losses and adversarial modality classification to enforce c

198d41c866849595fa149875eb0d73cb62f9a590.title: Predicting Longitudinal Brain Change from Baseline 3D MRI and Detecting Abnormal Atrophy Using Deep Learning
198d41c866849595fa149875eb0d73cb62f9a590.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is highly heterogeneous, with characteristic regional changes in patterns of cortical volume. This study aims to predict future longitudinal brain volume changes in older individuals with various stages of clinical diagnoses, from healthy to dementia, using predictions from baseline MRI. We test two deep learning (DL) approaches predicting longitudinal atrophy: (i) a unimodal model using baseline MRI scans from a single time point as predictor and log-Jacobian atrophy map as target, and (ii) a multimodal model including imaging and non-imaging data. We then developed a normative model using mixed linear regression, based on the longitudinal brain changes predicted by the DL model, to detect deviations in the clinical patient population. This preliminary result using the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) dataset demonstrated the efficacy of the pr

1960eaf36efa547f9805808c8bb0e4f6554fa13f.title: Microstructure Informed Mamba Vision Masked Autoencoder for Personalized Brain Injury Detection from Diffusion MRI
1960eaf36efa547f9805808c8bb0e4f6554fa13f.abstract: Personalized brain injury detection is crucial for clinical diagnosis, yet current methods often overlook subtle injuries and diverse disease diagnoses. This study introduces MEMAE, a new approach that improves global context modeling during 3D dMRI reconstruction while maintaining local details. By leveraging reconstruction errors from healthy dMRI data, MEMAE enables personalized detection of brain injury. It employs three advanced diffusion models to generate a multidimensional microstructural measure, enabling analysis of heterogeneous brain injuries across various health conditions. Experimental results show that MEMAE can establish a robust prior knowledge base with minimal healthy control data, distinguishing between tumor infiltration and cocaine-induced axonal degeneration. This approach shifts the focus from group to individualized analysis, offering a promising solution for ea

1846fd352340616f98ea9d102f3617517b9489f1.title: Annotation-Free Cerebrovascular Segmentation: A Synthetic Data Paradigm for TOF-MRA Segmentation
1846fd352340616f98ea9d102f3617517b9489f1.abstract: Time-of-flight magnetic resonance angiography (TOF-MRA), as a non-ionizing and non-invasive cerebrovascular imaging technique, holds significant clinical diagnostic value. Precise cerebrovascular segmentation and quantitative morphological characterization are crucial for the prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of cerebral diseases. However, manual annotation of the human brain's intricate vascular network is prohibitively time-consuming and costly. Unsupervised learning offers a promising solution by enabling TOF-MRA cerebrovascular segmentation without labeled data, substantially reducing clinicians' workload. In this study, we propose an unsupervised cerebrovascular segmentation framework that first synthesizes 3D tree-like vascular structures using a spatial colonization algorithm. These synthetic structures are then integrated into vascular-suppressed TOF-MRA backgrounds through Fo

17e4d39d64e67bff5ec8e69d8bd7a525bca24e4e.title: Towards Classifying Histopathological Microscope Images as Time Series Data
17e4d39d64e67bff5ec8e69d8bd7a525bca24e4e.abstract: As the frontline data for cancer diagnosis, microscopic pathology images are fundamental for providing patients with rapid and accurate treatment. However, despite their practical value, the deep learning community has largely overlooked their usage. This paper proposes a novel approach to classifying microscopy images as time series data, addressing the unique challenges posed by their manual acquisition and weakly labeled nature. The proposed method fits image sequences of varying lengths to a fixed-length target by leveraging Dynamic Time-series Warping (DTW). Attention-based pooling is employed to predict the class of the case simultaneously. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach by comparing performance with various baselines and showcasing the benefits of using various inference strategies in achieving stable and reliable results. 17cec1ed929a7d9b10e0466901ac93659ff846ec.title: Distilling Expert Surgical Knowledge: How to Train Local Surgical VLMs for Anatomy Explanation in Complete Mesocolic Excision
17cec1ed929a7d9b10e0466901ac93659ff846ec.abstract: Recently, Vision Large Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated high potential in computer-aided diagnosis and decision-support. However, current VLMs show deficits in domain specific surgical scene understanding, such as identifying and explaining anatomical landmarks during Complete Mesocolic Excision. Additionally, there is a need for locally deployable models to avoid patient data leakage to large VLMs, hosted outside the clinic. We propose a privacy-preserving framework to distill knowledge from large, general-purpose LLMs into an efficient, local VLM. We generate an expert-supervised dataset by prompting a teacher LLM without sensitive images, using only textual context and binary segmentation masks for spatial information. This dataset is used for Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and subsequent Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) of the locally deployable VLM. Our evaluation confirms

170073b136df62ad72619c78ada94d548d438e89.title: RIEMAE: Riemannian Masked Autoencoder for Classifying Malignant Prostate Cancer Patterns
170073b136df62ad72619c78ada94d548d438e89.abstract: Prostate cancer (PCa) is the most frequently diagnosed cancer in men and biparametric magnetic resonance imaging (BP-MRI) has emerged as a non-invasive alternative to characterize clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) lesions. However, the assessment of BP-MRI is expert-dependent and challenging due to the remarked variability in malignant and healthy observations. Current computational approaches rely on supervised learning tasks that require large annotated datasets for effective training. This work proposes a novel Riemannian Masked Autoencoder (RieMAE) that captures key relationships in BP-MRI regions of interest, leveraging self-supervised learning on symmetric positive definite (SPD) covariance matrices. The proposed RieMAE considers the Riemannian geometric structure of SPD matrices while reconstructing the original pairwise relationships within radiological findings. The

16971f306f8dc4b1ed78592284eeebf677638f5f.title: Robust and Efficient 3D Gaussian Splatting for Diagnostic Imaging
16971f306f8dc4b1ed78592284eeebf677638f5f.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) [1] has emerged as a popular technique for neural rendering. Use of simple Gaussian primitives that enable real-time rendering, faster training, and high visual fidelity makes its use compelling over alternatives like NeRFs. However, despite its success in natural image settings, 3DGS encounters notable rendering challenges in medical imaging. Our analysis reveals that the error characteristics of sparse reconstruction pipelines (e.g., COLMAP), which serve input to the 3DGS pipeline, differ significantly between medical and natural environments. This discrepancy leads to degraded rendering performance when noise propagates from sparsely reconstructed inputs. 15e7b0df5976791c63b2f06fdc2b259fdf524ca2.title: SLD: Segmentation-Based Landmark Detection for Spinal Ligaments
15e7b0df5976791c63b2f06fdc2b259fdf524ca2.abstract: In biomechanical modeling, the representation of ligament attachments is crucial for a realistic simulation of the forces acting between the vertebrae. These forces are typically modeled as vectors connecting ligament landmarks on adjacent vertebrae, making precise identification of these landmarks a key requirement for constructing reliable spine models. Existing automated detection methods are either limited to specific spinal regions or lack sufficient accuracy. This work presents a novel approach for detecting spinal ligament landmarks, which first performs shape-based segmentation of 3D vertebrae and subsequently applies domain-specific rules to identify different types of attachment points. 15e15782ed206f60f0cd5ba90fa44423a48336a3.title: Geometric Deep Learning Model of Left Atrial Geometry and Conduction Velocity in Atrial Fibrillation
15e15782ed206f60f0cd5ba90fa44423a48336a3.abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained arrhythmia, yet the coupling between left atrial (LA) geometry and conduction velocity (CV) during AF remains poorly characterized. We present a novel geometric deep learning framework that jointly models LA surface anatomy and spatial CV maps. Our architecture augments a point cloud completion network with a $\beta$-VAE to learn a shared, interpretable latent representation, enabling end-to-end reconstruction of anatomy and CV and controlled latent traversals for structure-function hypothesis testing. We show that our method can reconstruct LA geometry with an average error of 2.09 mm and CV with an average error of $0.477 ~\text{ms}^{-1}$, and that the learned factors capture physiologically coherent relations. 131bd097af6a9112a401ab8c7061f0052c90bda9.title: Uncertainty-Aware Multimodal Fusion for Prognostic Prediction in Myelodysplastic Syndromes
131bd097af6a9112a401ab8c7061f0052c90bda9.abstract: Myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) are clonal hematopoietic disorders with a substantial risk of progression to acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Predicting this disease evolution remains challenging, as conventional prognostic systems—such as the IPSS and IPSS-R—primarily rely on clinical, cytogenetic, and molecular information, while generally not incorporating quantitative imaging-derived features. Computational image analysis methods can extract rich morphological information from hematological images, which has the potential to enhance prognostic modeling. However, only a limited number of studies have investigated integrating image-based representations with clinical data, and to our knowledge, none have systematically addressed uncertainty in such multimodal fusion. 131af0f551dcb4c1b4c59466a3239d97fd167d44.title: Test-Time Fluorescein Angiography-Free Non-Perfusion Area Segmentation from Fundus Image
131af0f551dcb4c1b4c59466a3239d97fd167d44.abstract: Retinal non-perfusion areas (NPAs) are of critical importance for the diagnosis of certain retinal pathologies, particularly diabetic retinopathy. Fundus fluorescein angiography (FFA) is widely recognized as the clinical gold standard for identifying NPAs. However, FFA is an invasive imaging method. In this paper, we propose a color fundus photography (CFP) NPA segmentation framework that is FFA-free during testing, based on prompts for different missing-modality scenarios. Specifically, we design distinct learnable modality-conditioned prompts (LMCPs) for different missing-modality scenarios, catering to both single-modality input scenarios and dual-modality scenarios, enabling the network to perceive and learn the representations between different modalities. 13105e51824b548e99597cfe7de39133466add99.title: Boostlet.Js: Medical Image Processing Plugins for the Web via Javascript Injection
13105e51824b548e99597cfe7de39133466add99.abstract: Can web-based image processing and visualization tools easily integrate into existing websites without significant time and effort? Our Boostlet.js library addresses this challenge by providing an open-source, JavaScript-based web framework to enable additional image processing functionalities. Boost-let examples include kernel filtering, image captioning, data visualization, segmentation, and web-optimized machine-learning models. To achieve this, Boostlet.js uses a browser bookmark to inject a user-friendly plugin selection tool called PowerBoost into any host website. Boostlet provides on-site access to a standard API independent of any visualization framework for pixel data and scene manipulation. 12e2687f1beb57269391858dab1a85e6f3c835c9.title: U-Star: AN Asymmetric U-Shaped Network Based on Element-Wise Multiplication to Segment Nuclei in H&E Stained Histological Images
12e2687f1beb57269391858dab1a85e6f3c835c9.abstract: Nuclei segmentation in Hematoxylin and Eosin (H&E) stained images plays a crucial role in cancer diagnosis and pathological evaluation, enabling pathologists to identify abnormal cells and assess their morphology and distribution. While current automated nuclei segmentation methods predominantly employ convolutional neural networks and attention mechanisms, the potential of element-wise multiplication has been largely unexplored. This paper introduces U-Star, a novel asymmetric segmentation network based on the star block that leverages element-wise multiplication. U-Star adopts the classic encoder-decoder architecture and innovatively implements star-connection as an alternative to traditional skip-connections. 128c287f770eeef305c1732372f95dfeb7449d33.title: A Pair-Weighing Strategy for Enhancing Clip Zero-Shot Classification for Chest X-Rays
128c287f770eeef305c1732372f95dfeb7449d33.abstract: Chest radiography (CXR) is essential for diagnosing life-threatening diseases, yet the growing demand exceeds the availability of expert radiologists. Although deep learning models have achieved expertlevel performance, they require large labelled datasets, which are costly to obtain in the medical domain. Recent advances in selfsupervised representation learning, particularly contrastive visionlanguage models such as CLIP, enable label-efficient pre-training for zero-shot classification. In this work, we propose an optimized CLIP pre-training pipeline for chest X-ray interpretation that reduces computational costs while improving efficiency. Our method pretrains CLIP on chest X-rays and corresponding clinical reports, introducing two key modifications: a weighted contrastive loss to mitigate false negatives and prevent suboptimal representations, and a parameter-efficient fine-tuning st

1177b6c3b693f187da36e081e6496ccd6e3d7f07.title: Magnetic Resonance Elastography: Predicting Brain Stiffness in Parkinson's Disease Patients From Multidimensional Diffusion Mri
1177b6c3b693f187da36e081e6496ccd6e3d7f07.abstract: This study explores an alternative to Magnetic Resonance Elastography (MRE) for estimating brain stiffness, a potential biomarker associated with Parkinson's disease (PD). A 3D U-Net deep learning model was trained to predict stiffness maps from diffusion MRI parameters derived from advanced diffusion models. Mean diffusivity emerged as the most informative input, achieving a SSIM of $\sim 0.755$, MSE of $\sim 0.171 \times 10^{-2}$, and PSNR of $\sim 22.9$. Regional analysis confirmed consistent performance across brain areas. The findings suggest that diffusion MRI has the potential to approximate MRE-derived brain stiffness, offering a more accessible and cost-effective approach for assessing neurodegenerative changes in PD.

113727098ee6b869114f6c573ac3ef05474ec3cd.title: Detecting and Refurbishing Ground Truth Errors During Training of Deep Learning-Based Echocardiography Segmentation Models
113727098ee6b869114f6c573ac3ef05474ec3cd.abstract: Deep learning-based medical image segmentation typically relies on ground truth (GT) labels obtained through manual annotation, but these can be prone to random errors or systematic biases. This study examines the robustness of deep learning models to such errors in echocardiography (echo) segmentation and evaluates a novel strategy for detecting and refurbishing erroneous labels during model training. Using the CAMUS dataset, we simulate three error types, then compare a loss-based GT label error detection method with one based on Variance of Gradients (VOG). We also propose a pseudo-labelling approach to refurbish suspected erroneous GT labels. We assess the performance of our proposed approach under varying error levels. 11178681e1a44823c7771f7b59af322021ae6876.title: Advancing OCT-Based Retinal Disease Classification with XLSTM: A Framework for Variable-Length Volume Processing
11178681e1a44823c7771f7b59af322021ae6876.abstract: This paper presents a method for retinal disease classification using optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans, specifically addressing the challenge of variable B-scan density across dataset volumes. Deep learning methods often struggle with fluctuations in the number of B-scans within OCT volumes, which can limit their effectiveness. To address this, we propose an extended long short-term memory (xLSTM) model capable of processing variable-length B-scan sequences, capturing spatial and contextual information across entire volumes regardless of slice count. Leveraging xLSTM's advanced memory structure, our method enhances classification accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency. 10ebc0e1e7f7d776d4faa9f827d45fc9902080f7.title: Cross-Modal Graph Attention Network for Parkinson's Disease Diagnosis
10ebc0e1e7f7d776d4faa9f827d45fc9902080f7.abstract: Accurate diagnosis of Parkinson's disease (PD) remains challenging due to heterogeneous symptoms and subtle neuroanatomical changes. Although multimodal Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) provides complementary information, existing methods often fail to effectively model cross-modal interactions and brain anatomical connectivity. We propose a cross-modal graph attention network with self-supervised contrastive pretraining for PD diagnosis. Contrastive learning extracts robust volumetric representations from limited data, while a bidirectional cross-modal attention module enables deep interaction between T1-weighted MRI and quantitative susceptibility mapping features. 10e349de9526ab9ba7ea160a6dcce425a95d9acd.title: Deep Learning Based Landmarks Detection for Positioning Assessment in Mammography
10e349de9526ab9ba7ea160a6dcce425a95d9acd.abstract: Proper breast positioning is critical for reliable mammographic screening, yet remains a major source of diagnostic variability and exam failure. This study proposes an interpretable, landmark-based framework for the automated evaluation of the Adequate amount of pectoral muscle criterion in mediolateral oblique mammograms. The method was trained and evaluated on 2274 annotated MLO images derived from a multicenter audit, with a test subset independently labeled by three expert radiographers to account for inter-rater variability. 109bb991e8cc19b20042902879c0dfeee6039b27.title: Spinesynnet: Synthesis of Thin-Slice Spinal MR Images by a View-Prompt Elastic Deformation Network with Anatomical Constraint
109bb991e8cc19b20042902879c0dfeee6039b27.abstract: Thin-slice spinal MR images are essential for precise segmentation but are clinically limited by long scan times and possible motion artifacts. Achieving the synthesis of thinslice spinal MR images from a given thick-slice MR scan is a promising solution to solve the aforementioned issues. However, due to the diversity of spinal structures and the lack of medical image data, this remains an unprecedented challenge. In this paper, we propose a novel approach named SpineSynNet for synthesizing thin-slice MR images from thick-slice scans by interpolating multiple intermediate slices of two adjacent thick slices. 1047353fe76f747f32c7d13908b06cee4149b274.title: DBS-ElecNet: Automated Localization and Segmentation of DBS Electrodes in Clinical MRI
1047353fe76f747f32c7d13908b06cee4149b274.abstract: This paper presents DBS-ElecNet, a deep learning framework for automated segmentation of electrodes and artifact regions in post-operative DBS MRI. To overcome reliance on manual annotations, we introduce a hybrid approach where a traditional image processing pipeline generates initial segmentations for the 3D U-Net model, which uses these as ground truth, and achieves robust segmentation performance. DBS-ElecNet performs inference in $\sim 3$ seconds, a 60-100x speedup over manual segmentations. 0fb80a61b1f7b41d8ae6dca42ac71e90b65645d2.title: Optimization-Based Motion Estimation in HR-PQCT

Due to its long scan time, this modality is especially susceptible towards motion of the patient. In this work, an iterative motion estimation and compensation approach is proposed that is able to significantly reduce the amount of motion artifacts.
